artigo.texto: CATL's 7.8% Rebound Meets a Harder Question: Where Is the Profit? Published on 10/25/2026 at 06:41 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL shares climbed 7.8% on Friday as Chinese battery, EV and technology names recovered broadly, with media reports pointing to renewed appetite for growth stocks following a sharp selloff. The move came without a fresh company-specific announcement, and it is best read as part of a wider market swing rather than a re-rating of the battery maker on its own merits. That distinction matters, because the operating picture underneath the rally is more complicated than the price action suggests. Buybacks and swap deals sit behind the bounce Chinese sector coverage tied the recovery in battery stocks to several catalysts, among them CATL's own share repurchases and a string of battery-swapping partnerships. The company said it bought back 3,488,600 A-shares on Wednesday for roughly RMB 800 million, followed by a further 2,271,000 A-shares on Thursday for about RMB 499.9 million — purchases on two consecutive trading days. On the partnership front, CATL and the Shaanxi Transportation Holding Group signed a strategic cooperation agreement on Wednesday covering the electrification of commercial vehicles, battery-swap stations for heavy trucks, energy storage and highway charging infrastructure. Media reports also said CATL, its Chocolate Swap unit and Huawei subsidiary Yinwang agreed on Monday to link their systems technically, connecting Huawei's intelligent-driving technology with CATL's swap ecosystem. The planned vehicle-to-station sequence is designed to complete a battery swap in 99 seconds. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? Reuters, meanwhile, reported CATL's plans to expand its heavy-truck swap network to 900 stations in China by the end of the year, rising to 2,000 by 2027. Those targets give the cooperation agreements a concrete build-out schedule. The third-quarter numbers cut both ways The figures CATL reported on Tuesday for the third quarter of 2026 frame the tension. Revenue reached RMB 165.221 billion, up 58.58% year on year. Net profit attributable to shareholders came in at RMB 21.246 billion — 14.54% higher than a year earlier, but 5.77% lower than in the previous quarter. So the top line is expanding fast while the bottom line slipped sequentially. That gap is the crux for investors: the question is not whether CATL is growing, but whether profit can close the distance to revenue. Until that becomes clearer, the sales surge supports a constructive view without offering full reassurance. The reported gross margin of 20.69% gives a concrete data point to watch. A single figure says nothing about direction on its own, but combined with the next set of earnings it should help separate growth from earnings quality. JPMorgan steps back from its bullish call JPMorgan downgraded CATL's H-shares from Overweight to Neutral on Monday, cutting its price target to HK$500 from HK$725. The broker cited a faster-than-expected deterioration in industry profitability. That view goes to the heart of the investment case. If sector-wide earnings conditions keep worsening, even robust revenue growth may only partly support profit, and additional partnerships — strategically relevant as they are — would not be an immediate counterargument. CATL at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. Even after the target cut, the house kept its high-conviction expectation of above-average performance. The combination is what counts: lower expectations do not rule out a positive longer-term view, but they do demand closer scrutiny of earnings. What would confirm the recovery The bullish case rests on high revenue growth continuing while profit stabilizes, which would let the sequential decline look like a temporary soft patch and give the rebound a fundamental footing rather than mere market tailwind. The bearish case is equally concrete: surging sales paired with inadequate profit would mean friendly sentiment is papering over a persistent problem, and the quarterly profit drop would read as a warning rather than an anomaly. Further business figures and management commentary on profitability are the next real test, alongside tangible progress in integrating compatible BAIC models into CATL's Choco Swap network — a cooperation agreed on Thursday that both companies intend to serve one million vehicles. For now, neither the share-price jump nor a single analyst's target cut settles the argument. What matters is whether CATL can narrow the gap between dynamic revenue growth and weaker profit. artigo.texto: A fabricante americana de tintas e revestimentos PPG, sediada em Pittsburgh, projeta triplicar suas vendas de proteção industrial para data centers em 2026 na comparação com 2025. O crescimento decorre da corrida de empresas como Microsoft, Google e Amazon para erguer infraestruturas de inteligência artificial, movimentando um mercado onde cada obra consome entre US$ 3 milhões (R$ 15,1 milhões) e US$ 8 milhões (R$ 40,3 milhões) apenas com esses materiais. O avanço específico no setor de computação supera a média geral da companhia, que tem valor de mercado de US$ 24 bilhões (R$ 121 bilhões) e registrou alta de 7% nas vendas totais do trimestre mais recente, alcançando US$ 4,5 bilhões. “Nunca vi um boom tão grande quanto este”, disse Jenn Solcz, vice-presidente da divisão de revestimentos de proteção e marítimos da PPG para as Américas. Saiba mais: Inteligência Artificial na saúde exige cautela em consultas médicas Steelguard 951 e os testes da PPG contra fogo e eletricidade estática O produto central da PPG para atender os centros de dados é o revestimento intumescente cinza Steelguard 951, formulado para impedir que estruturas metálicas cedam durante incêndios. No Coatings Innovation Center, complexo de pesquisa situado em Allison Park, subúrbio a cerca de 21 km de Pittsburgh, a empresa realiza testes com maçaricos em um prédio de concreto conhecido como “o bunker”. Quando submetida ao fogo pelos pesquisadores, a camada aplicada sobre painéis de aço se expande de 1 milímetro de espessura para uma crosta preta de quase 10 milímetros de altura, retendo o ar para isolar o metal e evitar que ele amoleça sob alta temperatura. Paul Fenton, químico pesquisador sênior e engenheiro de testes da PPG, conduziu as demonstrações de resistência térmica no laboratório. “É como um marshmallow tostado, que gosta de se expandir”, afirmou Fenton, explicando que o ar retido no material expandido “mantém tudo frio”. Amy Ericson, vice-presidente sênior da PPG, diferenciou a tecnologia industrial dos produtos domésticos formados por simples pintura. “Não é como entrar em uma loja, comprar uma lata de tinta e passá-la na parede”, declarou a executiva sobre o sistema composto por primer de aderência, camada funcional e acabamento. Em abril de 2026, durante uma feira do setor em Washington, a fabricante apresentou um pacote de soluções adaptado para instalações de inteligência artificial e fábricas de chips, cobrindo mais de 75 componentes de um data center: Saiba mais: Inteligência artificial tem estrutura interna limpa, diz estudo - Revestimento intumescente Steelguard 951 para proteção de vigas e estruturas de aço contra fogo; - Isolante térmico Pitt-Therm 909 para manter frias as tubulações de água e impedir a condensação sobre equipamentos elétricos; - Pisos especiais projetados para evitar descargas de eletricidade estática que possam danificar servidores ou iniciar incêndios; - Primers antiferrugem e camadas que bloqueiam interferências elétricas entre máquinas; - Revestimentos específicos para equipamentos de refrigeração e carcaças de câmeras de segurança. Custos por obra e avanço da concorrente Sherwin-Williams A expansão da infraestrutura de computação — que já impulsionou fabricantes de chips como a Nvidia, laboratórios como OpenAI e Anthropic, além de fornecedores de brita, fios e cabos — também elevou os resultados da Sherwin-Williams, principal concorrente da PPG. Em julho de 2026, a presidente-executiva (CEO) da Sherwin-Williams, Heidi Petz, informou que as vendas da divisão de revestimentos de proteção e marítimos da empresa cresceram na casa dos dois dígitos, na faixa intermediária da escala, em relação ao ano anterior, puxadas pela aplicação de produtos das vigas de aço aos racks de servidores. Na companhia, o braço de revestimentos de performance também teve avanço superior a 6% nos dois últimos trimestres consecutivos. “Velocidade importa”, disse Petz. Veja também: Inteligência artificial no trabalho: modelo da LaunchReady.ai define 7 níveis de maturidade profissional Segundo Matthew Giddings, executivo que atua na administração de data centers na consultoria imobiliária comercial JLL, os produtos químicos são aplicados “das paredes às coberturas dos telhados, passando pelas estruturas de aço e pela parte externa do edifício” para evitar incêndios em salas elétricas e controlar a estática. Como os prédios abrigam majoritariamente servidores e quase não há circulação de pessoas, a aparência não é prioridade: a PPG fornece basicamente variações de cinza-claro, cinza e cinza-escuro. De acordo com Jenn Solcz, a estética “não está exatamente entre as principais preocupações de nossos clientes, nem dos proprietários de data centers, arquitetos e engenheiros com quem conversamos”. Mudança de foco da PPG em 2024 e gargalos de energia nos Estados Unidos Fundada em 1883 como Pittsburgh Plate Glass Corporation para fabricar vidro, a PPG reformulou seu modelo de negócios em 2024 ao vender suas lojas de tintas nos Estados Unidos e no Canadá, incluindo a marca varejista Glidden, comercializada na rede Home Depot. Desde então, a empresa concentrou a operação no fornecimento industrial para montadoras de carros, fabricantes de aviões, latas de bebidas e grandes obras. A mobilização para o setor de tecnologia teve início após o lançamento do ChatGPT pela OpenAI no fim de 2022. Como um data center é erguido em cerca de um terço do tempo de uma obra de infraestrutura tradicional, a PPG criou equipes exclusivas para atuar junto a engenheiros, arquitetos e gigantes de tecnologia antes do início das construções. Em conferência de resultados do segundo trimestre, realizada em julho de 2026, o CEO da PPG, Tim Knavish, destacou a demanda do setor: “Há uma carteira considerável de projetos em trabalhos de data centers, o que inclui não apenas proteção contra incêndio, mas pisos para aço estrutural, revestimentos isolantes e revestimentos dielétricos”, disse, em tradução livre. artigo.texto: CATL's 13,000-Truck Order Book Meets a 93.59% Cash Flow Collapse Published on 10/23/2026 at 15:11 | Editorial boerse-global.de Bank of America Securities trimmed its price target on CATL from 775 to 630 HKD, yet kept its "Buy" rating intact — a combination that captures the central tension in the battery maker's investment case. Robust demand is no longer the question. Converting that demand into dependable earnings and cash is. The brokerage now models higher shipments of energy-storage batteries but lower average battery prices and thinner gross margins. More units, in other words, no longer translate automatically into proportionally more profit. Its revised forecasts cut adjusted net profit by 8.6% for 2026 and by 14.8% for 2027 — and the fact that the outer year takes the deeper hit undercuts any reading of this as a one-quarter blip. A Quarter That Splits Growth From Profitability Tuesday's results laid out the gap in hard numbers. Revenue for the third quarter of 2026 reached 165.221 billion RMB, up 58.58% year on year, according to media reports. Net profit attributable to shareholders came in at 21.246 billion RMB, a gain of just 14.54%. The gross margin stood at 20.69%. That divergence is the metric to watch in coming reports: does the spread between top-line and bottom-line growth narrow? Until it does, additional scale offers no sufficient proof of stronger earning power. A convergence of the two rates would signal that CATL is wringing more out of its expansion. Cash generation sharpens the concern. Operating cash flow for the first nine months fell 23.60% year on year, while the third quarter alone saw a 93.59% plunge — the weakest reading since the second quarter of 2018, per media reports. CATL points to shorter payment terms with suppliers, higher advance payments and long-running overseas projects. Those are concrete explanations for the cash tie-up, but they do not alter the fact that the core business released far less money. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? Earnings took separate hits. A higher share of lower-value-added products and changed tax conditions weighed on profit, the company said, with the consumption tax on lithium batteries and a reduced export tax rebate compounding a problem that extra volume alone cannot fix. Heavy Trucks as the Demand Case The bullish counterweight sits in commercial vehicles. At Tuesday's launch of its Tianxing-II battery solution, CATL reported signed initial orders for 13,000 heavy trucks — a firmer demand signal than a bare product announcement. Reuters also reported that the Qiji system can swap a truck battery in roughly five minutes, with the economic opportunity lying in pairing that technology with a growing swap network. Rollout targets give the strategy a calendar. CATL aims for 900 heavy-truck swap stations in China by year-end and 2,000 by 2027, according to Reuters. Both are expansion goals, not installed totals. Station counts can make strategic progress visible; they do not by themselves settle the question of profitability. Market Share Slips as Competition Bites Against that stands a genuine risk. Reuters reported that intensifying battery competition and a cooling in Chinese car sales weighed on development — conditions under which a sharp revenue rise need not produce a matching profit increase. CATL's share of China's installed traction-battery market fell from 49.8% in January to 40.9% in September, Reuters said. The company can expand its business while ceding ground, and a sustained trend would further limit the economic benefit of extra sales. Share buybacks continued yesterday, with the repurchased stock earmarked for cancellation, according to media reports. That matters for the capital structure but says nothing about future earnings quality. What Would Change the Verdict Wednesday's 7.8% share-price gain is a positive market signal, not a fundamental turning point. It overturns neither the lowered profit forecasts nor last quarter's weak cash generation. The proof point is whether CATL can bring growth, profitability and operating cash flow back into alignment — and whether the truck orders and swap-station buildout turn into economically viable additional business. Demand, the company has already demonstrated. Turning it into retained financial firepower is the harder test. Ad CATL Stock: New Analysis - 23 October Fresh CATL information released. artigo.texto: CATL's Swap-Network Push Meets a Sobering Reset in Earnings Expectations Published on 10/23/2026 at 15:02 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL shares climbed 7.8% as part of a broader rebound across the lithium battery sector, a move that market commentary does not tie to any fresh company-specific catalyst. The gain offers little insight into the company's strategy on its own. Two separate developments tell a more useful story: a pair of battery-swapping partnerships that broaden CATL's ecosystem ambitions, and a downbeat revision from Bank of America Securities that questions how efficiently the company converts growth into profit. Wiring Vehicles to the Swap Network CATL and BAIC have signed a strategic cooperation agreement to improve the compatibility of vehicles with battery-swapping systems and to build out the supporting infrastructure. Their stated goal is to serve one million vehicles. BAIC intends to connect models from several of its group brands to CATL's Choco-Swap network. Perhaps the less glamorous part of the deal carries the most weight: BAIC will open its dealer network for the construction of swap stations. That brings site access for infrastructure into the arrangement, not just the vehicle side. A swap network and compatible cars are not separate stories, and the partners aim to advance both at once — an approach that addresses several preconditions for using the system simultaneously. The scale of the target should not be mistaken for an existing fleet. One million vehicles to be served is a goal, and both the planned model integration and the dealer-network opening describe intentions rather than completed build-out. The BAIC pact sits alongside another collaboration on the swap ecosystem. On Monday, Yinwang, CATL and Contemporary Amperex Energy Service Technology signed an agreement that Reuters reports will link Huawei's Qiankun intelligent driving system with CATL's Choco battery-swap ecosystem, covering compatible vehicles and the station network. That widens the scope: it is not only about connecting more models to a network, but also about integrating an intelligent driving system. Whether that produces a compelling combined offering cannot be read from a signed agreement alone, though the direction is clear — CATL is seeking links between vehicle technology and swap infrastructure. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? A different application area surfaced on Tuesday, when CATL presented a dual-electric battery system for extended range along with upgraded swap solutions for heavy trucks. Bloomberg reported announced agreements covering 13,000 units, including orders from SF Holding and China Postal Express & Logistics. Unlike the BAIC cooperation, where a joint expansion target takes center stage, this announcement comes with orders behind it. The two should be neither equated nor viewed in isolation: CATL is pursuing battery swapping across different vehicle applications and with different partners. A Buy Rating With a Lower Bar Bank of America Securities cut its price target on CATL to 630 HKD from 775 HKD, while keeping its "Buy" rating. That is not a full retreat, but it is a markedly more cautious view of earnings prospects. The reasoning behind the lower target matters. The bank expects higher shipments of energy storage batteries, but also lower average battery prices and gross margins. In that arithmetic, more volume does not automatically mean proportionally more profit. The firm trimmed its forecast for adjusted net profit by 8.6% for 2026 and by 14.8% for 2027. The steeper cut to the later estimate argues against the convenient explanation of a merely temporary quarterly hiccup. The unchanged buy rating should not obscure the reduced expectations. It shows the bank still sees opportunity, but it removes neither the pricing pressure nor the strain on profitability. A convincing re-rating would require more from CATL than rising shipment volumes. The Cash-Flow Signal In the third quarter of 2026, revenue rose 58.58% year on year, while net profit grew 14.54%. The gross margin stood at 20.69%. The company is expanding briskly but translating that growth only partially into additional earning power. That gap matters more than the impressive top-line figure in isolation: expansion loses quality for shareholders when a smaller share of revenue remains as gross profit. The operating cash flow figure is sharper still. It collapsed 93.59% compared with the prior-year quarter and, according to media reports, reached its lowest level since the second quarter of 2018. CATL cites shorter payment terms with suppliers, higher advance payments and long-running overseas projects. Those are concrete explanations for the cash tie-up, but they do not alter the fact that the running business released considerably less money. CATL at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. Earnings pressures are tangible as well. According to the company, a higher share of less value-added products and changed tax conditions weighed on profit. The consumption tax on lithium batteries and a reduced export tax rebate compound a problem that additional units alone cannot solve. The weak cash flow is neither proof of a lasting crisis nor a trivial accounting effect — it is a test. The cited payment and project conditions explain the strain but do not substitute for evidence of later improvement. What the Rally Does Not Prove Against that backdrop, the 7.8% advance is no all-clear. A single positive session refutes neither the lowered profit forecasts nor the weak cash generation of the past quarter. The operating question remains how much financial room the growing business actually leaves behind. CATL has already shown that demand can support strong revenue growth. artigo.texto: A proposta de metodologia para o “Restauro e Conservação de Pradarias Marinhas em Portugal Continental”, que alarga o Mercado Voluntário de Carbono (MVC) aos ecossistemas marinhos, entrou hoje em consulta pública, anunciou o Ministério do Ambiente e Energia. A iniciativa visa criar condições para mobilizar financiamento privado para a recuperação e conservação destes ecossistemas, promovendo em simultâneo os benefícios climáticos e a proteção da biodiversidade através do conceito de carbono azul. De acordo com o comunicado do ministério liderado por Maria da Graça Carvalho, os documentos ficarão disponíveis para recolha de contributos no portal Participa até ao dia 22 de novembro de 2026. “Queremos que o Mercado Voluntário de Carbono seja também um instrumento para financiar a recuperação da natureza. Com esta nova metodologia, damos um passo concreto para valorizar o carbono azul e o papel dos ecossistemas marinhos na ação climática”, afirmou a Ministra do Ambiente e Energia. A proposta de metodologia foi apresentada pela ANA – Aeroportos de Portugal, S.A., em parceria com a NBI Natural Business Intelligence, o Centro de Ciências do Mar da Universidade do Algarve e o Instituto Mediterráneo de Estudios Avanzados, tendo recebido um parecer favorável da Comissão Técnica de Acompanhamento do Mercado Voluntário de Carbono. O parecer técnico destaca a inovação da proposta e sublinha a oportunidade de atrair investimento privado para a recuperação do ecossistema marinho, bem como para o reforço do conhecimento científico e a diversificação de projetos no âmbito do MVC. A metodologia prevê a atribuição de “Créditos de Carbono +” a projetos que demonstrem ganhos adicionais para o capital natural e a biodiversidade, alinhando-se com as metas do Plano Nacional de Restauro da Natureza (PNRN). Ao assinalar o primeiro ano de atividade, a tutela informou que o MVC conta atualmente com três metodologias aprovadas, cinco projetos submetidos — dos quais dois já obtiveram aprovação —, 10 verificadores qualificados, 30 utilizadores registados e 977 créditos de carbono futuros emitidos. Maria da Graça Carvalho assinalou que, após um ano inicial focado na estruturação do mercado, a prioridade passa agora por “acelerar a sua dinamização, com mais projetos, novas metodologias e maior procura de créditos de carbono nacionais, para canalizar mais investimento privado para a descarbonização e para a valorização dos nossos recursos naturais”. artigo.texto: Solar Batteries for Home Energy Storage: Howell Energy's Rechargeable LiFePO4 Power Wall Solutions SHENZHEN, GUANGDONG, CHINA, October 25, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ -- Residential solar photovoltaic installations require dependable energy storage systems to increase self-consumption and provide uninterrupted backup power. Homeowners and solar installers prioritize wall-mounted battery units offering high energy density, multi-inverter protocol matching, and certified safety. Leveraging direct cell-to-pack manufacturing in Jiangsu and Dongguan, Howell Energy Co., Ltd. engineers premium wall mounted solar batteries for home energy storage with 51.2V 100Ah 5kWh capacities. Supported by 20+ years of factory heritage, these systems interface smoothly with mainstream hybrid inverters. Solar installers and system integrators evaluate four core supplier capabilities before deploying residential battery solutions: Modular 5kWh Storage Capacity: Standardized 51.2V 100Ah energy modules provide flexible plug-and-play capacity expansion up to 80 kWh. 6000 Deep Cycle Longevity: Premium prismatic LiFePO4 cells deliver over 6000 cycles at 80 percent depth of discharge for fifteen-year longevity. Multi-Brand Inverter Compatibility: Integrated CAN and RS485 communication protocols match leading global hybrid inverter brands. Extended 5 to 10 Year Warranty Coverage: Complete factory backing ensures long-term asset security and predictable return on solar investment. Modular Residential Energy Storage Form Factors Residential installations vary significantly across property types, available utility room spaces, and homeowner energy demands. Howell Energy manufactures a versatile portfolio of home energy storage architectures designed for clean residential environments. Installers select between wall-mounted Powerwall units, standard 19-inch rack modules, and high-capacity floor cabinets. The primary residential configurations include the following three engineered form factors: Wall-Mounted Powerwall Systems: Slim 48V and 51.2V architectures available in 5.12 kWh (100Ah) and high-density 10.24 kWh (200Ah) configurations, featuring integrated DC disconnects and optional front LCD status panels. Standard 19-Inch Rack-Mounted Battery Modules: Modular slide-in units, ranging from compact 2.56 kWh (50Ah) to 5.12 kWh (100Ah) units, designed for vertical cabinet expansion in space-constrained utility rooms. The BMS automatically identifies connected inverter models and establishes closed-loop digital control via standard CAN and RS485 communication ports. The internal control firmware matches major international inverter brands, including Deye, Growatt, Victron Energy, GoodWe, Solis, and Sofar Solar. Through synchronized data transfer, the inverter monitors real-time battery state of charge, cell voltages, operating temperature, and allowable charge current limits. This automated closed-loop management prevents cell overcharging, maintains balanced energy conversion, and improves overall round-trip storage efficiency. The smart BMS also integrates dual active and passive cell balancing circuits. During float charging cycles, internal balancing resistors redistribute energy across series cells, maintaining voltage variance within narrow millivolt bands. Integrated Coulomb-counting algorithms calculate precise state of charge metrics displayed on the external LCD screen and transmitted to mobile management applications. Howell Energy home storage assemblies comply with rigorous international electrotechnical safety certifications. Systems carry accredited testing certificates for UL 1973, UL 1642, UL 2054, IEC 62619, IEC 62133, and European CE directives. In addition, all battery assemblies pass UN 38.3 transport safety evaluations, including thermal shock, altitude simulation, vibration, and impact testing protocols. Enclosures are manufactured from heavy-gauge galvanized steel coated with flame-retardant industrial powder coatings. Depending on installation requirements, enclosures range from standard IP21 for indoor rack cabinets up to IP55 or IP65 sealed ratings for wall-mounted outdoor deployments. artigo.texto: Deutsche Bank has acted as original lender and mandated lead arranger on the refinancing of Akaysha Energy’s 1086-MW Australian battery energy storage system (BESS) portfolio, participating in the longer-tenor tranches of the AUS$1.75 billion senior secured, non-recourse portfolio financing. As the largest lender in the 10-year tranche, Deutsche Bank’s participation underscores its commitment to providing long-term capital to support the continued growth of Akaysha Energy’s Australian battery storage portfolio. The facility refinances existing project-level debt across four utility scale BESS assets into a single portfolio-level financing structure, providing a streamlined, flexible, and scalable framework to support Akaysha Energy’s continued portfolio expansion and the evolving need for large scale energy storage. The financing supports a portfolio comprising Ulinda Park 1, Brendale, Orana, and Elaine BESS, located across Queensland, New South Wales, and Victoria. Ulinda Park 1, Brendale, and Orana are already operational while Elaine remains on track to complete construction in 2H27. The financing also incorporates additional flexibility as Akaysha Energy advances its 5.7 GW/22.9 GWh+ Australian development pipeline across the National Electricity Market. Rachel Chia, Head of Project Finance, APAC at Deutsche Bank, commented: “We are pleased to have worked with Akaysha Energy to move beyond individual project financings and create a platform for portfolio growth. We are delighted to support this transaction, drawing on our project finance expertise to bring operational and construction-stage assets into one structure that meets the needs of a growing battery storage portfolio.” For more news and technical articles from the global renewable industry, read the latest issue of Energy Global magazine. artigo.texto: BYD Balances Next-Gen Battery Ambitions Against Cautious Analyst Revisions Published on 10/25/2026 at 02:51 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD has reaffirmed its commitment to megawatt fast-charging, a next-generation Blade battery and integrated body-battery technology, outlining the priorities on an investor platform. The disclosure confirms the company's technological direction but stops well short of a finished development milestone or a launch date — a distinction that matters for anyone trying to translate R&D talk into revenue. No performance figures accompanied the announcement. BYD said it will publish progress updates once formal disclosure obligations are triggered, which rules out reading a near-term product debut into the statement. The message underscores how central battery and charging technology remain to the development roadmap, yet it offers no basis for quantifying future sales or earnings contributions. Separating technological potential from commercially proven success stays the key exercise for valuation. That separation is already visible in showroom reality. On Tuesday BYD launched the second-generation Seagull in China, priced from 65,900 yuan, with Flash Charging versions starting at 75,900 yuan. The move puts fast-charging hardware into the budget end of the lineup rather than reserving it for premium models. The advertised charging speed, however, depends on compatible stations — the car's technical capability alone does not guarantee the same charging rate at every plug. For equipped variants, BYD quotes a 10% to 70% charge in 5 minutes. Those figures describe the Seagull technology on offer, not the next-generation development steps flagged today. A European launch for the new Seagull has not been confirmed, so the Chinese sales start implies no European volume contribution; the domestic rollout is the near-term focus. A Rebound With a Split Message The stock gained 4.4% on Friday, carried by a broad recovery across Hong Kong-listed electric-vehicle and technology names as investors returned following the previous session's selloff, according to media reports. The bounce was therefore not an isolated response to any company announcement — other automakers and lithium-battery shares advanced too. That distinction matters: buying after a weak session points to improved market sentiment, not automatically to revised business expectations for BYD. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? Valuation signals have turned more cautious even so. CLSA cut its price target on Friday to HK$104 from HK$120, while analyst Xiao Feng kept his emphatic recommendation to expect above-average share performance. The message is two-sided. The lower target caps expectations relative to the prior view; the retained rating signals the brokerage has not abandoned its constructive stance. The revision is neither a sell call nor an unchanged valuation. Citi offers a different yardstick. On October 15 the bank reiterated its buy recommendation with a target of HK$142 and forecast a net profit of RMB 12.95 billion. That estimate excludes currency effects and the contribution from BYD Electronic, making it explicitly an adjusted expectation rather than a reported result. Any later comparison with published earnings must account for the different scope. Both houses point in the same positive direction on recommendations while diverging on targets — reason enough to keep the market rebound separate from the question of which operating trajectory justifies each valuation. Earnings Risks Weigh Differently The technology push runs alongside a more cautious read on the business. One brokerage cites weak domestic demand, higher input costs and policy uncertainty as grounds for caution. Barclays, by contrast, sticks with "Overweight" and points to global expansion, while acknowledging softer domestic volumes after subsidy cuts and amid tougher competition. The differing emphasis makes one point plain: growth opportunities alone do not answer the question of future profitability, and the economic proof behind the development strategy remains a central valuation yardstick. BYD at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. BYD's statement today sharpens its research priorities without removing those earnings risks. Verifiable development progress and its conversion into sellable products will be what counts. Without performance data and launch dates, the next battery generation remains a development prospect rather than a secured earnings driver. October 30 Becomes the Next Concrete Test BYD is scheduled to publish its third-quarter 2026 report on October 30. The confirmed date shifts attention from short-term sector moves to actual business performance. Two layers now sit side by side for anyone sizing up the stock: the recent rally is explained by a friendlier market backdrop, while whether the business supports it can only be judged from published results. The quarterly report provides the next hard evidence — even as analysts, positive recommendations notwithstanding, apply markedly different valuation standards. artigo.texto: Iniciativa nos EUA prevê incentivos para residências e empresas reduzirem o consumo; capacidade disponibilizada ao Google equivale à de um reator nuclear O Google anunciou uma iniciativa para ajudar a reduzir a pressão sobre a rede elétrica nos Estados Unidos. A empresa firmou um acordo com a Voltus para criar uma espécie de “usina virtual”, que reunirá a capacidade de residências e empresas de diminuir o consumo de eletricidade em períodos de alta demanda, em troca de incentivos financeiros. O projeto poderá disponibilizar até 1.070 megawatts de capacidade elétrica, volume comparável à produção de um grande reator nuclear. Em vez de depender exclusivamente da construção de novas usinas, a proposta busca aproveitar a energia que pode ser economizada por consumidores quando o sistema elétrico estiver sobrecarregado. A redução do consumo poderá ocorrer de diferentes maneiras. Entre as possibilidades estão o ajuste automático de termostatos inteligentes, diminuindo o uso do ar-condicionado nos horários de pico, e a utilização de baterias para fornecer energia temporariamente. Cada medida representa uma economia pequena, mas o resultado pode ser significativo quando milhares de participantes aderem ao programa. Veja também Meta é condenada a pagar US$ 2,5 bilhões em processo sobre privacidade de dados Como Subir de Elo em Wild Rift: Estratégias, Mentalidade e Dicas para Ranqueadas A iniciativa surge em meio ao aumento da demanda por eletricidade provocado pela expansão da inteligência artificial e dos grandes centros de processamento de dados. Essas estruturas consomem grandes quantidades de energia para manter servidores, equipamentos e sistemas de refrigeração em funcionamento, ampliando a necessidade de soluções que garantam o abastecimento sem sobrecarregar a rede. Curtiu? Siga o PORTAL DO ZACARIAS no Facebook, Twitter e no Instagram. Entre no nosso Grupo de WhatApp, Canal e Telegram Apesar da nova estratégia, o Google ainda poderá precisar de investimentos em fontes convencionais e alternativas de geração para acompanhar a expansão de seus data centers. A empresa considera que as usinas virtuais podem funcionar como uma solução mais rápida e potencialmente menos poluente para atender às necessidades imediatas do setor, ao mesmo tempo que oferece compensações financeiras a consumidores dispostos a reduzir o próprio consumo.

artigo.texto: CATL's Firefly Battery Win Sits Alongside Buybacks and a Truck-Swap Gamble Published on 10/24/2026 at 16:31 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL has confirmed that Nio's Firefly will run its Qilin battery in a new 60-kWh pack, giving the compact EV a range of 560 kilometres on China's CLTC test cycle. The pack, which launched a day earlier, uses NCM cells rather than the LFP unit supplied by Sunwoda that has powered the Firefly until now. For the battery giant, the announcement is a tangible product-level marker of a partnership that has so far been mostly a piece of paper: the two companies signed a five-year strategic cooperation agreement in January. What the confirmation does not carry is a number. No sales volume, revenue contribution or profit effect has been attached to the Firefly deployment, leaving investors to weigh a concrete customer project against the absence of any quantified financial impact. Three Ways to Buy the Bigger Pack Pricing details show how Ningde-based CATL and Nio intend to push the larger battery into the market. The Firefly with the new pack starts at 136,800 yuan outright. Under the BaaS battery-rental model, the vehicle itself begins at 79,800 yuan, with a monthly battery fee of 599 yuan on top. The offer is not confined to new-car buyers. Existing owners can upgrade under certain conditions: outright purchasers pay 17,000 yuan after holding the car for at least a year, while current BaaS customers face a 3,000 yuan service fee before moving onto the higher monthly rental. That retrofit route pulls the installed base into the equation and widens the potential footprint of the Qilin cell inside the Firefly line-up. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? No Bet on a Single Chemistry The Firefly deal fits CATL's parallel work across several battery technologies. Akin Li, head of international business, said it remains unclear which chemistry will dominate by 2035, noting that the company is developing LFP, NMC, sodium-ion and solid-state batteries side by side. Li also pointed to substantial hurdles in the commercial mass production of solid-state cells. The Firefly confirmation, by contrast, concerns technology already in service and a vehicle programme already on the road. Buybacks Put Capital Behind the Story Alongside the product news, CATL has been putting money to work in its own equity. The company bought back A-shares on Wednesday and Thursday for a combined roughly 1.299 billion RMB, with the shares acquired on Thursday earmarked for cancellation. The move followed a 7.8% gain on Wednesday, when the stock rode a broader recovery in Chinese battery and electric-vehicle names as investors returned to growth shares after a sell-off. That bounce was framed as a rebound from oversold conditions rather than a confirmed turning point — a friendlier tape can ease selling pressure without settling the underlying business questions. A buyback is not a substitute for operating progress. It shows the company is willing to spend on its own stock; it does not by itself improve competitive standing or guarantee a lasting recovery. The distinction matters most after a sharp drawdown, when corporate demand for its own paper and the earning power of the business answer two different questions. Revenue Outpaces Profit Those questions have a hard backdrop in the third-quarter 2026 figures. Revenue climbed 58.58% while net profit attributable to shareholders rose 14.54% — the top line grew far faster than the bottom line. Reuters reported that profit growth fell short of analyst expectations, citing tougher competition in the battery market and slower growth in Chinese car sales. The larger trend, then, is not simply a story of rising demand; for CATL it is also about converting growth into earnings. Stronger business momentum can impress and still miss forecasts. CATL at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. Heavy Trucks and 2,000 Swap Stations The longer-term answer is being sought in heavy trucks. On Tuesday the company unveiled a new battery generation and sketched the expansion of its QIJI battery-swap network, targeting 900 swap stations in China by the end of this year and 2,000 by 2027, according to Reuters. These are build-out goals, not stations already in place. Still, the step ties battery development to a widening swap infrastructure, pushing the industrial wager beyond any single product and giving investors a firmer yardstick than a single session's sentiment. Read together, the pieces form a sober picture: a market backdrop explains the recent lift, the buybacks show concrete capital deployment, and the network plan describes where CATL wants to direct part of its development. The Firefly contract proves the company can convert partnerships into shipped product. Whether that combination turns into stronger earnings is a question neither the share-price jump nor the battery announcement answers on its own. The global market for lithium metal protective additives is a specialized niche within the advanced battery materials ecosystem, poised for significant expansion over the 2026-2035 forecast period. These functional, high-purity, and specialty chemical formulations are critical for stabilizing the interface between lithium metal anodes and electrolytes, mitigating dendrite formation, and extending cycle life in next-generation batteries. As of the 2026 base year, the market is driven by the accelerating transition to electric mobility, the proliferation of high-energy-density portable electronics, and the growing need for stationary energy storage solutions. While still a relatively small segment compared to mainstream battery materials, protective additives are projected to experience robust growth, underpinned by rapid technological advances and increasing commercialization of lithium metal batteries. The competitive landscape remains fragmented, featuring a mix of established chemical corporations, specialized battery material suppliers, and venture-backed startups. Demand is outpacing supply in several regions, leading to strategic partnerships between additive producers and battery manufacturers. Challenges persist in cost optimization, scalability of synthesis processes, and regulatory hurdles related to reactive lithium-based materials. Nevertheless, the long-term outlook is positive, with protective additives poised to become a standard component in commercial lithium metal battery designs by the early 2030s. This analysis synthesizes core findings on market structure, demand drivers, supply dynamics, trade patterns, pricing behavior, and competitive positioning, providing a data-grounded roadmap for stakeholders through 2035. The functional grades segment will benefit from widespread adoption in industrial processing and formulation, while high-purity grades will see increased use in research and development for next-generation solid-state batteries. Regionally, Asia-Pacific is projected to maintain its dominance, supported by China's aggressive battery production targets and the presence of major battery manufacturers. North America and Europe will experience above-average growth, driven by government initiatives and investments in domestic battery supply chains. Supply constraints, including the limited availability of high-purity precursors and the complexity of scaling up production, may temper growth in the short term. However, ongoing capacity expansions and strategic partnerships between additive producers and battery makers are expected to alleviate these bottlenecks. Pricing is forecast to remain premium, reflecting the specialized nature of these additives and the stringent quality requirements. Overall, the market is poised for a period of dynamic expansion, with opportunities for both established players and new entrants. Currently, most EVs use conventional lithium-ion batteries, but the transition to lithium metal anodes is accelerating, particularly in premium and long-range models. Protective additives are essential to stabilize the lithium metal interface, preventing dendrite formation and improving cycle life. Through 2035, demand will be driven by the growing EV production volumes, especially in China, Europe, and North America, and the increasing penetration of solid-state batteries. Key demand-side indicators include EV sales, battery energy density targets, and the number of lithium metal battery gigafactories. The mechanism is straightforward: as battery manufacturers scale up lithium metal anode production, they require larger volumes of protective additives to ensure safety and performance, leading to a direct correlation between EV adoption and additive demand. artigo.texto: Inteligência artificial, data centers, soberania digital, terras raras, mudanças climáticas e transição energética estão entre os principais desafios que o próximo presidente do Brasil terá de enfrentar. O Olhar Digital consultou especialistas para analisar as propostas de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), candidatos que disputam o segundo turno das Eleições 2026, para cada um desses eixos estratégicos. A forma como lidamos com a tecnologia mudou drasticamente. Durante anos, usamos computadores e programas simples apenas para automatizar tarefas do dia a dia. Hoje, o avanço da IA generativa – capaz de criar conteúdos, analisar dados complexos e tomar decisões – exige computadores e centrais de processamento muito mais potentes. Para qualquer país, acompanhar essa evolução virou uma questão de sobrevivência econômica. O Brasil ocupa uma posição altamente estratégica nesse ecossistema. Já possuímos uma das matrizes elétricas mais limpas do planeta, característica ideal para suprir o altíssimo consumo de energia exigido pelos data centers e supercomputadores, além de contar com um enorme mercado consumidor interno. No entanto, a dependência externa e o avanço desregrado de algoritmos trazem sérios riscos à segurança nacional, à privacidade, ao emprego e à proliferação de desinformação. Em paralelo, a geopolítica das tecnologias emergentes exige autonomia sobre recursos minerais críticos e terras raras – eixos indispensáveis para a fabricação de hardware, baterias, painéis solares e sistemas de defesa. O Brasil detém a segunda maior reserva mundial desses elementos, e o debate central gira em torno de processar esses insumos no país em vez de exportar matéria-prima bruta. Diante desse cenário, a transição energética – a substituição gradual de combustíveis fósseis por fontes limpas – torna-se indissociável da pauta tecnológica e ambiental, especialmente em um país vulnerável a eventos climáticos extremos que causam impactos severos à infraestrutura e à economia. Quem são os especialistas consultados pelo Olhar Digital Para analisar as propostas relacionadas à tecnologia e à soberania digital, o Olhar Digital ouviu JB Queiroz Filho, empresário, especialista em transformação digital e CEO da JBQ.Global, consultoria voltada para inovação e tecnologia da informação; Lucas Reis, pesquisador do Instituto Nacional de Ciência e Tecnologia em Democracia Digital (INCT.DD); e Thiago Muniz, especialista em economia digital e estratégia de negócios, além de professor da Fundação Getúlio Vargas (FGV). Na área de minerais críticos e terras raras, participaram o geólogo Álvaro Penteado Crósta, autoridade em exploração mineral, professor emérito da Universidade Estadual de Campinas (Unicamp) e membro titular da Academia Brasileira de Ciências (ABC); e o neurocientista e futurista Álvaro Machado Dias, professor livre-docente da Universidade Federal de São Paulo (Unifesp) e colunista do Olhar Digital. Já a análise das propostas para mudanças climáticas e transição energética contou com Paulo Eduardo Artaxo Netto, físico com doutorado em física atmosférica e professor titular do Instituto de Física da Universidade de São Paulo (USP). Vamos agora ao resumo dos planos de cada candidatura: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) No plano de governo de Lula, a IA, os data centers, a soberania digital, o uso de minerais críticos e a transição energética são eixos centrais de um projeto de reindustrialização verde (Nova Indústria Brasil) sob coordenação ativa do Estado. A candidatura reafirma o compromisso de garantir que o país desenvolva tecnologia própria, regule o setor para evitar abusos e proteja o trabalho de criadores e profissionais. Na área de regulação, direitos e governança, a proposta prevê a criação do Centro Nacional de Transparência Algorítmica, a regulamentação para remunerar artistas e criadores pelo uso de obras no treinamento de IAs, o combate às fake news associado à regulação de redes e a defesa de regras globais de governança digital. Para os serviços públicos e a economia, o plano propõe a difusão de inteligência artificial no agronegócio, no Sistema Nacional de Emprego (SINE) e na saúde, com triagem inteligente no Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS). Em infraestrutura tecnológica e soberania, projeta a atração de data centers e supercomputadores vinculada ao uso obrigatório de energia limpa, eficiência energética e reserva de capacidade computacional para pesquisas nacionais, além da criação do Conselho Nacional pela Soberania Digital, do desenvolvimento de IAs nativas em português e da implementação do Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescente Digital (ECA Digital). Quanto aos recursos minerais estratégicos, a prioridade é a consolidação da Política Nacional de Minerais Críticos sob gestão estatal, estabelecendo exigências legais para que o beneficiamento e a separação química de terras raras ocorram em solo nacional. A proposta estabelece exigências legais para que o beneficiamento e o refino químico de terras raras ocorram em solo nacional, evitando a exportação de minério bruto sem valor agregado. Para isso, o projeto estabelece a Região Nordeste como polo de plantas industriais movidas a energia eólica e solar, contando com financiamentos do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES), investimentos de empresas públicas e cooperação com universidades brasileiras. No cenário internacional, a candidatura defende alianças geopolíticas diversificadas com países do Sul Global, o bloco dos BRICS (grupo que reúne nações emergentes como China, Índia e Rússia) e também os Estados Unidos, focando na cooperação e na transferência mútua de tecnologia. EMA Launches Energy Storage Vision and Calls for Industry Solutions to Scale Deployment 26 Oct 2026 Media Releases 26 Oct 2026 Share The Energy Market Authority (EMA) has launched an Energy Storage Systems Vision and Industry Consultation Paper, calling on the industry to propose practical energy storage technologies, business models, and projects that can be commercially deployed at scale. Singapore aims to triple its energy storage capacity from about 350 megawatt-hours (MWh) today to around 1 gigawatt-hour (GWh) by 2030. Singapore’s power system is changing. Electricity demand is expected to grow rapidly over the next several years, driven by new large demand loads such as semiconductors, data centres, and electrification of the transport system. The use of renewable energy such as domestic solar is also likely to continue its strong momentum. The increase in large discrete loads, coupled with the larger impact of solar intermittency, can make it more difficult to maintain the current high standards of reliability of the Singapore power system. These developments increase the need for flexibility – the ability to adjust electricity supply and demand when needed. How Energy Storage Can Support Singapore's Power System ESS can help Singapore’s power system respond to changing electricity needs in several ways: Strengthening power system reliability: ESS can respond quickly to fluctuations in solar generation and other supply disruptions to help maintain the power system’s stability. Managing electricity demand when network capacity is limited: Should there be high demand for electricity in some areas of Singapore, such as through increased electricity demand for electric vehicle charging, the electricity that an ESS has stored can be released to meet the additional demand. This would reduce the strain on the electricity network. Harnessing smaller ESS to support the power system: ESS in homes, businesses, and electric vehicles could be coordinated to collectively support Singapore's power system, including through arrangements known as Virtual Power Plants (VPP). Puah Kok Keong, Chief Executive of EMA, said: "Singapore’s need for flexibility in the power system is growing. We would like to partner companies to turn promising ideas into commercially viable energy storage solutions that can be deployed at scale. By doing so, we can strengthen power system reliability while making better use of every storage. Call for Industry Solutions EMA will work with the industry and relevant agencies to improve access to energy market information, review existing rules, and explore ways for ESS to support Singapore's electricity needs more effectively. EMA will also develop requirements for how ESS operate and enable them to be centrally controlled when needed, depending on their size and role in the power system. As part of this effort, EMA invites the industry to propose technologies, business models, and projects that can address power system needs and support wider ESS deployment. Feedback is also welcomed on existing rules, technical requirements, infrastructure constraints that may hinder ESS deployment, and how these could be addressed. To support continued collaboration, EMA is also seeking industry interest in forming an industry-led Energy Storage Workgroup to share experiences, develop practical solutions and address common barriers to ESS deployment.

artigo.texto: UTICA — The city of Utica Common Council extended its moratorium on the development of battery energy storage systems (BESS) for another 45 days at a Wednesday, Oct. 21 meeting, allowing the council to prepare its proposed BESS legislation for a vote. The city has a moratorium on battery storage projects, as it prepares legislation to place regulations on battery energy storage systems. There is currently a piece of legislation in the Committee of the Whole that would ban Tier 2 Battery Energy Storage Systems, which have an energy capacity of more than 600 kilowatt-hours, or have more than one storage battery technology in a room or enclosed area. Developer presentationRobert Woods, energy storage project developer with Nexamp, attended the pre-meeting conference to ask the council to consider allowing battery storage systems in industrial and industrial mixed-use zones, with clear safety requirements and careful review of each project. The energy developer hopes to propose a battery energy storage system (BESS) at 2007 Beech Grove Place. The street runs through a commercial/industrial area, parallel to the Dwyer Avenue and the Route 5S corridor and Bleecker Street. “Battery storage holds electricity and sends it back into the grid when demand is high, supporting a more reliable electrical system,” he said. “Think of a hot summer day, when AC units are all blowing at the same time. A charged battery can deliver electricity during those periods to help meet demand. Storage can also hold electricity generated by renewable resources for use later, essentially.” He said that in Utica, such projects could stimulate private investment in industrial properties at a small footprint. Safety needs to be central in discussions about BESS projects, Woods said, so residents deserve clear answers and firefighters need to have information, training and emergency response plans. “Developers have a responsibility to explain how each proposed project would address equipment safety, monitoring noise, setbacks, emergency access and eventually decommissioning at the end of the 25-year lifecycle,” Woods said. “We’re prepared to work with city staff and the fire department to explain our proposal, hear their concerns and identify what information they may need to evaluate each system.” He asked the council to create a path for review of proposed BESS projects, rather than to close the door on them altogether. Council discussion Councilor-at-large Samantha Colosimo-Testa asked how the proposed BESS would have a direct benefit on the city of Utica, if homes in Utica have not had previous issues with electricity. “It’s grid reliability. A five-megawatt system, which we’re proposing, would be about 20 megawatt hours, and that would be four hours of power for up to 1,000 homes, depending on various factors,” Woods said. Sixth Ward Councilor Joseph Betrus said that many of the proposed BESS projects would be in his district. While he is not necessarily in favor of them, he said he’d prefer a way to evaluate proposals on a case-by-case basis, rather than a blanket denial. Assistant Corporation Counsel Stephanie DiGiorgio had originally prepared legislation divided battery storage systems into two categories: tier 1, which is for small systems, and tier 2, which is for large systems. It allowed for the small systems, but required large systems to receive a special use permit. The legislation was later amended by Third Ward Councilor Joseph Betar to totally prohibit the large systems. DiGiorgio said that the longer a moratorium is extended, the more problematic it becomes. However, she advised that it be extended for a short period of time, so she can finish reviewing the amended legislation. “I’m taking a piece of legislation that was specifically targeted for one aspect, and it’s now being amended to address a totally different purpose for the most part,” she said. “When it was initially drafted, it was expected that we were going to allow these systems, and now it’s expected that it’s really going to prohibit them. Joe did a great job of cutting stuff up, but I have to go back and make sure that it actually makes sense.” Codes Commissioner Marques Phillips suggested creating a middle tier for commercial systems that would be over 60 kilowatt hours but below 600 kilowatt hours to allow for greater specificity. The council decided to pass a 45-day extension on the moratorium to allow the council and DiGiorgio to refine the legislation. This would extend it through the council’s Dec. 2 meeting. “If something is passed and we don’t love it, if 30 applications flood in, they have to be processed in what we passed, versus if we took the extra 45 days with the moratorium, tightened everything up, and then passed something, we’d then feel a lot more comfortable with it,” Betar said. “Then if any applications were submitted, we wouldn’t have to worry about, ‘Did we cover this? Did we cover that?’”

artigo.texto: CATL's Buyback Spree and Swap-Station Push Sit Beside a Slowing Profit Engine Published on 10/25/2026 at 02:52 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL shares climbed 7.8% in the latest session, riding a broad rebound across Chinese battery, EV and technology names. The move had nothing to do with fresh company-specific news. Instead, investors returned to growth stocks after a sharp selloff, with buying in growth-oriented exchange-traded funds adding fuel to the recovery, according to City News Service. That distinction matters. A friendlier tape can support a share price, but it doesn't erase the economic pressure building underneath the business. Real Money Behind the Bounce The rebound wasn't purely a sentiment story. Chinese sector coverage pointed to several catalysts behind the battery rally, including CATL's own share repurchases and a string of battery-swapping partnerships. The wider market also recovered, led by battery and other growth names. CATL bought back 3,488,600 A-shares on Wednesday for roughly RMB 800 million, followed by another 2,271,000 A-shares on Thursday for about RMB 499.9 million. That put the company in the market for its own stock on two consecutive trading days. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? The Numbers That Matter More For all the buyback firepower, the decisive gauge is profitability per unit. At Tuesday's earnings presentation, CATL said product mix and policy-related costs had weighed on margins. Management still flagged growth potential in global demand for power and storage batteries. Wednesday's figures laid out the tension. In the third quarter of 2026, CATL posted revenue of RMB 165,220.844 million and net profit attributable to shareholders of RMB 21,246.061 million. Revenue rose 58.58% year on year, while attributable net profit grew just 14.54%. Reuters reported Tuesday that this was the slowest profit growth in nearly two years and that it fell short of analyst expectations. Scale alone doesn't answer the investor question. What counts is how much additional earnings the expansion generates. Rising demand would be less convincing if higher costs or an unfavorable product mix ate up the benefit. Swapping Stations, Swapping Partners CATL is pursuing uses beyond its core battery business. A strategic agreement with BAIC, closed on Thursday, targets battery-swap services for one million vehicles. BAIC is to bring compatible models into the Choco-Swap network and support station build-out through its dealer network. The opportunity lies in pairing vehicle supply with infrastructure — compatible models and build-out support could make usage easier. The agreed target, though, is neither equivalent to vehicles already served nor to secured additional revenue. Heavy transport follows a similar playbook. Reuters reported Tuesday on the launch of the Tianxing II battery platform and plans to expand the Qiji battery-swap network. CATL is aiming for 900 stations in China by year-end and 2,000 by 2027. Partnerships are stacking up. On Wednesday, CATL and the Shaanxi Transportation Holding Group signed a strategic cooperation agreement covering electrification of commercial vehicles, battery-swap stations for heavy trucks, energy storage and highway charging infrastructure. Media reports said CATL, its Chocolate Swap unit and Huawei subsidiary Yinwang agreed Monday to link their systems technically, connecting Huawei's intelligent driving systems with CATL's swap ecosystem. The planned vehicle-to-station flow is designed to enable a battery swap in 99 seconds. The bull case requires these projects to unlock demand that CATL can serve profitably. That would give growth a broader base. A durable re-rating, however, would need the expansion to lift earnings quality rather than merely business volume. Costs, Competition and a Twelve-Month Slide The bear argument carries real weight: strong revenue growth is no shield against fading profitability. Reuters tied the weaker profit performance Tuesday to higher costs and competition, compounded by difficult conditions in the Chinese auto market, whose downturn had run for twelve months through September. CATL at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. A scenario where CATL expands without shareholders benefiting accordingly is conceivable. New network offerings could be strategically sound and still deliver no near-term relief on the bottom line. Better market sentiment would only paper over that conflict. Cash generation is another checkpoint. Operating cash flow for the first nine months came in at RMB 61,625.487 million, down 23.60% from the year-earlier period, according to Wednesday's figures. Cash flow doesn't explain every shift in the business, but it sharpens the picture on profit: a convincing operating improvement shouldn't show up only in revenue. The ability to generate funds from operations remains relevant to investors. The Year-End Station Target Is the Next Test As long as the broader market recovery holds, it could give CATL further support. A more durable advance would require costs and product mix to weigh less on earnings. If sentiment turns while profitability stays under pressure, the recent rebound would be especially vulnerable. The next concrete operational marker is the year-end station target for the Qiji network. Progress could underscore the company's execution power, though it would not yet prove higher profits. For investors, the link remains the key: infrastructure and demand must grow without economic quality falling behind. Ad CATL Stock: New Analysis - 25 October Fresh CATL information released. artigo.texto: Hoymiles, a global leader in module-level power electronics and energy storage, opened its REI Expo 2026 showcase with a new product launch and a comprehensive portfolio of solar and storage solutions. The company introduced its MiS 6-in-1 Microinverter to the Indian market and showcased solar and storage solutions for every scale of energy, from rooftops to the grid, at Hall 12, Booth B531, India Expo Mart. At Asia’s premier clean energy event, which brought together over 60,000 professionals from more than 70 countries, Hoymiles attracted strong interest from visitors, industry experts and potential partners, while also welcoming senior leadership from Hoymiles China. Since 2012, Hoymiles has worked to turn untamed natural power into energy that is open to all. In India, one of the world’s fastest-growing solar markets, that mission is more relevant than ever. One Portfolio, Every Scale of Energy At its booth, Hoymiles presented five solution families, demonstrating how rugged and reliable technology can serve homes, businesses and the grid: - Residential solar and storage: Smart, safe and easy-to-install systems that give homeowners greater control over the energy they generate and use. - Plug-in storage: Compact, ready-to-use batteries that simplify storage for new and existing solar users, supported by AI-powered energy management. - C&I solar and storage: Efficient, liquid-cooled commercial and industrial systems designed to reduce energy costs and keep businesses running. - Utility solar and storage: Large-scale solar and storage solutions designed to support grid reliability and meet the demands of utility projects. - PCS storage solutions: High-efficiency power conversion systems engineered to perform even under weak-grid conditions. New Launch: MiS 6-in-1 Microinverter, Built for Indian Rooftops Hoymiles introduced the MiS 6-in-1 Microinverter (MIS-3680-W) to the Indian market. A single unit supports one to six PV modules, allowing installers to design systems around rooftop configurations rather than inverter limitations. Key features of the new microinverter include: - Efficient generation: Two independent MPPTs support split and multi-orientation rooftops while limiting losses from partial shading. Each input accepts up to 2,200 W and 23 A, making the system compatible with 700 W+ modules. It also supports unbalanced layouts of 0–3 modules per input and offers an EU efficiency of 96.3%. - Stable and reliable performance: With IP67 protection, an operating temperature range of –40°C to +85°C and a wide AC voltage range of 160–295 V, the microinverter is designed for demanding conditions and variable grids. Over 1,000,000 hours of reliability testing, built-in AFCI arc-fault protection and a galvanically isolated topology further enhance safety. Low-voltage DC operation eliminates the need for long high-voltage strings on rooftops. - Simple and smart installation: The Flex-S3 plug-and-play cable system simplifies wiring. Bluetooth direct connectivity and Wi-Fi Mesh allow installers to commission one device and automatically synchronise the remaining devices through the S-Miles Installer App. The system also supports remote diagnostics, over-the-air upgrades and an AI assistant for technical support. - Local support: The microinverter comes with a 12-year standard warranty and is backed by an India-based technical support team. Amid India’s rapidly growing solar and storage market, Hoymiles showcased its technological leadership and localised service capabilities tailored to market requirements. Leveraging its position as the world’s top shipper of microinverters (excluding the U.S.) and a BloombergNEF Tier 1 global energy storage manufacturer, Hoymiles aims to support India’s clean energy transition with reliable, accessible and cost-effective solutions. Its latest innovations integrate solar generation, energy management and storage to maximise performance, efficiency and sustainability. To expand its presence in India, Hoymiles has partnered with leading distributors across different regions. Through these partnerships, the company is building a robust nationwide sales and service network to deliver timely, reliable and customer-focused support. One Team, One Vision: China Leadership Joins India Team The product launch was attended by Hoymiles Founder and CEO Dr. Yang Bo and Vice President Mr. Guy Rong, who joined the REI Expo 2026 exhibition alongside colleagues from China and India. Their participation highlighted the importance Hoymiles places on India as a long-term market and its commitment to working closely with local customers, installers and distributors. Hoymiles already has a presence across India’s rooftop solar market, with hundreds of megawatts of its systems powering homes, businesses and projects nationwide. The company’s team also travelled to 63 cities to meet customers and partners in person and better understand their requirements. Hoymiles remains committed to being a long-term partner in India’s renewable energy journey, working closely with distributors and industry stakeholders towards a cleaner, smarter and more sustainable energy future for all. artigo.texto: Carroll County supervisors will travel this week to Alabama, where they plan to visit a data center on a fact-finding mission related to a proposed development at the regional Wildwood Commerce Park. The development, code named “Project Lightning,” has not been moving at a lightning pace. This month, the county’s board of supervisors broke with its partners in the commerce park — Grayson County and Galax — when it voted against handing over the project’s final approval to a regional economic development authority. The unanimous Oct. 5 vote came about a month after Carroll board members passed an emergency zoning ordinance regulating large data centers in their county, where the Wildwood park is located off Interstate 77. It was unclear where in Alabama the supervisors and their guests are headed. The county’s administrative coordinator, Crystal Adams, said late last week that County Administrator Mike Watson is the only one with that information, and he was out of town at a conference. Messages to the board members were not returned. Local officials have said that the project, if approved, could deliver millions of dollars in tax revenue, sufficient to shore up flatlining budgets. Several citizens speaking in public comment sessions have said the data center could be a good thing, but many wanted to know more about what exactly would be coming, and Carroll County residents in particular were keen to maintain local control of decisions on an industrial park near their home. Grayson County supervisors in late September, and the Galax City Council in early October, voted in favor of amending their agreement with the Blue Ridge Crossroads Economic Development Authority, giving power over final decisions to the authority, whose board includes two members of each locality’s government. Now they’ll have to wait at least until Carroll County leaders visit Alabama. “I’m unsure of which direction they are going at this time,” Watson said in a phone call earlier in October. The final spot Site 1 is the last remaining parcel at Wildwood Commerce Park. The 75-acre plot in Carroll County is home to multiple abandoned mines whose presence has driven off potential suitors over the years. An engineering report obtained from the economic development authority via a Freedom of Information Act request showed 28 features, including pits, trenches and collapsed shafts near I-77. Mines in that area yielded copper, zinc, iron, arsenic and other materials, according to the report. Two of the abandoned mines were filled with trash, including tires, appliances and a toilet. “In fact, we felt for a long time that it would be extremely difficult to develop, and we thought it might be a throwaway site that would never be developed,” Grayson County Administrator Steve Boyer told his board of supervisors recently. Then “Project Lightning” came calling. Rumors and FOIA requests have flown, and in the recent government meetings, officials publicly addressed some of the transparency concerns. In a Sept. 29 special meeting of the Grayson County Board of Supervisors, Boyer said he expects an investment of more than $11 million over a three-year period to build a project that would employ at least 1,000 construction workers, then employ 200 people at about $85,000 a year once it’s finished. The facility’s closed-loop water recirculating system would require 25,000 gallons of water per day to cool its servers, Boyer said. That’s less than about 40,000 gallons that the two local golf courses average daily and the 85,000 gallons that recently closed yarn manufacturer Parkdale Mills, in Hillsville, used per day in Carroll County, Galax officials posted on the city’s Facebook page. The water would come from Public Service Authority pipes, with discharge processed through its wastewater system, the city posted. Project Lightning would pay for power transmission upgrades needed at the industrial site, and recent State Corporation Commission requirements should mitigate utility cost increases for the region’s citizens, the city posted. Boyer and Galax officials expect that after the site is complete, it would deliver about $1 billion in new tax revenue for Galax, Grayson and Carroll to divide evenly over the following 10 to 15 years — about $22 million each annually, if stretched over 15 years. That annual revenue would be about 40% of Carroll County’s $55.5 million fiscal year 2027 budget. It would be about two-thirds of Grayson County’s recent annual budgets of at least $30 million. Galax’s fiscal 2027 budget is $29.3 million. “With this future revenue, we can do a lot of things,” Boyer said, adding that he is “confident we’re working with the right company.” Boyer gave those details along with a pitch for the board to approve the amended agreement among the Blue Ridge Crossroads Economic Development Authority and the three localities. “Now this doesn’t guarantee anything,” Boyer said. Boyer told his board that all three localities’ signing the agreement was crucial for negotiations to “move forward,” with very limited options if they don’t. Revenue issues Without that windfall, Boyer told the supervisors and visitors to the Sept. 29 meeting streamed on YouTube that they would have to make tough choices on the county’s revenue, as no growth lies on the horizon otherwise. “The only way for us to grow at this point is to tax our citizens or cut services,” Boyer said. “The board can raise real estate tax or property tax. We just don’t have revenues coming in, and the revenues are flat, and your costs are going up. Everybody understands what diesel … costs now. It’s just getting really expensive. Our healthcare costs just went up another half million dollars. “But where the board is, if we don’t increase revenue, we’ll be looking at cutting things like the sheriff’s office, parks and rec, library, trash service, and the money we provide, $1.7 million to the volunteer agencies, volunteer fire and volunteer EMS.
