artigo.texto: A HiTHIUM pretende fornecer mais de 33% da capacidade concedida no primeiro leilão de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS) do Brasil. Para atingir esse objetivo, a empresa trabalha há mais de um ano com parceiros de integração locais para adaptar sua oferta às exigências de conteúdo local do mercado brasileiro. A medida surge em meio a uma concorrência crescente, com 6.091 projetos registrados, totalizando 296.807 MW de interesse , segundo dados da Energy Research Company (EPE). Embora esse volume não represente a capacidade que será efetivamente contratada, ele demonstra a magnitude da oferta potencial em comparação com as licitações iniciais. “O Brasil apresenta um desafio diferente porque o conteúdo local é fundamental no primeiro leilão de dezembro. Estamos trabalhando com parceiros de integração locais há mais de um ano e nosso objetivo é capturar mais de um terço (33%) da capacidade leiloada no Brasil”, afirmou Alejandro Nahuel Angeli, Gerente Sênior de Desenvolvimento de Negócios para a América Latina da HiTHIUM , durante entrevista no programa de streaming “It Had to Be Said and It Was Said”, da Energía Estratégica. A estratégia de negócios da empresa envolve combinar sua capacidade de produção na China com a participação de atores brasileiros na integração dos sistemas, aspecto que se torna relevante dadas as condições regulatórias previstas para a contratação de armazenagem. Em particular, o Brasil está avançando com duas modalidades diferentes: LRCAP 2026 - Armazenamento Nacional , voltada para projetos com equipamentos que atendam aos requisitos de conteúdo nacional, e LRCAP 2026 - Armazenamento , destinada a contratar nova capacidade nas demais condições estabelecidas. Ambos os mecanismos fazem parte das diretrizes promovidas pelo Ministério de Minas e Energia para fortalecer a confiabilidade do Sistema Nacional Interligado e promover o desenvolvimento de uma cadeia produtiva ligada ao armazenamento. Nesse cenário, a participação do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES) na acreditação de equipamentos também introduz uma variável para os fabricantes, devido às condições de acesso aos incentivos associados à produção local. Portanto, os acordos com integradores nacionais são um componente central da preparação da HiTHIUM. No entanto, a empresa ainda não especificou quais processos serão realizados no Brasil nem qual será o percentual de conteúdo local em suas soluções. A combinação da demanda projetada, das condições de contratação e das exigências industriais cria o cenário em que a empresa pretende alcançar uma participação de mercado superior a um terço do mercado licitado. Fabricação própria e novas demandas da China: o suporte industrial da HiTHIUM Além das alianças brasileiras, a empresa identifica suas próprias capacidades de fabricação como um diferencial em relação a outros fornecedores, especialmente em um contexto em que a China está pressionando por padrões de qualidade mais rigorosos para tecnologias de armazenamento . “A HiTHIUM é a segunda maior fabricante de sistemas de armazenamento de energia do mundo. No Chile, já vendemos mais de 6 GWh. Projetamos um crescimento de dois e até três dígitos na região nos próximos cinco anos”, afirmou Angeli. Segundo o representante regional, uma das principais diferenças competitivas dentro do setor reside na capacidade de produzir as células diretamente, em vez de depender exclusivamente de fornecedores externos para integrar os sistemas. “Existem poucas fábricas de células no mundo, a maioria delas na China. Algumas fabricam apenas as células, outras fabricam o contêiner CC, e os integradores compram células ou módulos para montar a solução com PCS (inversores) e EMS/BMS”, explicou o executivo. A cadeia de valor abrange tudo, desde a fabricação de células eletroquímicas até sua integração em contêineres de corrente contínua, sistemas de conversão de energia e plataformas de gerenciamento de energia e baterias. Nesse esquema, a capacidade de controlar diferentes etapas da produção representa um dos argumentos industriais com os quais a HiTHIUM busca competir em licitações na América Latina . “Nós abrangemos toda a cadeia: fabricamos a célula, o contêiner CC e oferecemos soluções CA integradas”, enfatizou Angeli. Essa integração vertical está ganhando maior relevância diante do endurecimento das exigências tecnológicas na China, o que, segundo o executivo, pode modificar as condições de concorrência entre fabricantes e integradores. Seguir leyendo “O governo chinês está estabelecendo padrões de qualidade mais elevados para as tecnologias de armazenamento de energia em baterias (BESS). Isso elevará o nível global e eliminará os integradores menores que não possuem capacidade de fabricação própria de células ou suporte a longo prazo”, alertou o executivo. Do ponto de vista da empresa, as novas normas podem favorecer fornecedores com capacidade de produção própria e que possam garantir suporte técnico durante todo o ciclo de vida dos projetos , enquanto integradores de menor escala enfrentariam maiores exigências. Esse processo constitui um segundo componente de sua estratégia no Brasil, onde as condições para o conteúdo local devem estar alinhadas com os requisitos de qualidade, segurança e suporte técnico exigidos pelos desenvolvedores. No entanto, o executivo não identifica regulamentações chinesas específicas nem um cronograma de implementação, portanto, o alcance dessas mudanças na concorrência internacional permanece sujeito à sua implementação. Serviço pós-venda e garantias: os fatores que a HiTHIUM considera decisivos para o BESS (Sistema de Armazenamento de Energia em Baterias). artigo.texto: Ashland Global Holdings Inc. Key supplier of rheology modifiers and dispersants According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Lithium Ion Battery Dispersant market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global lithium ion battery dispersant market is a critical enabler of gigafactory scaling and next-generation battery performance, with demand structurally tied to cell manufacturers' capital expenditure cycles and yield optimization imperatives. As the industry transitions to advanced cathode chemistries such as high-nickel NMC and LMFP, and anode materials including silicon and lithium metal, the dispersion challenges intensify, directly impacting cell energy density, cycle life, and safety. This report provides a comprehensive analysis of the market from 2026 to 2035, covering historical data from 2012 to 2025, and examines the market through deployment use cases, buyer environments, upstream input dependencies, qualification requirements, pricing architecture, and country capability differences. The market is characterized by a dual technology push towards water-based dispersant systems for sustainability and cost reasons, and specialized formulations for emerging solid-state battery electrode processing. Supply is constrained by specialized synthesis and purification capabilities, formulation intellectual property, and lengthy qualification cycles. The competitive landscape is bifurcating between diversified specialty chemical giants and focused battery material specialists. This study is designed for battery and storage manufacturers, power-electronics suppliers, system integrators, EPC partners, developers, utilities, investors, and strategic entrants seeking a clear view of deployment demand, technology positioning, manufacturing exposure, safety and qualification burden, project economics, and competitive structure. The baseline scenario for the lithium ion battery dispersant market anticipates robust growth through 2035, driven by the rapid expansion of global lithium-ion battery production capacity and the increasing complexity of electrode formulations. As cell manufacturers scale gigafactories to meet electric vehicle and stationary storage demand, the need for dispersants that enable higher slurry solid content, improved coating uniformity, and reduced drying energy becomes paramount. The market is expected to grow at a CAGR of 8.5% from 2026 to 2035, reaching a market index of 225 (2025=100). This growth is supported by the transition to high-nickel cathodes and silicon anodes, which require advanced dispersion solutions to overcome agglomeration and stability issues. Regionally, Asia-Pacific will maintain its dominance, accounting for over 70% of global demand, led by China's battery manufacturing ecosystem. North America and Europe are expected to witness faster growth rates as local gigafactory capacity comes online, supported by policy incentives and supply chain localization efforts. The competitive landscape will see intensified R&D activities focused on water-based and bio-based dispersants, driven by regulatory pressures such as the EU Battery Passport and restrictions on solvent use. Pricing power will reside with suppliers who can demonstrate measurable cost-in-use advantages and provide technical support for formulation co-development. The market is bifurcating between diversified chemical giants and specialized battery material firms, with strategic partnerships and long-term supply agreements becoming the norm. The electric vehicle segment is the largest and fastest-growing end-use sector for lithium ion battery dispersants, accounting for an estimated 55% of global demand in 2025. This dominance is driven by the massive scale of EV battery production and the industry's shift toward higher-energy-density chemistries. As automakers push for longer range and faster charging, cell manufacturers are adopting high-nickel NMC cathodes (e.g., NMC 811) and silicon-doped anodes, both of which require advanced dispersants to maintain slurry stability and electrode uniformity. Dispersants enable higher solid content in slurries, reducing solvent usage and drying energy, which directly lowers production costs and environmental impact. The demand for dispersants in EVs is also supported by the need for consistent cell performance and safety, as agglomeration can lead to hotspots and premature failure. Through 2035, the EV segment will continue to dominate, with demand growth fueled by the expansion of gigafactories in Asia, Europe, and North America. Key demand-side indicators include EV sales volumes, battery pack sizes, and the adoption rate of high-nickel and silicon anode technologies. Major companies in this segment include Tesla, Volkswagen, BYD, LG Energy Solution, and CATL. Current trend: Growing rapidly, driven by global EV adoption and government mandates. Major trends: Shift to high-nickel NMC cathodes (811 and beyond) requiring specialized dispersants, Increasing use of silicon-based anodes to boost energy density, Adoption of water-based dispersant systems to reduce solvent emissions and costs, Rising demand for dispersants that enable higher slurry solid content and faster drying, and Growing focus on dispersant formulations that improve cycle life and safety. Representative participants: Tesla, Volkswagen, BYD, LG Energy Solution, CATL, and Samsung SDI. The stationary energy storage segment, including utility-scale, commercial, and residential applications, represents approximately 20% of global dispersant demand. This sector is growing steadily as renewable energy penetration increases and grid operators seek flexibility and reliability. Stationary storage batteries often prioritize cycle life, safety, and cost over energy density, but the trend toward larger cells and higher-voltage systems is driving demand for advanced dispersants.

artigo.texto: Chennai: The Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation (TNPDCL) has received regulatory approval to procure 600MW of solar power backed by a battery energy storage system for 25 years at a tariff of â¹3.12 per unit. This is expected to help meet the stateâs growing electricity demand and reducing dependence on expensive short-term power purchases. The Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission (TNERC) approved the procurement from the Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI). A trading margin of â¹0.07 per unit will be payable to SECI over and above the discovered tariff. The arrangement includes a 300MW battery energy storage system with a capacity of 1,800MWh. While TNPDCL will receive 600MW of solar power during solar-generation hours, the storage system will supply 300MW for six selected hours during the evening and early-morning peak window, between 6pm and 9am the following day. The project is expected to be commissioned within 24 months of the effective date of the power purchase agreement. The utility said long-term procurement at a discovered tariff would help reduce exposure to volatile prices in short-term electricity markets, improve grid stability and support compliance with renewable purchase obligations.

artigo.texto: Greater Noida: Solaryaan, a clean energy solutions brand of HowD Innovations Pvt. Ltd., is showcasing its hybrid inverters and battery storage solutions at Renewable Energy India (REI) Expo 2026, held from October 22 to 24 in Greater Noida. The company aims to help households, businesses and industries reduce dependence on grid electricity through integrated solar power and energy storage solutions. Gujarat Manufacturing Expansion Solaryaan is planning a 2 lakh sq. ft. manufacturing facility in Kadi, Gujarat, targeting 5 GWh battery manufacturing capacity in the next financial year. The first phase will include 1.2 GWh lithium-ion battery capacity and 2 GW inverter manufacturing capacity. The expansion forms part of its Solaryaan 2.0 strategy, aimed at transforming the company into an integrated clean energy solutions provider. New Hybrid Inverters And Battery Solutions A major attraction at the expo is Solaryaan's All-in-One (AIO) system, combining hybrid inverters and lithium-ion battery storage. The system offers hybrid inverters ranging from 3 kW to 10 kW, alongside 10 kWh battery storage, enabling households to store solar electricity for later use. For commercial and industrial customers, Solaryaan is showcasing its 125 kW/241 kWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), designed for peak demand management, backup power and solar energy storage. Its wider portfolio includes HV6 and HV12 batteries and DM-series configurations, offering scalable storage capacities between 241.05 kWh and 7.23 MWh. Focus On Energy Independence Manoj Patel, Founder and CMD of Solaryaan, said hybrid technology and battery storage are essential for making energy independence practical. He emphasised developing solutions suited to Indian weather conditions and different customer requirements. Shalin Botadra, JMD and Co-Founder, said the proposed manufacturing expansion would strengthen domestic clean energy capabilities under Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat. Expanding Distribution Network Solaryaan currently operates a partner network across 13 Indian states, supporting product availability, installation and after-sales services. CEO Chirag Patel said regular training programmes and stronger local support would help customers adopt integrated clean energy solutions. The company is displaying its products at Stall C-259, Hall 14, India Expo Centre & Mart, Greater Noida, until October 24.

artigo.texto: Russia’s Digital Development Ministry proposes placing strategically important data centers underground or in bunkers Russia’s Digital Development Ministry has approved recommendations for protecting data centers from drone attacks and other aerial threats, the Russian business daily Kommersant reported, citing a document it had reviewed. The ministry wants to divide critical data centers into three categories based on the consequences a potential attack could cause. The first category, K1, covers strategic facilities whose damage could disrupt key government functions for an hour or more. Security requirements will vary by category. For strategic facilities, the recommendations call for underground or bunker placement, Kommersant reported. The recommendations also call for reducing data centers’ visibility from the air, combining “physical reinforcement” with electronic warfare equipment and systems to counter aerial threats. The recommendations, which Kommersant reviewed, apply to data centers in Russia that are being designed, built, or already operating, regardless of ownership or operator. In October, Ukraine began striking similar facilities in Russia in response to Russian military strikes on data centers in Kyiv. Within a week, Ukrainian strikes hit three of the six data centers belonging to Yandex, in Sasovo in the Ryazan region, in Kaluga, and in Vladimir. Ukraine then struck a data center belonging to Sberbank in the Saratov region. IT market sources cited by Kommersant estimated that replacing equipment knocked out by the Ukrainian strikes on Yandex’s data centers will take up to six months. artigo.texto: SK Nexilis Develops Carbon-Coated Copper Foil for High-Silicon Anode Batteries, Targets 2027 Commercialization Published: Oct 23, 2026 18:27 (GMT+8) Share Share Save SK Nexilis, a battery copper foil enterprise under South Korea's SKC, announced on October 20 that it has developed a carbon-coated copper foil for next-generation high-silicon anode lithium-ion batteries: by applying a specialized carbon coating to the copper foil surface, it enhances the adhesion between the copper foil and silicon anode materials, suppresses the delamination of the anode coating caused by the expansion of silicon materials during charge and discharge, and improves electrode stability and battery life. The product is also compatible with dry electrode processes, which eliminate solvent coating and drying steps, thereby reducing battery production costs and energy consumption, but impose higher requirements on the adhesion between the electrode and the current collector. The company plans to build a pilot production line to verify process stability, targeting commercialization in H2 2027, with capacity and investment amounts not yet disclosed. The global stationary lead acid battery storage market is a mature, value-driven segment that remains structurally anchored in critical backup power applications, particularly telecommunications and legacy uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems. Despite intensifying competition from lithium-ion chemistries in high-cycle grid-scale projects, lead-acid technology retains durable economic advantages in CapEx-sensitive, long-duration, and less operationally intensive deployments. The market is forecast to expand at a modest compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 2.1% from 2026 to 2035, reaching a market index of 123 (2025=100) by the end of the forecast period. This growth is primarily supported by ongoing network expansion and resilience investments in developing economies, where low upfront capital expenditure and proven reliability outweigh higher maintenance burdens. The supply chain's profitability is intrinsically tied to the closed-loop lead recycling economy, with volatility in recycled lead prices and environmental constraints on smelting representing primary supply bottlenecks. Competitive intensity is bifurcated between large-scale, low-margin volume production for standard modules and higher-margin, engineered solutions for complex system integration. Value capture is migrating to system-level integration, specialized battery management systems for longevity, and service/warranty packages that mitigate the technology's higher operational maintenance and replacement cycle burdens. The regulatory environment is a double-edged sword: stringent recycling and extended producer responsibility laws reinforce the circular economy advantage but add compliance cost, while evolving fire codes and grid standards increasingly favor lithium-ion's footprint and performance characteristics in new installations. The long-term outlook to 2035 is one of managed decline in share but resilient absolute demand in core niches, with market leaders optimizing for circularity, developing carbon-enhanced products for renewable cycling, and forming strategic alliances to embed lead-acid as a component within broader hybrid storage solutions. The baseline scenario for the stationary lead acid battery storage market from 2026 to 2035 anticipates resilient absolute demand despite a gradual erosion of market share to lithium-ion technologies. The market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 2.1%, with the market index rising from 100 in 2025 to 123 by 2035. This outlook is underpinned by the technology's entrenched position in telecommunications backup power, where proven reliability, safety, and high surge-current capability create significant switching costs and qualification burdens for alternatives. Additionally, growth in renewable energy integration and off-grid systems in developing economies provides a secondary demand pillar, driven by low upfront capital expenditure and suitability for long-duration, partial state-of-charge cycling. The supply side is characterized by a bifurcated competitive landscape: large-scale, low-margin volume production for standard modules versus higher-margin, engineered solutions for complex system integration. Profitability is closely tied to the closed-loop lead recycling economy, with recycled lead price volatility and environmental constraints on smelting acting as primary supply bottlenecks. Pricing power is constrained by the commoditized nature of the core electrochemistry, pushing value capture toward system-level integration, specialized battery management systems, and service/warranty packages. The regulatory environment presents both opportunities and challenges, with stringent recycling and extended producer responsibility laws reinforcing the circular economy advantage but adding compliance costs, while evolving fire codes and grid standards increasingly favor lithium-ion in new installations. Overall, the market is expected to experience managed decline in share but resilient absolute demand in core niches, with leaders focusing on circularity, carbon-enhanced products, and hybrid storage solutions. Telecommunications backup power remains the largest and most resilient end-use sector for stationary lead acid battery storage, accounting for approximately 35% of global demand. The segment is structurally anchored in the need for reliable, high-surge-current backup power at cell towers, switching centers, and remote network nodes, where grid instability or outages can disrupt critical connectivity. Lead-acid batteries are favored due to their proven reliability, safety, and low upfront cost, despite higher maintenance requirements. Through 2035, demand is expected to be supported by the expansion of mobile networks in developing economies across Asia-Pacific, Africa, and Latin America, where reliable grid power is often unavailable. The rollout of 5G infrastructure may create incremental demand for upgraded backup systems, though lithium-ion competition is intensifying in higher-value installations. Demand-side indicators to watch include telecom capital expenditure trends, mobile subscriber growth, and network uptime regulations. The replacement cycle for existing lead-acid batteries, typically every 3-5 years, provides a steady baseline of demand. Major companies supplying this segment include Clarios, EnerSys, and GS Yuasa, which offer specialized telecom battery solutions with enhanced cycling performance. artigo.texto: Data center do Google em New Albany, na região central de Ohio (EUA) — Foto: Divulgação/Google O Google anunciou nesta quarta (22) que vai pagar a moradores e empresas nos Estados Unidos que reduzirem o consumo de energia elétrica. O objetivo é destinar a energia economizada a seus data centers de inteligência artificial. A iniciativa será realizada em parceria com a Voltus, empresa de recursos energéticos distribuídos. Ela vai disponibilizar ao Google até 1.070 megawatts de capacidade elétrica quando a companhia precisar. Segundo o jornal The New York Times, essa capacidade equivale à de um reator nuclear. Esse modelo de negócio é conhecido como usina elétrica virtual (VPP, na sigla em inglês). Em vez de concentrar a produção em uma única usina, o sistema coordena recursos espalhados por diferentes locais, reunindo residências e empresas que podem reduzir o consumo de eletricidade da rede ou usar a energia que geram. Quando acionados, os participantes recebem incentivos financeiros. Segundo a Voltus, os benefícios incluem economia nas contas e pagamentos diretos, transformando a demanda do Google por capacidade elétrica em ganhos econômicos para os clientes. A Voltus também recomenda o uso de termostatos inteligentes, que podem ajustar, por exemplo, o tempo em que um ar-condicionado permanece ligado. Nesses casos, a redução do consumo ocorre automaticamente. Os valores que serão pagos, no entanto, não foram divulgados.

artigo.texto: The Cap Times is an independent newsroom serving Madison and Wisconsin. Sign up for the Morning Update to receive news in your inbox each morning. As employees and students grapple with questions around artificial intelligence, the University of Wisconsin-Madison has decided to work with a Milwaukee company for some of its data center needs. For years, the university has previously relied on two data center services to host research and administrative computing for campus, according to Rob Cramer, UW-Madison’s top financial official. One is run by the state Department of Administration, and the other is run by a private company, US Signal. With UW-Madison’s contract with US Signal scheduled to end in early 2029, Cramer recently told the UW system’s Board of Regents, the university began looking for a replacement provider. After a bid process, UW-Madison selected Milwaukee-based Data Holdings. “This will provide us with a long-term solution that will both meet research computing needs and provide, basically, a backup for our administrative computing,” Cramer told the Board of Regents this summer. “It increases our capacity and it also moves us forward with respect to some of the higher demands of current research computing, including liquid cooling of the equipment.” The switch will also improve the university’s ability to secure new grants and contracts, according to the board’s meeting materials. Board of Regents members approved the switch in August. The transition will cost about $17 million and be funded by UW-Madison. Cramer estimated the total cost over the next decade will be about $60 million. Data Holdings is owned by the Forest County Potawatomi Community tribe in northern Wisconsin, as a subsidiary company of Potawatomi Ventures. The company’s customers include government, healthcare, hospitality and other organizations, according to Ryan Brooks, Data Holdings’ chief technology officer and general manager. “The Tribe's long-term perspective and commitment to responsible and sustainable investment helped shape the development of Data Holdings from the beginning and continues to influence how we operate and grow today,” Brooks told the Cap Times in an email. Increased development of data centers and how to regulate the facilities has prompted debate in communities across Wisconsin and the nation, and percolated in the state’s fall elections, including in the gubernatorial race. Data Holdings opened a two-story, 46,000-square-foot facility in Milwaukee in 2013. The scale of the building pales in comparison to some larger proposed data centers in Wisconsin, such as Meta’s facility in Beaver Dam, which is expected to span more than 500 acres. At a campus meeting this month, faculty leaders asked interim Chancellor Eric Wilcots where the university stood on data centers. “We're not going to take a position on large data centers across the state. That is not our place,” Wilcots said. “Can we inform the debate and the discussion? Absolutely. … Because we have experts who think about energy policy. We have experts who think about fresh water. … We have experts who think about the role of people in government.” In addition to contracts with data center providers, UW-Madison operates its own data centers on campus for specific research and administrative needs, said Greg Bump, a university spokesperson. “There are small facilities within the Computer Sciences and Statistics building serving the Division of Information Technology, College of Computing and Artificial Intelligence, Wisconsin Public Radio, and others,” Bump said in an email to the Cap Times. “Across the street, the Atmospheric, Oceanic and Space Sciences building has its own small data center serving the department and processing satellite data and creating weather models used all over the world.” Data centers can vary in scale, from the size of a closet to the size of a warehouse, according to Kyle Cranmer, a physics professor and director of UW-Madison’s Data Science Institute. Some research projects at the university collect lots of data, he said. It may make sense to store and process the data locally, out of convenience and to allow more local control. Depending on the need, though, it may be more cost effective and energy efficient to centralize resources at a data center, he said. UW-Madison has been working to scale up its artificial intelligence-related research, such as through its RISE-AI initiative and new College of Computing and Artificial Intelligence. “AI is not just about chatbots, like ChatGPT,” Cranmer said. “There's lots of other kinds of artificial intelligence that ... can be more relevant for science problems.” For instance, researchers are working to find ways to remove toxic “forever chemicals” known as PFAS from water, he said, and to make society more resilient to convective storms that produce tornadoes and hail. Generally, Cranmer added, “AI is definitely driving a lot of the increase in demand for data centers,” but not all AI requires big data centers. UW-Madison administrators designated 2026 as the university’s “Year of AI Readiness and Competency.” Members of a working group have wrestled with questions about how to think about and use AI on campus, Wilcots said. “What kind of guidance can we give to instructors? But also how we're going to think about using it administratively,” he said. “Because there's a lot of things I think in the AI space where we will be using it. We are using it. But we've got to think about how to do that carefully. We've got to think about issues of data privacy. We've got to think about issues of … ethics and philosophy.” With committees and groups tasked with working on AI across campus, “there is often a starting point … that assumes that moving forward robustly with AI is evidently going to occur, and the question is kind of how and to what effect,” said Nancy Kendall, a professor of educational policy studies at UW-Madison. “I think it is very much the wrong s

A iniciativa será realizada em parceria com uma empresa de recursos energéticos distribuídos, que poderá disponibilizar uma capacidade elétrica equivalente a de um reator nuclear. Conhecido como usina elétrica virtual, o modelo possui um sistema que busca coordenar recursos espalhados por locais diferentes, reunindo empresas e residências que podem reduzir o consumo de eletricidade da rede ou usar a energia que geram, sem precisar concentrar toda a produção de energia em uma única usina. artigo.texto: NEW DELHI: India needs to expand battery storage and grid infrastructure alongside renewable energy capacity to ensure reliable power supply as it moves towards its target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, experts said at an industry event. The country has crossed 300 GW of installed non-fossil fuel capacity, but integrating more renewable power into the grid will require investment in energy storage, domestic manufacturing and research, said Jai Asundi, executive director of the Centre for Study of Science, Technology and Policy (CSTEP). The discussions took place at the Renewable Energy India Expo, held alongside The Battery Show India and the Energy Storage Summit India in Greater Noida. Yogesh Mudras, managing director of Informa Markets in India, said renewable energy generation and grid storage must expand together as Indiaâs clean energy market grows. âWe have reached an execution phase where generation and grid storage must scale in tandem,â he said, adding that Indiaâs renewable energy market was projected to reach 486 GW by 2030, while its battery storage sector was expected to cross $8.5 billion by 2031. Anandi Iyer, director of the Fraunhofer Office in India, said the world added around 800 GW of renewable energy capacity in 2025, while global battery storage deployment reached 108 GW, up 40% from the previous year. She said India and Germany could work together in battery research, power electronics and advanced engineering. Australiaâs high commissioner to India, Philip Green, said the two countries could combine Australiaâs critical mineral resources and solar technology with Indiaâs manufacturing capabilities to strengthen clean energy supply chains. Australia produces more than half of the worldâs lithium, he said. Scotland First Minister John Swinney said Scottish expertise and innovation could complement Indiaâs manufacturing scale and market potential to support the clean energy transition. Manu Srivastav, additional chief secretary in Madhya Pradeshâs power and renewable energy department, said falling technology costs and economies of scale were making renewable energy increasingly competitive with conventional power. The three-day event, which opened on Thursday, has over 1,080 exhibitors and 1,400 brands, with participation from more than 10 countries.

artigo.texto: Procura por armazenamento de energia cresce 48% nos últimos 12 meses, com mais de 50 mil pesquisas relacionadas no Google O interesse por soluções de armazenamento de eletricidade vem se intensificando no país. De acordo com levantamento da Descarbonize Soluções, energytech especializada em energia solar e transição energética, nos últimos 12 meses, mais de 50 mil consultas relacionadas ao tema foram registradas no Google, representando uma alta anual de 48%. Nesse cenário, os Sistemas de Armazenamento em Baterias (BESS, na sigla em inglês para Battery Energy Storage System) se destacaram com a maior expansão, ultrapassando 104 mil procuras e avanço de 120%. Por outro lado, as baterias estacionárias mantêm a liderança em volume total entre as tecnologias analisadas, acumulando 248 mil pesquisas. Fatores econômicos vêm impulsionando o segmento. Segundo a Agência Nacional de Energia Elétrica (ANEEL), os primeiros leilões voltados ao armazenamento no Brasil entraram em consulta pública, com licitações previstas para 2 e 4 de dezembro de 2026. Além disso, o custo dessas estruturas se tornou inferior ao das usinas termelétricas a gás pela primeira vez. Dados da BloombergNEF apontam que, desde 2022, os investimentos em instalações de porte utilitário caíram mais de 50%, com retração de 27% apenas no último ano. O movimento expressivo evidencia a busca dos brasileiros por autonomia e segurança energética, minimizando a dependência da rede de distribuição tradicional. Além disso, o cenário é de que, cada vez mais, grandes empresas e setores, como o do agronegócio, adotem a tecnologia das baterias de armazenamento não apenas como forma de auto suficiência energética, mas também buscando economia, controle e segurança operacional. Baterias estacionárias lideram em volume, mas BESS registram maior aceleração no período Entre os equipamentos mais procurados, as baterias estacionárias figuram no topo, por trás de 248 mil buscas online e alta de 22% no último ano. Em seguida, destacam-se “bateria para energia solar” (69 mil pesquisas, +22%), “kit energia solar” (61 mil consultas, +22%) e “kit energia solar off-grid” (27 mil procuras, +53%). “O método de geração de energia por meio da luz solar está cada vez mais acessível e popular. Existe uma forte relação entre o interesse crescente por BESS e a consolidação das baterias estacionárias, visto que são soluções complementares para assegurar estabilidade e autossuficiência ao sistema”, explica Schaaffhausen. Os estados que mais buscaram Os estados com maior volume de pesquisas por “BESS” no último ano foram Santa Catarina, seguida pelo Distrito Federal e pelo Paraná. São Paulo aparece na quarta posição, enquanto Mato Grosso, Espírito Santo, Rio de Janeiro, Goiás, Rio Grande do Sul e Minas Gerais completam a lista dos dez estados com maior interesse pelo tema. O destaque catarinense ganha relevância diante dos investimentos na cadeia produtiva da tecnologia: em 2026, o BNDES aprovou R$280 milhões em financiamento para a construção de uma fábrica de sistemas de armazenamento de energia em baterias em Itajaí (SC). O movimento acompanha o avanço do armazenamento como alternativa para ampliar a flexibilidade do sistema elétrico e aproveitar melhor a energia gerada por fontes renováveis. Já o interesse concentrado em estados como Amapá e Roraima reflete a busca por estabilidade diante de vulnerabilidades históricas e a adaptação estrutural após a integração ao Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN), respectivamente. O Distrito Federal, por sua vez, acompanha de perto as discussões regulatórias e os leilões do setor, o que justifica a forte movimentação local. Metodologia Os dados utilizados na pesquisa foram levantados a partir da identificação das buscas no Google para os termos relacionados à “BESS”, “baterias de armazenamento” e “armazenamento de energia”. As buscas online correspondem ao período de setembro de 2025 a agosto de 2026, sendo os dados mais recentes disponibilizados pelas plataformas do Google no momento em que a pesquisa foi realizada. Para descobrir os estados brasileiros que mais buscaram por “BESS” e “armazenamento de energia”, foram analisadas as pesquisas no Google pelos termos e suas buscas relacionadas. Após a coleta dos volumes de busca, foi feita a proporção desses valores com o número de habitantes de cada estado, gerando rankings que garantem maior correspondência com a realidade. Sobre a Descarbonize Soluções A Descarbonize Soluções é uma empresa especializada que oferece um ecossistema completo e integrado para o setor de energia solar fotovoltaica. A empresa faz parte de um grupo com mais de 40 anos de história, e reúne três frentes estratégicas: a Aldo Solar, uma das maiores distribuidoras de equipamentos solares do país; a Sol Agora, fintech que oferece financiamento 100% digital para projetos de energia limpa; e a Descarbonize Serviços, especializada em assistência técnica e suporte ao cliente final. A Descarbonize Soluções tem presença em mais de 2.900 cidades brasileiras e conta com mais de 420 mil instalações realizadas. A Descarbonize Soluções faz parte do portfólio da Brookfield, uma das maiores empresas de gestão de ativos no mundo.

artigo.texto: Chevrolet Spark: pontos positivos e negativos do SUV elétrico da Chevrolet Crédito: Vinicius Montoia A Chevrolet decidiu dar um empurrão nas vendas do Spark EUV, o SUV elétrico de entrada da marca. A grande novidade é um corte de até R$ 5.800 no preço de tabela do modelo. Vendido por R$ 146.990 à vista, o desconto é exclusivo para unidades pintadas na cor Branco Cupuaçu e não exige veículo usado na troca. Para quem prefere apostar no financiamento, a fabricante também estruturou uma modalidade com taxa zero, exigindo entrada de R$ 88.990 complementada por 24 parcelas de R$ 2.530,66 — embora encargos operacionais e despesas adicionais acabem encarecendo a conta final a prazo. Com esse desconto, o SUV elétrico da Chevrolet fica mais barato que alguns rivais a combustão bem equipados, como Jeep Avenger Limited (R$ 147.990) e VW Tera High (R$ 147.190). Além disso, com o novo preço, o Spark EUV fica abaixo do BYD Dolphin GS, um dos seus principais rivais no segmento, vendido por R$ 149.990. Com o Chevrolet Spark mais barato e o crescimento do segmento de entrada, vale conferir a lista com os modelos elétricos mais acessíveis à venda no País. 5. Chevrolet Spark EUV - R$ 146.990 O Chevrolet Spark aposta em um visual quadrado inspirado em jipes clássicos, linhas retas e tampa do porta-malas com abertura lateral. Com medidas compactas pensadas para o uso urbano, o modelo ocupa a 5ª colocação entre os elétricos mais baratos do Brasil. Sob o capô, o SUV é equipado com um motor elétrico que entrega 102 cv de potência e 18,4 kgfm de torque. O conjunto é alimentado por uma bateria de 42 kWh, garantindo autonomia de 258 km pelo ciclo do Inmetro. Na recarga em corrente contínua de até 50 kW, o modelo vai de 30% a 80% em cerca de 35 minutos. O modelo sai de fábrica com central multimídia e painel digital de 10,1 e 8,8 polegadas, respectivamente, além de ar-condicionado digital, sensores de estacionamento dianteiros e traseiros e câmera de ré. O pacote de segurança é completo, trazendo seis airbags, controle de cruzeiro adaptativo (ACC), alerta de colisão frontal, frenagem automática de emergência e assistente de permanência em faixa. Vale, porém, uma ressalva nesta posição. Sem descontos, o 5º lugar seria do BYD Dolphin GS, vendido pela fabricante chinesa por R$ 149.990. O veículo utiliza uma bateria LFP de 44,9 kWh, assegurando autonomia oficial de 291 km aferida pelo Inmetro. No quesito desempenho, o propulsor elétrico entrega 95 cv de potência e 18,4 kgfm de torque, oferecendo respostas ágeis para o trânsito urbano. 4. GAC Aion UT - R$ 139.990 A GAC marca presença no segmento com o Aion UT, que vem crescendo no mercado nacional. O modelo busca conquistar espaço entre os elétricos de entrada com uma proposta diferenciada. O ponto alto está na motorização: o veículo é equipado com uma bateria LFP de 44,12 kWh, proporcionando alcance de 253 km pelo padrão Inmetro, além da entrega de 204 cv de potência e 21,4 kgfm de torque — bem acima dos seus concorrentes diretos. Para acomodar a bagagem dos ocupantes, o porta-malas oferece capacidade para até 340 litros, alinhando desempenho e utilidade no dia a dia. 3. MG4 Urban - R$ 129.990 Em sequência temos o MG4 Urban, mais especificamente na versão Comfort, que equilibra dimensões generosas, visual moderno e um conjunto mecânico encorpado. O propulsor desenvolve 150 cv de potência e 25,5 kgfm de torque. Alimentado por uma bateria de 43 kWh, o veículo atinge autonomia de 299 km segundo as medições oficiais do Inmetro. No quesito habitabilidade e transporte de cargas, o modelo se destaca com um espaçoso porta-malas de 382 litros, um dos maiores da categoria. 2. Geely EX2 - R$ 123.800 O Geely EX2 na versão Pro surge como uma opção versátil para quem deseja migrar para a mobilidade elétrica. O modelo aposta em soluções inteligentes de aproveitamento de espaço. O veículo utiliza uma bateria LFP de 39,4 kWh, oferecendo 289 km de autonomia pelo ciclo do Inmetro. Em termos de condução, entrega 116 cv de potência e 15,3 kgfm de torque, garantindo um rodar equilibrado na cidade. Um de seus maiores trunfos está no aproveitamento de espaço, com destaque para o entre-eixos de generosos 2,65 m de comprimento. Além disso, conta com porta-malas de 375 litros e um compartimento frontal adicional de 70 litros. 1. BYD Dolphin Mini - R$ 119.990 O título de carro elétrico mais acessível do País (e também mais vendido) segue firmemente nas mãos do subcompacto da BYD em sua versão de entrada GL. O modelo traz um motor elétrico de 75 cv de potência e 13,8 kgfm de torque. Sua bateria de 38 kWh assegura autonomia de 280 km pelo ciclo do Inmetro, ideal para a rotina diária sem preocupações constantes com recargas. Por conta de suas dimensões mais compactas voltadas à cidade, o espaço interno é mais restrito, refletido no porta-malas com capacidade para 230 litros. No entanto, a lista de equipamentos é boa: tela de instrumentos digital, central multimídia de 10,1” e diversos assistentes. Aliás, na China, o modelo acaba de ganhar uma nova geração maior, com mais equipamentos e acabamento superior. Carregando ofertas...

artigo.texto: LOGAN — Utah State University has completed the second phase of its campus solar expansion, adding more than 1 megawatt of solar generation capacity and its first large-scale battery storage system as part of an effort to reduce energy costs and the university's environmental impact. The latest installations bring USU's total new solar capacity to more than 2 megawatts across seven locations, with the combined systems expected to generate more than 3 million kilowatt-hours of electricity annually. The second phase includes two projects in Logan and one at the university's Uintah Basin Campus in Vernal. In Logan, a 317-kilowatt ground-mounted solar array has been installed at the Poisonous Plant Research Lab at 1150 East 1400 North, while a 239-kilowatt system has been added to the roof of the new Canyon Terrace parking structure along 400 North. The largest installation in the second phase is at the Uintah Basin Campus, where a 449-kilowatt ground-mounted solar array has been paired with a 500-kilowatt-hour battery storage system. The battery represents a significant addition to USU's renewable energy infrastructure, allowing the university to store electricity generated during daylight hours for use when needed. The Vernal project received financial support through Rocky Mountain Power's Blue Sky Program and Wattsmart Battery Program. Under the arrangement, a portion of the battery's capacity is reserved for Rocky Mountain Power to dispatch when needed, helping improve the reliability of the regional electrical grid. “Every kilowatt-hour we generate on our own campuses is one we don’t have to buy, and over the 25- to 30-year life of these systems, those savings add up,” said Zac Cook, associate director of utilities and energy management at USU. “Projects like this save the university money while reducing the environmental impact of our operations. Adding battery storage in Vernal helps us get even more value from that clean energy and gives us experience we can carry to future projects across the state.” The newly completed installations are expected to produce approximately 1.5 million kilowatt-hours of electricity annually, enough to power roughly 140 average Utah homes for a year. University officials estimate the second phase will also avoid more than 1,100 metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions annually, comparable to removing approximately 245 passenger vehicles from the road or avoiding the burning of about 1.1 million pounds of coal. The expansion follows the completion of the first phase earlier this year, which added 1,058 kilowatts of solar capacity. Together, the two phases represent a significant investment in USU's long-term energy infrastructure, with the systems expected to operate for 25 to 30 years. Beyond reducing electricity purchases, the projects will provide the university with practical experience in solar generation and battery storage technology that could help guide future energy investments at USU campuses throughout Utah.

artigo.texto: Huawei's foray into the battery swapping industry has made NIO absolutely thrilled. NIO is no longer the "lone warrior in battery swapping" at last. On October 19, Zhiyue signed a strategic cooperation agreement on smart battery swapping ecosystem with CATL and E-Car Service, where the three parties will connect vehicles, battery swapping stations and the cloud, to promote the synergy between Huawei Qiankun and CATL's Choco-Swap network. Two points are particularly emphasized in the cooperation: First, to create a "smart and non-inductive energy replenishment" experience, where vehicles will realize a full-process intelligent closed loop of autonomously judging energy replenishment demands, searching for stations, entering stations, aligning positions, completing 99-second full-automatic battery swapping, and driving away independently. Second, Zhiyue will officially join CATL's Choco-Swap ecosystem, and work with strategic partners to jointly expand the battery swapping energy replenishment ecosystem around the adaptation and access of cooperative models to CATL's Choco-Swap network. In simple terms, the cooperation essentially leverages Huawei's intelligent driving capabilities, and with the help of CATL's battery swapping network, the intelligent driving system will independently decide "whether to swap the battery" and "where to swap the battery", so as to realize the smart and non-inductive energy replenishment experience. On the premise that the technology is fully verified, the relevant brands under Zhiyue including the Jing series will further launch battery swapping models. It is rumored that CATL and Zhiyue are advancing the development of the first batch of five battery swapping models, which are scheduled to be launched in 2027. Coincidentally, on October 22, BAIC Group also officially announced that it has signed a "million-unit" battery swapping strategic cooperation agreement with CATL. According to the agreement, BAIC Group will promote the access of adapted models of its multiple brands to CATL's Choco-Swap ecosystem, and strive for the target of one million battery swapping vehicles. It is worth noting that BAIC Group will also open its dealer network resources, while CATL's Choco-Swap will accelerate the station deployment relying on dealer stores, and the two sides will jointly explore the joint operation model. Although the battery swapping models of Huawei and BAIC, as well as their specific launch time, have not been officially confirmed, this series of "alliances and collaborations" has indeed brought a new trend: in the pure electric vehicle market, flash charging and ultra-fast charging are not the only solutions, and battery swapping is gaining recognition from more industrial players. What NIO has been waiting for is not just Huawei's entry When talking about battery swapping, NIO is an unavoidable name. Since its establishment more than ten years ago, NIO has always taken its battery swapping system capability as its "moat". However, battery swapping is a capital-intensive business, which requires investment in construction, maintenance and battery reserve. If it only relies on its own vehicle models, the scale and utilization rate of the battery swapping network will eventually be limited by sales volume. Therefore, from the very beginning, NIO has hoped that more players will join the big family of battery swapping. From another perspective, on the same track of battery swapping, NIO's experience in battery swapping can also be transformed into real competitive advantages. In fact, since November 2023, NIO has reached battery swapping cooperation with Changan Automobile, Geely Holding Group, Chery Automobile, JAC Group, Lotus, GAC Group, FAW Group and other enterprises. However, these "cooperation frameworks" are far less significant than the cooperation finalized between NIO and Geely. On September 28, NIO and Geely Holding reached a comprehensive strategic cooperation in the field of charging and battery swapping. According to the agreement, Geely will take a stake in NIO Energy with the equity of Yiyi Internet and cash, holding 30% of the shares after the transaction is completed; Geely will develop consumer-oriented battery swapping models, with NIO Energy providing battery swapping services. The fact that multiple battery swapping cooperations have been reached in the industry in a short period of time is by no means "child's play", but indicates that in the mainstream passenger vehicle market in the future, battery swapping models will no longer be exclusive to NIO. Geely, Huawei's Jing series brand will all launch competitive products in this field. From a competitive perspective, NIO has more rivals now, which may affect the sales of its own products. But for NIO, its first-mover advantage in battery swapping is still solid. What's more, the completion of a battery swapping station does not mean that the battery swapping business is successful. The bigger "hurdle" lies in operation. A battery swapping station needs a sufficient number of vehicles in continuous use to spread the costs of equipment, site, battery reserve and operation personnel. Car owners hope to have more stations nearby, while operators hope to get more orders from each station. The two sides restrict each other, which makes battery swapping easily fall into a vicious circle: the network is not large enough for users to choose battery swapping; without enough users, the network cannot continue to expand. This is also the reason why NIO keeps looking for partners. However, it must be made clear that as more participants join the battery swapping industry, whether the energy replenishment networks can be interconnected and whether the standards can be compatible is still a practical problem to be solved. artigo.texto: Supercharging is getting faster and faster. Why are car manufacturers setting their sights on battery swapping? In China's new energy vehicle industry, battery swapping has long been a niche route, but now this solution has suddenly become the focus of major industry players. On October 19, 2026, Huawei HiChord, CATL and E-Chen New Energy signed the "Strategic Cooperation Agreement for Intelligent Energy Replenishment Ecosystem". The three parties will strengthen cooperation in swappable batteries and battery swapping networks, and work with ecosystem partners to jointly build an intelligent battery swapping ecosystem. In the future, battery-swapping models equipped with Huawei's intelligent driving solution will support autonomous battery swapping. On October 22, BAIC and CATL signed a comprehensive agreement to deepen cooperation in battery swapping business. Multiple brand-adapted models under BAIC will be connected to CATL's Chocolate Battery Swapping Ecosystem. The two sides will jointly build a nationwide, highly interconnected public energy replenishment infrastructure network in the future. The question that follows is: with the advancement of ultra-fast charging technology and the gradual popularization of ultra-fast charging stations, the charging time of new energy vehicles has been continuously shortened, and the gap in energy replenishment time between charging and battery swapping is also narrowing. Why are so many automakers ramping up their investment in battery swapping? Ultra-fast Charging is Speeding Up, and Battery Swapping is Gaining Momentum Although at the early stage of the birth of new energy vehicles, automakers represented by BAIC and NIO began to deploy battery swapping technology, this solution has never become the mainstream energy replenishment method. The reason is that due to the separation of batteries and vehicles, compared with fast charging technology, the operation chain involved in battery swapping solutions is more complex. On the one hand, automakers cannot "work behind closed doors" and need to carry out overall design for models, batteries and battery swapping stations. As battery technology evolves rapidly, batteries of various models and specifications emerge in an endless stream, and battery swapping solutions will limit the technological iteration of automakers to a certain extent. Source: NIO On the other hand, in the context where cross-brand compatibility and network sharing are not yet sufficient, automakers need to bear large investment in station construction and operation, and large-scale promotion also faces considerable pressure. More importantly, as ultra-fast charging technology matures gradually, the comparative advantage of battery swapping solutions in "fast energy replenishment" will be weakened. Source: BYD For example, in March 2026, BYD launched the second-generation Blade Battery and its flash charging technology, which can achieve 10%-70% charge in 5 minutes, 10%-97% full charge in 9 minutes, and only takes 3 minutes longer than at room temperature at minus 30℃ for 20%-97% charging. The following month, CATL released its third-generation Shenxing ultra-fast charging battery, which delivers equivalent 10C and peak 15C ultra-fast charging capabilities, taking only 6 minutes and 27 seconds to charge from 10% to 98%. Source: Li Auto In April 2023, Ma Donghui, President and Chief Engineer of Li Auto, explained why Li Auto chose ultra-fast charging instead of battery swapping. Because electricity has no physical boundary, but battery swapping requires replacing the entire PACK (battery pack), which has physical boundaries. At the same time, achieving compatibility between different models and different brands is a huge challenge, which does not conform to Li Auto's principle of prioritizing efficiency. Different from the fact that it is difficult to form an effective unified standard for battery swapping, Ma Donghui believes that the charging gun standard is easier to unify and become a public resource, so he "does not think battery swapping can perform better than ultra-fast charging in the promotion of passenger vehicles." All in all, the thresholds such as technical adaptation, station investment and cross-brand collaboration have prevented battery swapping from becoming the mainstream energy replenishment method. The development of ultra-fast charging technology will further weaken the comparative advantage of battery swapping. With brands such as Feifan and Ruilan fading out, only NIO still adheres to the battery swapping technology route in the consumer market before. Lowering Vehicle Purchase Threshold, Battery Rental Solution Has Become a Consensus Since 2026, the battery swapping solution has become increasingly popular, not because the battery swapping technology itself has made considerable progress, but because the market environment of China's new energy vehicles has undergone significant changes. Source: China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) Data disclosed by CPCA shows that in September 2026, the retail sales of passenger vehicles in China reached 1.618 million units, down 28.0% year on year. Among them, the retail sales of new energy vehicles decreased by 16.7% year on year, with a penetration rate of 67%, and the growth of penetration rate began to slow down. Against the background of sluggish retail performance in China's passenger vehicle market, new energy vehicles are also facing the challenge of poor sales. For automakers, in addition to continuing to attract fuel vehicle users, they also need to reduce the initial purchase cost to attract potential consumers who are still on the fence. Source: NIO Since the vehicle and battery can be separated, the battery swapping mode can significantly reduce the price of vehicles. artigo.texto: The follow-on deal, signed through its U.S. subsidiary Samsung SDI America, lifts the total volume contracted with AOP to 1.5 GWh after an initial order late last year. AOP will deploy the systems, due for delivery by year-end, at a large-scale Texas power project set to break ground next year. The order covers the Samsung Battery Box 1.7, an all-in-one unit built with high-nickel NCA cells at StarPlus Energy, Samsung SDI's Indiana joint venture with Stellantis. It packs 17 percent more energy density than its predecessor into the same 20-foot container and holds NFPA 855 and UL 9540 safety certifications. All three Korean battery makers are retooling U.S. electric vehicle lines for energy storage as EV demand cools, and Samsung SDI's turn has gathered pace this year. It landed a 1.5 trillion won ($1.13 billion) U.S. ESS order in March and agreed in August to buy General Motors' stake in their Indiana joint venture, with storage batteries the near-term priority. Samsung SDI says it is the only non-Chinese maker of prismatic ESS batteries in North America, a format it says outlasts pouch cells in durability and fire safety. The company is in talks with several other U.S. customers and expects further orders soon. "Alpha Omega Power is one of the fastest growing independent power producers in the country, and the kind of sophisticated operator we want to partner with to tackle grid reliability challenges," said Fabrice Hudry, executive vice president and head of the ESS team at Samsung SDI America. He said the company would widen its footing in North America through "differentiated technology and local production capabilities." AJP Takeaways - Samsung SDI said on Oct. 26, 2026 that its U.S. unit had signed a 1 GWh energy storage supply deal with Alpha Omega Power, bringing their total contracts to 1.5 GWh. - The SBB 1.7 units will be made at StarPlus Energy in Indiana, Samsung SDI's joint venture with Stellantis, for a Texas power project due to break ground in 2027. - The order follows Samsung SDI's 1.5 trillion won U.S. ESS deal in March 2026 and its August 2026 agreement to buy General Motors' stake in their Indiana battery joint venture. artigo.texto: Samsung SDI has secured a 1-gigawatt-hour energy storage system supply deal with US power developer Alpha Omega Power, bringing their combined contracts to 1.5 GWh as the Korean battery maker expands its North American business. The latest agreement, signed through Samsung SDI's Michigan-based subsidiary, follows an initial deal made last year, the company said Monday. The StarPlus Energy plant in Kokomo, Indiana, will produce the battery cells and modules, with deliveries scheduled by year-end. Samsung SDI will supply its Samsung Battery Box 1.7, an integrated ESS solution using high-nickel nickel-cobalt-aluminum prismatic batteries. The system offers 17 percent higher energy density than its predecessor, SBB 1.5, within the same 20-foot container. It also features AI-based monitoring to detect abnormalities and predict battery life. For fire protection, SBB 1.7 uses Samsung SDI's Enhanced Direct Injection technology, which delivers fire-extinguishing agents directly into battery modules. The company said the system complies with US fire safety standard NFPA 855 and holds UL 9540 certification. AOP plans to deploy the batteries at large-scale power projects in the western US and Texas, where construction is expected to begin next year. The projects aim to support grid reliability as electricity demand rises. "American-made ESS from Samsung SDI will play an important role in AOP's continued growth," said Alpha Omega Power CEO Paul Choi. "This second agreement strengthens our domestic supply chain supporting the next generation of energy infrastructure." Samsung SDI is seeking additional ESS contracts in North America, positioning its locally manufactured prismatic batteries as an alternative to Chinese suppliers. Fabrice Hudry, head of Samsung SDI America's ESS team, said the company plans to expand its regional business by leveraging its battery technology and US production capabilities. yejinlim@heraldcorp.com

K-Battery Production Ramp-Up Expected to Gain Momentum" Independent research firm Growth Research said on October 26 that domestic battery makers are stepping up production as the energy storage system (ESS) market expands amid the growth of artificial intelligence (AI) data centers and renewable energy. In a report released that day, Han Yonghee, a researcher at Growth Research, said, "New global battery ESS installations reached 108 GW in 2025, up 40% from the previous year, while new installations in the United States rose 60% to 19 GW. As demand for electricity storage grows amid the expansion of AI data centers and renewable energy, the average price of ESS battery packs has also fallen 45% from the previous year, lowering the cost barrier to adoption." Domestic battery makers are also increasing ESS production to meet rising demand. "LG Energy Solution plans to secure annual production capacity of more than 50 GWh for LFP batteries for ESS in North America by the end of 2026. Samsung SDI and SK On are also working to expand ESS supply through U.S. production and the conversion of existing facilities," Han said. "As customers increase their production, supply volumes of modules, thermal management components, and cooling systems used in batteries could also rise." Han named Sebang Battery, Shinsung ST, and Hanjung NCS as companies to watch, saying that increased ESS production by domestic battery makers and the expansion of local production in North America could lead to more orders for modules, components, and cooling systems. artigo.texto: Promover a produção com baixas emissões. Desde a transformação das técnicas agrícolas e a utilização de subprodutos agrícolas até a construção de marcas de produtos agrícolas de baixa emissão, as principais áreas agrícolas da província mantêm e desenvolvem práticas de agricultura circular, adaptando-se às mudanças climáticas, abrindo oportunidades para agregar valor aos produtos agrícolas, aumentar a competitividade e participar gradualmente do mercado de créditos de carbono. Na área de agricultura orgânica do bairro de Lang Biang, em Da Lat , a fazenda do Sr. Nguyen Thanh Hai reestruturou suas plantações, praticando a rotação de dezenas de tipos de frutas e verduras que, ao longo dos anos, têm sido consumidas pelo mercado, com aumento da produção e agregação de valor. Assim, em seus mais de 1,5 hectares de terra com certificação orgânica, o Sr. Hai organiza o plantio de diferentes hortaliças em áreas separadas, seguindo um cronograma de plantio contínuo. Ao final de cada ciclo de produção, ele trata o solo e passa a plantar tomates, acelga chinesa, espinafre, alface e dente-de-leão, antes de retornar ao plantio de pimentões. O espinafre tem um ciclo de cultivo de cerca de 35 a 40 dias; amaranto, couve-flor, aipo e brócolis são cultivados em rotação, de acordo com suas características de crescimento e as condições climáticas em diferentes épocas. Para obter a certificação orgânica no início de 2023, o Sr. Hai investiu amplamente em infraestrutura, melhoria do solo e ajustes nos processos agrícolas, incluindo um sistema de irrigação automatizado, áreas para mistura de esterco com subprodutos da colheita e a produção de pesticidas biológicos para o controle de pragas. “Os primeiros ciclos de cultivo enfrentaram dificuldades devido a problemas de saúde do solo após o uso prolongado de fertilizantes e pesticidas inorgânicos. Portanto, a transição geral para a agricultura de baixa emissão exige que os produtores equilibrem os nutrientes orgânicos, controlem pragas e doenças usando soluções biológicas integradas e mantenham um ecossistema agrícola estável, adequado às condições e características do solo”, compartilhou o Sr. Hai. Na comuna de Quang Lap, a fazenda orgânica Thien Sinh vem aprimorando e expandindo continuamente sua área de cultivo orgânico e criação de animais há quase 20 anos, atingindo 15 hectares. Isso inclui 10 hectares dedicados à rotação de culturas de hortaliças e frutas, produzindo de 1,5 a 2 toneladas de produtos por dia. Os 5 hectares restantes são destinados a forragem, currais, pastagens naturais para gado e porcos criados soltos, oficinas e armazenamento refrigerado para o processamento e conservação pós-colheita de hortaliças. Comparadas às hortaliças cultivadas convencionalmente, as hortaliças cultivadas organicamente rendem cerca de 70% mais, sendo vendidas a preços 2,5 a 3 vezes maiores. Além disso, a fazenda desenvolveu um rebanho de mais de 50 bovinos de alta produção e centenas de porcos híbridos, alimentados com ração processada localmente. Simultaneamente, utiliza materiais biológicos para cama dos animais, compostando-os com subprodutos agrícolas para criar fertilizante orgânico que fornece nutrientes para as hortaliças e frutas. O proprietário da fazenda, Nguyen Quoc Thang, disse: “A fazenda é inspecionada e avaliada regularmente por órgãos competentes para garantir a qualidade dos padrões orgânicos para vegetais, frutas e todo o processo de criação de animais. Como resultado, a fazenda recebeu a certificação orgânica pela terceira vez, válida até 2028. O mercado interno reconheceu os benefícios dos produtos agrícolas orgânicos e os consome muito rapidamente. O mercado internacional está fazendo grandes encomendas, então precisamos continuar investindo e expandindo a escala da agricultura e criação de animais com baixa emissão de carbono no futuro…” Promovendo o selo "Baixa Emissão" Estatísticas mostram que a província possui atualmente cerca de 110.700 hectares de produção agrícola de alta tecnologia. Desse total, cerca de 2.100 hectares são destinados à agricultura orgânica, com a meta de expansão para 11.200 hectares até 2030. Para 2050, a província almeja que 100% de suas principais culturas adotem técnicas de cultivo sustentáveis; estabelecer um banco de dados digitalizado conectado ao sistema nacional de monitoramento; e construir e popularizar gradualmente o selo de "Baixa Emissão" para produtos agrícolas, melhorando a eficiência no uso de recursos e a qualidade de vida da população. De acordo com o plano de ação do Comitê Popular Provincial até 2035, toda a província pretende reduzir as emissões totais de gases de efeito estufa da produção agrícola em pelo menos 15% em comparação com 2020; a taxa de resíduos agrícolas coletados e reutilizados na economia circular deverá atingir mais de 80%. A área de terras cultivadas aplicando padrões de produção sustentável e reduzindo as emissões deverá atingir mais de 30% da área total cultivada da província. Além disso, a província selecionará diversos modelos agrícolas com potencial para gerar créditos de carbono, atendendo aos requisitos de organizações internacionais. Para alcançar esses objetivos, o Comitê Popular Provincial orientou os departamentos e agências competentes a revisar a estrutura de produção e identificar áreas adequadas para a implementação de soluções de agricultura sustentável. Áreas de produção ineficientes estão sendo destinadas à conversão para o cultivo de culturas de alto valor econômico e baixa emissão, com potencial para geração de créditos de carbono, adequadas às condições ecológicas e às demandas do mercado.

artigo.texto: State Bank of Pakistan, WWF Turn Green Taxonomy Into Carbon-Intensity Checks for Textile SMEs - Toolkit launched: WWF-Pakistan and the State Bank of Pakistan released the SME Green Transition Toolkit for the Textile Sector. - Taxonomy in practice: The toolkit converts Pakistan’s Green Taxonomy into steps for assessing carbon intensity and energy efficiency. - Bank pilots next: Banks are expected to test the toolkit with textile clients, backed by further guidance and training. WWF-Pakistan and the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) have launched the SME Green Transition Toolkit for the Textile Sector. The toolkit aims to help financial institutions support textile small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in adopting cleaner, more resource-efficient practices. It translates Pakistan’s Green Taxonomy, a classification of green economic activities, into practical steps for lenders. WWF-Pakistan developed the toolkit with the SBP’s Small and Medium Enterprises (SME), Housing & Sustainable Finance Department. The steps cover assessing carbon intensity, or emissions per unit of output, and energy efficiency. They also cover identifying green technologies such as solar energy and waste heat recovery. Finally, the toolkit guides users in developing financeable transition plans, supported by an Excel-based tool. The textile sector contributes about 8.5% of Pakistan’s GDP and employs nearly 40% of its labour force. As sustainability requirements in international markets evolve, access to green finance is becoming more important for the sector’s competitiveness. By linking environmental performance with financing pathways, the initiative aims to help textile SMEs improve resource efficiency and competitiveness. It also aims to contribute to Pakistan’s broader climate and sustainable finance goals. RELATED ARTICLE: Deutsche Bank and WWF Team to Further Advance Sustainable Finance The launch brought together representatives from government, financial institutions and development partners. It also included a technical demonstration of the toolkit. Banks are expected to begin piloting it with textile clients, supported by further guidance and training. The SBP and WWF-Pakistan did not name the participating banks, a pilot timeline or the number of SMEs targeted. Who It Affects - Banks and financial institutions: Gain a Green Taxonomy-based method, with an Excel tool, to judge whether textile SME transition plans can be financed. - Textile SMEs: Borrowers seeking green finance from piloting banks face checks on carbon intensity and energy efficiency, and need financeable transition plans. - Green technology suppliers: Solar energy and waste heat recovery are named as technologies lenders can identify for textile SMEs to adopt. artigo.texto: Time- and Cost-Burdening SW Code Verification… 'AI Supervision Team' Emerges to Solve Inefficiency Kim Ki-seop, Professor in the Department of Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Information Technology at Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology (DGIST) Development of LLM-Based Software Development, Analysis, and Security Automation Technologies "Multiple AI Agents Simultaneously Review Code… Saving Time and Costs" Verification of software (SW) code generated by artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a new challenge. Whether written by humans or AI, deploying code to actual services without review can lead to errors and security incidents. The procedure to prevent this is 'code review,' which involves examining the functionality, quality, and security issues of the code. Because such code reviews also require significant time and cost, research into automating them with AI has continued. Most approaches have centered on a single AI reviewing the entire codebase. Kim Ki-seop, Professor in the Department of Electrical Engineering, Computer Science and Information Technology at Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology (DGIST), said, "It is like having a single building inspector check everything from design to finishing alone," adding that it is "inefficient in terms of time, cost, and other aspects." Professor Kim's research team created an 'AI Supervision Team' where multiple AIs with divided roles review code together. One AI verifies whether the code has been implemented according to the design, while another identifies security vulnerabilities. Yet another checks whether the team's established coding rules have been followed. However, as the number of AIs and items to review increases, errors may occur where the code review deviates from its original purpose. The AI agents continue conversations with each other, effectively forgetting the initial supervision objective. To prevent this, the research team added an AI called a 'QA (Quality Assurance) Checker' that oversees the entire supervision team. Its role is to correct course when there is a risk of the AI agents losing the direction of the code review. Professor Kim stated, "The core function of the QA Checker is to ensure that the AI code review team properly reaches its initial goal." Professor Kim's research team will directly introduce this technology at the '2026 K-Premier Deep Tech Festa' (Registration: https://vvd.bz/buvX), held on the 29th at COEX in Seoul. Professor Kim is also conducting research into examining the thinking processes of AI models. Just as stimulating specific areas of the human brain activates language or physical functions, this research aims to identify neurons within AI that handle specific functions. Professor Kim said, "I was curious whether there are separate neurons responsible for each language inside an AI, and if removing those parts would truly disable that language capability." Analysis results showed that removing neurons responsible for a specific language actually reduced the ability in that language. However, there were also cases where abilities in other languages declined simultaneously. Professor Kim explained, "If we only remove the neurons responsible for Japanese but Korean becomes clumsy as well, we must preserve the neurons among them that affect Korean," adding, "This way, we can accurately remove only the target to be deleted while using the remaining knowledge as before." The research team is also conducting studies on enhancing specific neurons to boost corresponding capabilities. This research connects to technology for erasing knowledge that AI has already learned. In December 2024, the Indian Publishers Association, with participation from Bloomsbury, the publisher of Harry Potter, filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, claiming that ChatGPT provided book summaries without permission. The publishers demanded that if license agreements would not be signed, the training data should be deleted. However, retraining an AI from scratch to erase already learned content costs tens of billions of won. Professor Kim is researching methods to store knowledge in easily erasable locations from the learning stage. Citing a classroom environment composed of multiple separate blackboards as an example, he said, "If we need to erase Harry Potter content, it would be like removing only the Harry Potter auxiliary blackboard," adding, "AI can be designed from the start to facilitate 'partial deletion.'" Professor Kim emphasized, "The technologies I am researching will fundamentally align with the concerns of most AI companies," stating, "I want to better understand the needs of domestic companies and provide directly applicable technologies, thereby contributing to our country's economic development." This is because the cathode material, which determines battery performance, does not match well with solid electrolytes.
