artigo.texto: CATL's Market Share Slips to 40.9% as Buybacks and Swap Deals Underpin a Sentiment-Led Bounce Published on 10/25/2026 at 08:10 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL shares climbed 7.8% on Friday, lifted by a broad recovery across Chinese and South Korean equities rather than by any fresh company announcement. Media accounts attributed the move to shifting trading flows and a rotation back into previously sold-off sectors, framing it as a mood-driven countermove following steep losses rather than confirmation of a fundamental turnaround. Battery-linked names and other growth sectors helped drive the afternoon rebound in China. Third-Quarter Profit Misses Expectations The rally follows a Tuesday earnings release in which CATL reported a third-quarter 2026 net profit of 21.2 billion yuan, up 14.5% year on year. According to Reuters, that marked the slowest earnings growth in nearly two years. Revenue for the same quarter rose 58.6% to 165.2 billion yuan, yet both the top and bottom lines fell short of analyst expectations, Reuters reported. Management pointed to product mix as well as consumption-tax and export-tax-rebate effects when explaining per-unit profitability. Reuters also noted that CATL's share of China's traction-battery installation market stood at 40.9% in September, down from 49.8% in January. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? Nine-Month Figures and Buyback Activity For the first nine months of 2026, CATL posted revenue of 442.14 billion RMB and a net profit of 64.53 billion RMB. Alongside those results, the company repurchased 3,488,600 A-shares on Wednesday for roughly 800 million RMB, according to its own disclosures, then added a further 2,271,000 A-shares on Thursday for about 499.9 million RMB — buying back stock on two consecutive trading days. A mandatory disclosure to the Hong Kong exchange put the Wednesday tranche at 3.49 million A-shares for around 800 million RMB. Battery-Swap Partnerships and Network Targets Chinese industry coverage tied the battery sector's recovery to several catalysts beyond the buybacks, including partnerships built around battery swapping. On Wednesday, CATL and the Shaanxi Transportation Holding Group signed a strategic cooperation agreement covering the electrification of commercial vehicles, battery-swap stations for heavy trucks, energy storage and charging infrastructure along highways — a collaboration spanning multiple corners of transport infrastructure. CATL, its Chocolate Swap unit and Huawei subsidiary Yinwang also agreed on Monday to link their systems technically, according to media reports. Huawei's intelligent-driving systems are to be connected with CATL's battery-swap ecosystem, with the planned vehicle-to-station workflow designed to complete a swap in 99 seconds. Reuters additionally reported on CATL's plans to expand its battery-swap network for heavy trucks. The company is targeting 900 stations in China by the end of the year, rising to 2,000 by 2027 — concrete build-out goals that sit alongside the newly signed cooperation agreements. artigo.texto: O ciclo de investimentos em inteligência artificial, a temporada de resultados do terceiro trimestre de 2026 e a entrada de capital estrangeiro na B3 dominaram a pauta de estrategistas na semana, segundo compilação do InfoMoney. Entre os pontos analisados estão as projeções da XP para o capex das oito maiores empresas americanas — que podem chegar a US$ 1,8 trilhão até o fim da década —, o papel dos fundos imobiliários na expansão dos data centers e o ingresso de R$ 10,1 bilhões de investidores externos no primeiro pregão depois do 1º turno. Capex de IA e o gargalo da execução A equipe de estratégia da XP avaliou os aportes de capital das companhias ligadas à inteligência artificial para identificar pressões operacionais, oportunidades e as teses de posicionamento mais defensáveis. O levantamento projeta que as oito principais empresas dos Estados Unidos concentrem US$ 1,8 trilhão em investimentos até o encerramento desta década, montante que redesenha as perspectivas do setor de tecnologia e exige leitura cuidadosa dos reflexos sobre as carteiras. A infraestrutura física exigida por essa corrida coloca os data centers no centro do ecossistema. artigo.texto: EMA seeks industry proposals to scale up energy storage Submissions are due by 29 January 2027. The Energy Market Authority (EMA) has launched a consultation paper, calling on the industry to propose technologies, business models, and projects for energy storage systems (ESS) that can be commercially deployed at scale. The development comes as Singapore aims to triple its energy storage capacity from about 350 megawatt-hours to around 1 gigawatt-hour by 2030. Electricity demand is expected to grow rapidly over the next few years, driven by new large loads such as semiconductors, data centres, and the electrification of the transport system, according to EMA. The ESS can respond quickly to fluctuations in solar generation and other supply disruptions to help maintain the power system’s stability. Electricity stored in ESS can also be released should there be high demand in some areas, reducing the strain on the electricity network. Smaller ESS in homes, businesses, and electric vehicles could be coordinated to collectively support the country’s power system, including through arrangements known as virtual power plants. “Singapore’s need for flexibility in the power system is growing,” said Puah Kok Keong, chief executive of EMA. “We would like to partner [with] companies to turn promising ideas into commercially viable energy storage solutions that can be deployed at scale,” he added. EMA said it will work with the industry and relevant agencies to improve access to energy market information and review existing rules. It will also develop requirements for how ESS operate and enable them to be centrally controlled when needed, depending on their size and role in the power system. The authority is also seeking industry interest in forming an industry-led energy storage workgroup to share experiences, develop practical solutions, and address common barriers to ESS deployment. The consultation paper is available on the EMA website, and parties are invited to submit their views and proposals by 29 January 2027 to [email protected].

artigo.texto: Greenvolt Power, part of Greenvolt Group, has agreed to divest two completed battery storage projects in north-eastern Poland, totalling 400MW/1.6GWh, to Malta-based investment vehicle A&R Investments. The assets comprise the stand-alone Ełk and Turośń Kościelna battery energy storage system (BESS) projects. Discover B2B Marketing That Performs Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms. Each project has 200MW of power capacity and 800MWh of energy storage capacity, allowing it to discharge at full power for approximately four hours. Greenvolt Power expects to complete the transaction by the end of 2026, provided all customary conditions are met. Financial details of the transaction were not disclosed. A&R Investments director Christian Buhagiar said: “These projects represent an important addition to our portfolio and an opportunity to invest in large-scale battery storage assets in Poland. “Their scale and role in providing flexibility to the electricity system make them valuable assets in a market where storage is becoming increasingly important.” The Ełk and Turośń BESS facilities were completed in the third quarter of 2026 and have secured the necessary permits for operation. The assets have each obtained 17-year capacity market contracts starting in 2028, under which they will receive fixed payments for making 85% of their rated capacity available to the national electricity system. Additionally, the facilities are supported by a ten-year tolling agreement designed to optimise battery operations and the trading of their flexibility in power markets. The BESS projects aim to provide additional flexibility to Poland’s electricity system, supporting the integration of renewable energy. The sale forms part of Greenvolt Power’s asset-rotation strategy, under which it aims to sell between 70% and 80% of the projects it develops internally, unlocking value from development activities and reinvesting capital in new opportunities. Greenvolt Power CEO Weronika Nowak said: “Ełk and Turośń demonstrate Greenvolt Power’s ability to take complex, large-scale battery storage projects from development to completion. “Poland is a strategic market for us and a key driver of our growth in Central Europe, where we will continue to deliver projects that meet the evolving needs of the energy system.” Greenvolt Power currently has a pipeline of approximately 4.6GW of BESS projects across its markets. In August 2026, the company obtained €218m in financing from UniCredit to support its BESS projects at Ełk and Turośń.

artigo.texto: GM Simulates 300,000 EV Battery Designs Before Production General Motors (GM) has revolutionized electric vehicle (EV) battery development by virtually testing over 300,000 battery configurations before producing any physical cells. This extensive simulation approach, utilizing approximately 300 million computing hours—equivalent to roughly 34,000 years on a single computer—enabled GM to finalize a battery pack design in just one month. Advancing Battery Technology with LMR Chemistry The simulations primarily focused on a novel battery chemistry known as lithium manganese-rich (LMR). GM claims that LMR batteries offer 33% greater energy density than conventional lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries while maintaining comparable costs. Additionally, LMR cells incorporate 30-40% nickel, a significant reduction from the typical 85% nickel content in current high-nickel batteries. Despite previous challenges with battery longevity associated with LMR chemistry, GM states it has addressed these issues, supporting the rollout of its upcoming fourth-generation EV platform. This platform is expected to deliver around 20% more driving range per kilowatt-hour than existing GM vehicles, alongside streamlined electric motors featuring 40% fewer parts, a 30% reduction in wiring, and a central computer with 40 times increased processing capacity. Implications for U.S. EV Industry and Manufacturing GM’s innovative simulation methods are also shortening the traditional development cycle—the company anticipates reducing what typically takes four to five years by half. For instance, air flow simulations that used to require 60 hours can now be completed in just a minute, while the assembly process in their PlantBrAIn factory has accelerated battery pack production by 30%. These virtual models even assist in optimizing factory layouts before construction. The LMR battery cells will be manufactured at the Ultium Cells plant in Spring Hill, Tennessee, a joint venture between GM and LG Energy Solution. Meanwhile, GM’s $900 million battery facility in Warren, Michigan, is slated to reach full operational status later this year, with mass production expected to commence in 2028. GM Vice President of battery technology Kurt Kelty emphasized the company’s commitment to domestic innovation, stating, “We’re not licensing this from China.” With an investment exceeding $16 billion in U.S. research and manufacturing this year, GM aims to leverage artificial intelligence and advanced simulation to remain competitive internationally—particularly against Chinese automakers—by accelerating timelines and lowering costs. Why This Matters for Pakistan GM’s pioneering use of AI-driven battery design and manufacturing signals a transformative shift in automotive innovation that is reshaping the global EV landscape. For Pakistan, a nation keen on expanding its electric vehicle market and manufacturing base, GM’s advances highlight the importance of integrating digital technologies and investing in local research capabilities to compete globally. As the electric vehicle industry grows rapidly worldwide, Pakistan’s stakeholders can draw lessons from GM’s model to enhance local production efficiencies, develop cost-effective battery technologies, and reduce dependence on imported automotive components. Incorporating such innovations could accelerate Pakistan’s ambition to improve green mobility, reduce fossil fuel reliance, and foster economic growth through technology-driven manufacturing sectors.

artigo.texto: Did Ukraine's data center strikes affect Russia's bot army? We now have better evidence. Pro-Russian accounts targeting Ukrainians on Facebook and Telegram sharply declined after Ukrainian drone strikes on Yandex data centers, according to a new report from a Ukrainian government agency. It’s the most direct evidence so far behind a claim that went viral last week, but it falls well short of proving it. The report comes from Ukraine’s Center for Countering Disinformation (CCD), which operates under the country’s National Security and Defense Council. It was published Oct. 15, and United24 Media covered it on Oct. 17. The CCD used software from the Ukrainian security firm Osavul to track accounts it flagged as showing "signs of inauthentic behavior." According to Osavul's website, the firm "builds AI-powered risk intelligence for hybrid threats." According to United24, the CCD analyzed 22,664 messages from 5,201 accounts posted between Oct. 6 and 12, across 26 topics in Ukraine’s information space. The report found two sharp drops in activity, each following a strike that fully shut down a Yandex facility. On Oct. 8, the day a fire took Yandex’s data center in Sasovo, in Russia’s Ryazan region, offline, messages fell 83.6 percent, from 4,032 to 660. You May Also Like The number of active accounts fell by a similar share. Activity rebounded past pre-strike levels by Oct. 10, but on Oct. 12, a day after a strike fully halted operations at a Yandex data center in Vladimir, messages fell by 42.6 percent and active accounts dropped by 41 percent. A smaller group of 98 accounts that posted pro-war propaganda, conspiracy theories, or calls for violence followed the same pattern. The CCD concluded that strikes on data centers can significantly disrupt Russian influence networks, but the effect appears to be short-lived. Mashable was unable to verify the CCD’s findings independently. Before publication, we emailed Osavul to request the underlying dataset, the criteria it uses to flag inauthentic behavior, and any information about where the accounts were hosted. Osavul did not respond by publication time. The report never defines "inauthentic behavior." While the term is quite broad, some general signals that researchers typically attribute to bot accounts include newly created profiles, unusually high posting volume, blank or AI-generated profile photos, and activity across many unrelated political narratives. Without Osavul’s criteria, it’s unclear whether these accounts are automated, run by coordinated humans, or a mix of both. Still, if the numbers hold up, they point to something real. The CCD argues that the drops show strikes on data centers can significantly constrain Russia’s information operations by disrupting the automated networks behind them. However, the agency also acknowledges how quickly the accounts came back, suggesting the disruptions were "substantial but short-lived." Why it matters The findings arrive after a week of overheated claims. Last week, Mashable looked at viral claims that Ukrainian drone strikes on Yandex data centers had knocked Russia’s bot army offline. The conclusion we and other outlets reached was that the data behind those claims couldn’t support them. That claim spread like wildfire on social media, amplified by European officials and even backed up by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum, President Zelenskyy said "everyone noticed" a drop in Russian bot activity. Social media users echoed similar observations about the seemingly stark decline in pro-GOP and pro-AfD posts after the strikes. It was an easy idea to believe, given how platforms like Facebook and X incentivize and reward polarizing political ragebait, and Russia’s online influence operations are well-documented. The claim also seemed to have supporting data. United24 Media, the Ukrainian government-run outlet whose reporting drove much of the conversation, cited an analysis by The Deep Dive of Cloudflare Radar data. That data showed automated traffic from Yandex’s network had nearly vanished by Oct. 11. As Mashable reported at the time, that data couldn’t support the claim. "Automated traffic" means any request that software, rather than a person, sends to a website, and most of it is mundane. Yandex, often called "Russia's Google," runs the Federation's biggest search engine, so its network constantly sends out crawlers to index the web. Knocking its data centers offline would stop that traffic, whether or not a single troll account went quiet. We found no published evidence tying influence campaigns on social media to Yandex servers, and United24 acknowledged the same limitation. Cloudflare has since published its own analysis. It said its data doesn’t appear to support claims that the strikes crippled social media manipulation, though it couldn’t rule out a connection. Zelenskyy’s office has also narrowed his remarks. According to BBC Verify, his office said the president was "talking about the atmosphere on social media" rather than a fall in bot activity. Topics Cybersecurity Chance Townsend is the General Assignments Editor at Mashable, covering tech, video games, dating apps, digital culture, and whatever else comes his way. He has a Master's in Journalism from the University of North Texas and is a proud orange cat father. His writing has also appeared in PC Mag and Mother Jones. In his free time, he cooks, loves to sleep, and greatly enjoys Detroit sports. artigo.texto: NASA Develops Freeze-Resistant Battery with EV Potential NASA has advanced battery technology with the creation of a freeze-resistant solid-state battery designed to operate in extreme cold environments, such as the lunar South Pole. This innovation holds promise not only for space exploration but also for future applications in electric vehicles (EVs) and other terrestrial technologies. Breakthrough in Cold-Climate Battery Technology The newly developed solid-state battery prototype, part of NASA’s SPEARS (Solid Power for Extreme Environment Adaptability and Resilience in Space) project, has demonstrated remarkable resilience by surviving temperatures as low as minus 274 degrees Fahrenheit (minus 170 degrees Celsius) without sustaining damage. Moreover, the battery maintained functionality at significantly cold temperatures of minus 112 degrees Fahrenheit (minus 80 degrees Celsius), albeit at reduced performance, and showed optimal operation within a range from minus 76 to 176 degrees Fahrenheit (minus 60 to 80 degrees Celsius). This development represents a critical advancement because conventional lithium-ion batteries, which rely on liquid electrolytes, fail to operate effectively in the harsh conditions faced on the lunar surface, where temperatures at the South Pole can plunge to minus 328 degrees Fahrenheit (minus 200 degrees Celsius). Solid electrolytes in the new design eliminate issues related to freezing and the risk of fire, making them ideally suited for space missions and potentially safer for everyday use. Implications for Space Missions and Earth Applications The freeze-resistant batteries could power lunar rovers, scientific devices, and emergency tools as part of NASA’s Artemis program, which targets renewed human presence on the moon. While these batteries remain laboratory prototypes yet to be tested in space, NASA envisions that the technology could be adapted for a range of terrestrial uses including electric vehicles, drones, mobile phones, and grid energy storage systems. In the context of Pakistan, where extreme weather conditions and energy storage reliability pose ongoing challenges, innovations like NASA’s battery technology could have significant future benefits. Enhanced battery resilience and safety would improve the performance and dependability of electric vehicles and renewable energy systems, contributing to cleaner energy use and greater energy security in diverse Pakistani climates. As Haley Zaremba, an energy journalist, notes, “The ability of these solid-state cells to endure such extreme lows paves the way for safer, more efficient batteries beyond space exploration.” This breakthrough underscores the growing importance of solid-state batteries in advancing the next generation of clean energy and electric mobility solutions worldwide.

artigo.texto: A Autoridade Finlandesa de Licenciamento e Supervisão (LVV) ordenou que o Google interrompesse temporariamente as obras de dois data centers no país após a empresa realizar o corte raso de florestas sem concluir os estudos de impacto ambiental exigidos. A decisão atinge as obras em Muhos, no norte da Finlândia, e em Otanmäki, cerca de 62 milhas a sudeste. O Google afirmou que suspendeu os trabalhos preparatórios nos dois locais e que vai cumprir as exigências do regulador. O que aconteceu Uma estimativa da Associação Finlandesa para a Conservação da Natureza (SLL) citada pela Mother Jones aponta que cerca de 250 mil árvores foram removidas em Muhos, em uma área de 815 acres. No site de Otanmäki, a ecologista Mari Annala, da SLL, calcula que outras 150 mil árvores tenham sido derrubadas. A reportagem também informa que o projeto de infraestrutura de inteligência artificial do Google na Finlândia é estimado em US$ 17 bilhões e que mais de 93 mil pessoas assinaram uma petição pedindo regulação para data centers e compensação às comunidades locais. O primeiro-ministro Petteri Orpo classificou o ocorrido em Muhos como um choque. Moradores relatam impactos diretos. Em Otanmäki, a perda de vegetação e de animais silvestres levou lobos a se aproximarem da vila, segundo Anni Ranta, que vive na região há gerações. Ela disse que os animais deixaram a floresta e que o ruído das obras, em solo de rocha dura, reverbera como um tambor. O pai dela, Pentti Korhonen, afirmou que a água do córrego próximo ficou marrom depois da derrubada. Em Muhos, o morador Antti Jakonen criticou a forma como o corte foi feito, classificando-a como um método sem sentido. O gerente do Google na Finlândia, Antti Järvinen, pediu desculpas pelos desmatamentos, mas disse que a empresa agiu com base no entendimento da legislação que tinha à época. Um porta-voz da companhia afirmou que o Google atua no país há 15 anos e sempre buscou atender ou superar exigências de zoneamento, meio ambiente, saúde e segurança. Segundo a empresa, após receber as cartas da LVV em 6 de outubro, as obras preparatórias em Muhos e Kajaani, onde fica Otanmäki, foram paradas e uma resposta formal foi enviada ao regulador. O Google também informou que planeja replantar árvores em 74 acres no local de Muhos.

artigo.texto: Beijing, 26 out (Xinhua) -- A integração da China entre tecnologias digitais e finanças verdes está abrindo novas oportunidades para a cooperação global na transição de baixo carbono, disseram os participantes na Conferência Anual 2026 do Fórum da Rua Financeira, em Beijing. Sob o tema "Construindo um ecossistema aberto, colaborativo e inclusivo para o desenvolvimento financeiro global", o evento de quatro dias foi encerrado na semana passada. Ele reuniu participantes nacionais e internacionais, tanto online quanto presencialmente, para discutir o desenvolvimento financeiro e a cooperação diante dos desafios econômicos globais. "Nos últimos anos, vimos o mercado de finanças verdes da China crescer várias vezes", disse Ma Jun, presidente do Instituto de Finanças e Sustentabilidade em Beijing. "A integração das finanças digitais e verdes criou muitas oportunidades de crescimento e ajudou a impulsionar os investimentos transfronteiriços." Esse crescimento ganhou reconhecimento internacional. " A China melhorou a qualidade do ar ao desenvolver uma economia circular e construir uma sociedade ambientalmente amigável", disse Yaseen Anwar, ex-presidente do Banco Estatal do Paquistão, em um fórum paralelo. Ele acrescentou que a capacidade instalada de energia eólica e solar do país continua a crescer, enquanto produtos verdes, como veículos de nova energia (NEVs), lideram globalmente. Dados divulgados pelo Ministério da Ecologia e do Meio Ambiente mostram que a capacidade instalada de geração de energia renovável do país atingiu 2,455 bilhões de quilowatts no primeiro semestre deste ano, representando 60,7% de sua capacidade total instalada de geração de energia. A China ocupa o primeiro lugar mundial tanto na produção quanto nas vendas de NEVs há 11 anos consecutivos. Nos últimos anos, a China tem oferecido amplas oportunidades para o investimento verde global e a transição de baixo carbono, aplicando tecnologias como big data, blockchain e IA para melhorar a governança das finanças verdes, modernizar as estruturas industriais e aprimorar o meio ambiente ecológico. O Banco da China emitiu títulos verdes no âmbito da Iniciativa Cinturão e Rota para apoiar grandes projetos verdes, como usinas fotovoltaicas de grande escala em países parceiros. Espera-se que esses projetos forneçam às comunidades locais um abastecimento estável e de longo prazo de energia renovável limpa. O mercado de carbono é uma importante ferramenta política para lidar com as mudanças climáticas por meio de mecanismos de mercado e para acelerar a transformação verde abrangente do desenvolvimento econômico e social. O volume acumulado de negociação de cotas de emissão de carbono no mercado nacional de carbono da China ultrapassou 1 bilhão de toneladas, de acordo com dados do Ministério da Ecologia e do Meio Ambiente. A experiência da China no desenvolvimento de seu mercado de carbono também oferece lições com as quais outros países podem aprender. "Os compromissos da China em relação às emissões de carbono e o desenvolvimento de seu mercado de carbono têm dado uma contribuição enorme para a ação climática global", disse Charles Bowman, copresidente da Força-Tarefa de Finanças Verdes Reino Unido-China. "A cooperação em finanças verdes entre a China e o Reino Unido tem promovido a transformação econômica, a conservação da biodiversidade e o desenvolvimento sustentável em ambos os países", acrescentou ele. Essa cooperação também está se estendendo aos parceiros da Iniciativa Cinturão e Rota. Muitos deles estão implementando ativamente políticas verdes e sustentáveis, ao mesmo tempo que mobilizam capital. "A China adaptou serviços para diferentes regiões, incluindo a promoção da aplicação de instrumentos de finanças verdes e do desenvolvimento de mercado, a realização de pesquisas aprofundadas sobre políticas verdes e o avanço dos mecanismos do mercado de carbono", disse Cheng Lin, chefe do Escritório do Secretariado em Beijing para os Princípios de Investimento Verde para a Iniciativa Cinturão e Rota. Especialistas observaram na conferência que, como as tecnologias digitais e inteligentes remodelaram profundamente o setor financeiro nos últimos anos, potencializar as finanças verdes com essas tecnologias é um caminho fundamental para o desenvolvimento sustentável global. "As tecnologias digitais e inteligentes podem oferecer um importante apoio às finanças verdes, superando gargalos na coleta e análise de dados e monitoramento e avaliação de riscos", disse Zhang Bei, vice-chefe do departamento de pesquisa do Banco Popular da China. À medida que os eventos climáticos extremos se tornam mais frequentes, tecnologias como sistemas de informação geográfica, sensoriamento remoto por satélite e grandes modelos de linguagem podem ajudar a avaliar com maior precisão como diferentes regiões e grupos populacionais estão lidando com as mudanças climáticas, identificar prioridades para a adaptação e direcionar o financiamento para as áreas com maiores necessidades, observou Zhang. O papel cada vez mais importante da tecnologia digital nas finanças verdes da China deve beneficiar mais parceiros globais em seus esforços de desenvolvimento sustentável. Mari Elka Pangestu, vice-presidente do Conselho Econômico Nacional da Indonésia, disse que a China é líder em tecnologias limpas. Ela expressou esperança de aprofundar a cooperação com parceiros chineses além do investimento de capital, por meio do estabelecimento de mais joint ventures, do aumento da produção local e do fortalecimento da transferência de tecnologia. O 15º Plano Quinquenal da China (2026-2030) prevê a expansão de produtos e serviços financeiros verdes e o incentivo a maiores investimentos no desenvolvimento verde e de baixo carbono.

artigo.texto: The U.S. government's new designation of helium gas as critical for artificial intelligence and data centers may spur drilling projects in Kansas, Oklahoma and Texas. "Helium is essential to producing the semiconductors and advanced technologies that power our economy. By designating helium as a critical material, we are taking another step toward securing our supply chains, creating American jobs, and ensuring the United States leads the world in energy and technological innovation," U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright announced Oct. 23. Reasons for the critical-material designation were outlined the same day in a four-page Federal Register notice. It stated that growing AI infrastructure in the United States will depend on the ability of the nation to produce semiconductors. "Helium's unique properties make it indispensable to semiconductor production, with no viable substitutes in many critical applications. The United States has significant domestic deposits of helium-rich natural gas to support growing industrial demand," the Department of Energy noted. What Is Helium? Helium is one of seven types of "Noble Gases" named as such because they don't have normally have chemical reactions with any other gas or substances. (Other types of these inert gases include helium, krypton, neon and radon.) "Noble gases are the least reactive elements in the periodic table, and they condense out of the air at very low temperatures. They are therefore extremely difficult to trap at temperatures above freezing," according to DOE. Helium (which is non-toxic and lighter than air) has no odor or color. A byproduct of extracting natural gas, helium has multiple high-tech uses including in use in quantum computing, air-to-air missile guidance systems, medical MRI machines, cardio-pulmonary resuscitation pumps for heart surgery, fiber-optic cables, blimps, deep sea diving and leak testing natural gas infrastructure. Domestic Helium The most recent U.S. Geological Survey assessment of helium stated that in 2025 there were 29 plants producing various types of helium domestically. In addition, Texas had three underground cavern storage sites for helium. "In 2025, six new helium operations (three in New Mexico and one each in Colorado, Kansas, and Montana) began producing helium in the United States. A helium storage cavern was brought online in Beaumont, TX, which was able to store excess helium production," stated a 2026 mineral commodity summary for helium. USGS estimated that last year's sales of Grade-A helium (99.997% helium or greater) and gaseous helium (above 98% helium) amounted to $970 million.

artigo.texto: Alto valor das baterias e mercado ilegal de peças multiplicam furtos e roubos de carros elétricos em São Paulo Foram 186 ocorrências de janeiro a julho de 2026 contra 62 no mesmo período do ano passado Os carros elétricos e híbridos entraram na mira dos ladrões no estado de São Paulo, e os casos de furtos e roubos cresceram 200%, segundo levantamento feito pela empresa de rastreamento de veículos Ituran para O GLOBO. A empresa analisou dados de roubos e furtos da Secretaria de Segurança Pública (SSP) e registros que identificam as marcas e os modelos envolvidos nas ocorrências, o que permitiu calcular a evolução dos crimes envolvendo carros elétricos e híbridos. Foram 186 ocorrências de janeiro a julho de 2026 contra 62 no mesmo período do ano passado. Veículos a combustão, no entanto, ainda são responsáveis por praticamente 99% desse tipo de crime no estado: houve mais de 56 mil ocorrências entre janeiro e julho deste ano. - Infecções, falhas na assistência e inconsistências em prontuários: Tudo sobre a morte de seis bebês em hospital de SP - Vídeo: Clube da Esquina, local histórico para a MPB, é vandalizado com tinta vermelha em Belo Horizonte; polícia investiga A Polícia Civil encontrou desmanches clandestinos focados em carros elétricos principalmente da montadora chinesa BYD, em ao menos duas ocasiões, na Zona Leste da cidade de São Paulo. Delegados da unidade especializada em roubos de veículos ouvidos pelo GLOBO apontam que ainda não identificaram pelas peças provenientes de crimes nas fiscalizações a desmanches legalizados — aqueles que revendem peças de veículos apreendidos ou leiloados, por exemplo. Se até 2025 a maior parte dos casos envolvendo carros elétricos ou híbridos era de roubos com uso de violência, em 2026 o cenário apontou para uma alta de furtos. Especialistas ouvidos pela reportagem afirmam que os ladrões aprenderam a quebrar as barreiras de segurança desses modelos. O principal alvo dos criminosos são as baterias, informam seguradoras e delegados. A peça chega a corresponder a 50% do valor dos carros — os modelos citados na reportagem, quando novos, variam entre R$ 120 mil a R$ 250. Também estão na mira dos criminosos itens para reposição, como para-choques, retrovisores e portas, que têm alto custo e são escassas no mercado nacional. Os dados apontam que o modelo que mais aparece nos boletins de ocorrência é o BYD Dolphin, seguido do Toyota Corolla Cross híbrido. As versões mais visadas têm entre dois e cinco anos de fabricação. Essa fatia responde por 47% dos casos. O Toyota Corolla Cross não é o modelo híbrido mais vendido atualmente, mas a demanda por peças de reposição aumenta à medida que a frota envelhece. Incidência na capital A capital paulista concentra a maior parte dos casos registrados no estado, com 137 ocorrências. Um engenheiro de 67 anos, que pediu para não ser identificado, teve um BYD Dolphin Mini furtado na Zona Leste. No dia 14 de julho deste ano, um domingo, por volta das 7h40, ele estacionou o carro na Avenida Secondino, na Vila Prudente, e quando retornou ao local, no fim de tarde, não o encontrou mais. O carro tinha rastreador, e o proprietário conseguiu localizá-lo num endereço a cerca de 20 minutos de distância, em Sapopemba, também na Zona Leste. A vítima acionou a polícia, que identificou no local uma loja de peças automotivas aparentemente ilegal. Os policiais encontraram ali um alçapão, que dava acesso a um porão, onde se depararam com peças do carro do engenheiro, como o para-brisa, além do motor de outro veículo com registro de furto, também da BYD. Cinco pessoas foram presas em flagrante. — O furto me causa medo e apreensão até hoje. A estrutura montada para o desmonte do meu carro era bastante organizada e profissional, se é que posso utilizar essa palavra — diz o engenheiro. — Não existe sistema (antifurto) seguro. É só questão de tempo para (criminosos) descobrirem as brechas Outro desmanche clandestino foi encontrado em agosto passado durante uma operação do 42º DP do Parque São Lucas que investigava uma quadrilha especializada no furto de veículos elétricos. Policiais civis bateram na porta da casa de um homem apontado como membro do grupo, no bairro Vila Ema, para cumprir mandados de busca e apreensão, quando se depararam com uma dezena de peças automotivas, entre portas, capô, para-choques e volantes. Os policiais conseguiram identificar uma porta de um BYD Song Plus que havia sido furtado dois meses antes. O homem que morava no local foi preso. O principal foco desse grupo eram as baterias dos carros. A equipe da delegacia ainda tenta desvendar como funcionava a cadeia de receptação da quadrilha e os possíveis compradores desses componentes. Uma tentativa de roubo a dois BYDs na Zona Sul de São Paulo quase terminou em latrocínio em novembro do ano passado. Era manhã de uma sexta-feira na região do bairro do Ipiranga quando três homens conseguiram entrar na residência de um casal e ficaram à espreita na garagem, onde os carros eram carregados. Sem conseguir ligar os automóveis, eles esperaram os proprietários aparecerem. O primeiro alvo, a mulher, foi surpreendida pelo trio quando descia as escadas em direção à garagem. Um dos homens, armado, a derrubou e apontou a arma para a boca da vítima, pedindo que ela ficasse quieta. Ela gritou, e o ladrão atirou. O disparo a atingiu de raspão a pálpebra e a testa da vítima. A movimentação foi percebida pela vizinhança, que chamou a polícia. Os criminosos desistiram de levar os veículos e começaram a buscar outros bens. Após roubarem um celular e as chaves da casa, eles foram contidos por vizinhos e pela Polícia Militar durante tentativa de fuga. Entre janeiro de julho deste ano, 83% das ocorrências envolvendo carros elétricos e híbridos foram furtos. Até 2025, nesse mesmo intervalo, a dinâmica criminal era diferente: 59% dos casos eram roubos, com abordagens diretas e uso de violência contra as vítimas. — Em 2025, nossa percepção é que (os elétricos e híbridos) ainda eram novidade,

artigo.texto: Plataformas Broadcast Soluções de Dados e Conteúdos Soluções de Tecnologia 23 de outubro de 2026, às 14:37 Artigo de: Eduardo Sattamini Ao longo das últimas décadas, o Brasil construiu uma das matrizes elétricas mais renováveis do mundo e segue ampliando a participação de fontes como a solar e a eólica. Esse avanço, essencial para a transição energética, traz um novo desafio: garantir que a energia esteja disponível não apenas quando é produzida, mas quando é necessária. É nesse contexto que o armazenamento ganha importa ncia estratégica. A geração solar, por exemplo, está concentrada durante o dia, enquanto um dos períodos mais desafiadores para a operação ocorre no fim da tarde e início da noite, quando a produção fotovoltaica cai rapidamente e a demanda permanece elevada. É justamente nesse descasamento que o armazenamento demonstra seu valor para o sistema. Seu papel, porém, vai além de deslocar energia no tempo. Baterias respondem rapidamente às necessidades do sistema, agregam flexibilidade, ajudam a administrar a variabilidade das fontes renováveis e podem contribuir para a estabilidade e a segurança do fornecimento. Por isso, armazenamento deve ser visto como infraestrutura do sistema elétrico, e não apenas como mais uma tecnologia de geração. Vale lembrar que o armazenamento de energia não se limita às baterias. Entre as principais soluções disponíveis estão as baterias químicas, como as de íons de lítio, e as tecnologias mecânicas, como as usinas hidrelétricas reversíveis. Cada alternativa possui características próprias de capacidade, duração, escala e aplicação. No contexto atual, entretanto, os sistemas de armazenamento em baterias (BESS) têm se destacado pela rapidez de implantação, modularidade e capacidade de responder às necessidades de flexibilidade do sistema elétrico. A experiência internacional mostra que esse mercado já alcançou escala. O Chile é hoje uma referência latino-americana na incorporação de sistemas de armazenamento, combinando projetos associados a renováveis e instalações conectadas diretamente à rede. A ENGIE, por exemplo, já possui mais de 800 MW de BESS em operação no País. Essa experiência mostra que a discussão deixou de ser conceitual: baterias já fazem parte da operação cotidiana de sistemas com elevada participação de fontes renováveis. Tocopilla é talvez o exemplo mais emblemático dessa transformação. Inserido em uma trajetória mais ampla de expansão do armazenamento no Chile, o projeto de Tocopilla representa um marco relevante na reconversão energética do país. No local onde funcionou por mais de um século um complexo termelétrico e cuja última unidade a carvão foi desligada em 2022, entrou em operação comercial um sistema de 116 MW e 660 MWh. Com quase seis horas de armazenamento, o projeto reaproveita infraestrutura existente e transforma um antigo polo de geração fóssil em um ativo voltado à flexibilidade e à estabilidade do sistema. É uma demonstração concreta de como armazenamento, descarbonização e reconversão de ativos podem caminhar juntos. No Brasil, as perspectivas também apontam espaço para expansão. O Plano Decenal de Expansão de Energia 2035 projeta crescimento expressivo do armazenamento em baterias, enquanto os primeiros leilões de reserva de capacidade dedicados à tecnologia devem abrir uma nova frente de investimentos. O interesse dos investidores no certame previsto para dezembro deste ano confirma essa percepção: o volume de projetos cadastrados mostra que existe capital e disposição para desenvolver esta tecnologia. Mas a largada precisa ser bem desenhada. O primeiro ponto é assegurar critérios robustos de pré-qualificação dos investidores. Um mercado nascente e estratégico exige participantes com capacidade técnica, financeira e operacional para cumprir os compromissos assumidos. Isso deve estar combinado a responsabilidades e penalidades adequadas em caso de descumprimento contratual. A competição deve produzir preços eficientes, mas, sobretudo, projetos executáveis. Também é fundamental uma alocação coerente dos custos. A contratação de baterias busca atender necessidades sistêmicas de potência, segurança e confiabilidade. Portanto, o desenho econômico e regulatório precisa refletir corretamente quem se beneficia desses atributos e evitar distorções que acabem sendo incorporadas aos preços ofertados ou prejudiquem a competição. Há, ainda, um ponto que merece mais atenção: operar baterias em grande escala é muito mais complexo do que pode parecer. À primeira vista, um sistema modular pode dar a impressão de um grande “lego”: instalar contêineres, conectá-los à rede, colocá-los à disposição do Operador Nacional do Sistema (ONS) e receber uma receita fixa de capacidade. Na prática, não é assim. O desempenho depende da integração entre baterias, sistemas de conversão de potência, transformadores, proteção, controle e infraestrutura de conexão. É preciso administrar ciclos de carga e descarga, eficiência e degradação dos equipamentos, disponibilidade, manutenção, limites térmicos, sistemas de controle e segurança, além da interação entre o despacho da bateria e outros ativos conectados ao mesmo ponto da rede. A experiência chilena mostra ainda que novos requisitos técnicos e regulatórios podem surgir à medida que a tecnologia ganha escala, exigindo capacidade de engenharia e adaptação operacional. Além disso, projetos de armazenamento exigem uma cadeia complexa de suprimentos, processos rigorosos de integração tecnológica, atendimento a requisitos de segurança cada vez mais sofisticados e equipes capacitadas para sua operação contínua. O desafio não está apenas em construir os ativos, mas em garantir seu desempenho ao longo de décadas, preservando confiabilidade, disponibilidade e capacidade de resposta às necessidades do sistema elétrico. Esses aspectos têm consequência direta sobre a confiabilidade e a economia dos projetos. O sucesso de um projeto não deve ser medido apenas pela sua implantação, mas pela capacidade de ent

artigo.texto: Segundo a CNBC, levantamento All-America Economic Survey da própria CNBC revela uma tensão política crescente nos Estados Unidos em torno da expansão da inteligência artificial: eleitores republicanos apoiam amplamente o desenvolvimento da tecnologia, mas muitos rejeitam a construção da infraestrutura necessária para sustentá-la perto de suas casas. O presidente Donald Trump tem tratado a corrida da IA com a China como imperativo de segurança nacional e pressionado por uma expansão acelerada de data centers e da rede elétrica que os alimenta. Entre apoiadores do movimento MAGA, quase 55% querem que as empresas sigam desenvolvendo IA avançada enquanto o Congresso trabalha em regras para o setor, ante 27% que defendem uma pausa. Apenas 29% apoiariam um data center a menos de 10 milhas de sua casa, enquanto 40% se opõem. Considerando todos os republicanos e simpatizantes, o apoio cai para 24%. No eleitorado em geral, 63% não querem um data center de IA por perto e só 13% são favoráveis. A resistência é maior entre democratas: 80% contrários e 4% favoráveis. A conta política A pressão tem obrigado Trump e republicanos em disputas acirradas a recalibrar o discurso do início do boom. Em Ohio, o senador Jon Husted, que em 2024, como vice-governador, anunciou uma expansão de US$ 10 bilhões da Amazon Web Services, agora promove um projeto de lei parado que obrigaria grandes instalações a cobrir seus próprios custos de rede e geração, em vez de repassá-los aos consumidores residenciais. Em agosto, o comitê republicano para o Senado alertou empresas de IA de que a rejeição a data centers ameaçava a reeleição de Husted e classificou o tema como um risco pouco notado para as eleições de meio de mandato, conforme reportou a Axios. No Texas, o governador Greg Abbott suspendeu licenças para data centers até a conclusão de revisões de impacto na rede elétrica e nos recursos hídricos, além de defender o fim de incentivos fiscais estaduais, menos de um ano depois de exaltar o estado como epicentro do desenvolvimento de IA. Na quarta-feira, Trump escreveu em publicação no Truth Social que os desenvolvedores deveriam pagar um dividendo financeiro às comunidades onde se instalam e gerar a própria energia. Questionados sobre a principal preocupação caso os republicanos mantenham o Congresso, 18% dos eleitores citaram a falta de regulação de IA e data centers, percentual empatado com a continuidade das ações militares no Irã. A pesquisa ouviu 1.000 eleitores registrados entre 14 e 18 de outubro, com margem de erro de 3,1 pontos percentuais. Sobre o ritmo da tecnologia, 52% dos eleitores querem o desenvolvimento de IA avançada pausado até o Congresso aprovar regras de segurança, ante 32% que preferem seguir adiante para acompanhar a China. Brad Carson, ex-deputado democrata e cofundador do Public First Action PAC, disse à CNBC que “muitas pessoas estão incomodadas com esses data centers”. A indústria rejeita a leitura: Dan Diorio, da Data Center Coalition, afirmou à CNBC que o setor gera empregos, investimento e arrecadação e que os operadores pagam pela energia que consomem.

artigo.texto: Next Upcoming Canary Live Bay Area By Canary Media Energy storage is taking off as the state moves to make development easier and more profitable, but the horizon isn’t all clear for the sector. Just outside Boston, a developer is getting set to build a 700-megawatt storage facility that is expected to dwarf every other battery project in New England. One town over, another energy company just closed on $850 million in financing to build a 250-MW battery. Down near the Rhode Island border, ground has been broken on a 200-MW storage facility that is expected to be up and running by the end of the year. These and roughly a half dozen other projects at various stages are taking advantage of policies Massachusetts has put in place to help reach its goal of getting 5 gigawatts of battery storage capacity online by 2030, with another 5 GW to follow by 2035. While several larger and generally sunnier states top the list for installed storage capacity — California boasts a whopping 23 GW — Massachusetts’ ambition and policies put it at the forefront of the push to get more batteries on the grid. Thirteen states have set procurement targets for battery storage, but Massachusetts’ total of 10 GW by 2035 is the highest. And its policy landscape is setting the state up for success, observers say. “Massachusetts is really a leader in this space,” said Erin Smith, energy and grid policy director for the Environmental League of Massachusetts. “We’re ahead of the pack as it relates to encouraging battery buildout.” Massachusetts has ambitious clean energy goals and some of the highest electricity prices in the country. Batteries, the state figures, can help with both. They can store energy when power is cheapest and cleanest — like on sunny days when solar farms are producing in abundance — then send it back onto the grid during times of heavier demand, cutting down on the need to generate pricier, dirtier power. Battery systems can also bolster resilience, reducing outages during increasingly extreme and erratic weather. “If we have storage on the system, we can deploy it at different times to manage our load,” said Elizabeth Mahony, commissioner of the state Department of Energy Resources. So for the past 11 years, Massachusetts has been working to encourage the development of large-scale batteries, beginning with the launch of the Energy Storage Initiative in 2015 under then-Gov. Charlie Baker (R). The state blew past its initial target of installing 1 GW of storage capacity by 2025, topping 1.6 GW. Progress has only accelerated since then, thanks to a trio of state policies making it easier and more profitable to locate batteries in the state. The Clean Peak Standard, which went into effect in 2020, is a first-in-the-country program that pays renewable energy facilities and energy storage owners to send power onto the grid during times of peak demand. It provides an additional revenue source that can make battery developments more financially viable. “Those credits are incredibly important to financing and developing these projects,” said Aaron Lang, a partner at Boston law firm Foley Hoag who counts several battery developers among his clients. New siting and permitting reforms that went into effect on July 1 are also making Massachusetts more attractive to storage developers by streamlining and speeding up the approval process, Lang said. The new rules give the state Energy Facilities Siting Board authority to approve large energy projects, including storage facilities with a capacity of 100 MW or higher, rather than making developers work with the disparate permitting processes of individual municipalities. Decisions must be made within 15 months of application. “It ensures we can bring more clean energy, including batteries, online sooner,” Smith said. The state has also undertaken a series of procurements aimed at securing large-scale storage capacity. In December 2025, Massachusetts selected four projects totaling 1.3 GW of capacity to move ahead to contract negotiations with the major utilities. A second solicitation received 35 bids before it closed earlier this month; selected projects are set to be announced in February. Together, these actions create a climate that storage developers can rely on, said Hans Detweiler, vice president of development for Jupiter Power, the company behind the 700-MW Trimount project just outside Boston, where construction is slated to begin next year. “Moving through permitting and state solicitations takes years, so developers need confidence that the policy framework will remain stable over that period,” he said. “The Healey administration has consistently supported a procurement process that brings cost-effective resources to the grid to reduce electricity costs for consumers.” Even with all the state’s efforts, however, barriers remain. Perhaps the most pressing is the cost of interconnecting major projects like these to the grid. In September, developers canceled plans for a 125-MW battery system in the town of Tewksbury, citing the unexpectedly high cost — $65 million — of the upgrades necessary to hook into the grid. And that number is on the low end. Grid operator Independent System Operator New England recently completed a study of likely interconnection costs for a number of proposed projects, most of which were battery developments sited in Massachusetts. Many of the estimates topped $200 million, “quite a bit higher than developers anticipated,” Smith said. “We have an older grid here in New England, and it genuinely does require some upgrade costs to accommodate the influx of batteries,” she said. “How to allocate grid upgrade costs is going to be a debate.” Many battery proposals are also running into ardent community opposition. artigo.texto: According to SCMP , shares of Contemporary Amperex Technology Limited (CATL), the world's largest electric vehicle battery manufacturer, plummeted after reporting a significant drop in net profit in the third quarter of 2026. Profits decline, stock prices plummet. Analysts are unanimously issuing warnings, suggesting that the position of the global "battery king" is shaky amid the risk of declining domestic demand in China next year. During this week's trading sessions, CATL's stock continuously plummeted, recording a drop of more than 10% on the Shenzhen exchange and 8.6% in Hong Kong (China). In a notice submitted to the Stock Exchange earlier this week, CATL announced that its net profit for the third quarter of 2026 reached 21.25 billion yuan ( US$3.18 billion ), a 14.5% increase year-on-year. However, this figure represents a sharp decline from the 36% growth in the preceding second quarter and the peak of 57% growth in the final quarter of 2025. Although third-quarter revenue still increased sharply by nearly 59% compared to the same period last year, reaching 165.22 billion yuan ( US$24.74 billion ), the growth in both profit and revenue was lower than analysts' forecasts (expected at 26.03 billion and 175.05 billion yuan, respectively). Just before the announcement of its earnings results, CATL shares experienced a sharp decline earlier in the week on both the Hong Kong and Shenzhen stock exchanges. Notably, the stock's sharp decline has been ongoing since September, when electric vehicle manufacturers Xiaomi and Li Auto partnered with rivals to produce secondary batteries, causing CATL shares to plummet by more than 20% on the Hong Kong exchange and as much as 31% on the Shenzhen exchange since the beginning of the year. Furthermore, the recent sell-off also stemmed from market doubts about the potential for demand for energy storage systems (ESS) to fall short of expectations. Expectations to maintain its position as the "king of batteries". Earlier this week, JPMorgan also unexpectedly downgraded CATL's Hong Kong-listed stock rating to Neutral. This move reflects deep concerns among analysts about the declining earnings performance of China's electric vehicle industry, a factor that could dampen demand for CATL's battery products. According to JPMorgan, pressure from the re-imposition of battery consumption tax, the repeal of export tax refund policies, and international trade barriers are plaguing electric vehicle manufacturers in the country. Despite this, the investment bank still expects CATL to be a breakthrough name and maintain its position as a winner in the global battery industry. In a report published in early October, Citigroup projected that global battery demand growth would slow by 26% next year. This is attributed to the shrinking growth potential of the Chinese electric vehicle market, along with a slowdown in the growth of energy storage systems (ESS) due to the high base effect experienced in the earlier period. In the first nine months of this year, CATL's inventory increased by 53%, reaching 144.77 billion yuan ( US$21.68 billion ). Meanwhile, ongoing projects increased by 45% to 43 billion yuan ( US$6.44 billion ). The company explained this move as part of its strategy to expand its scale and enhance its production capacity. Amidst mounting market pressure, CATL spent nearly 50 million yuan ( $7.49 million ) earlier this week to buy back shares listed in Shenzhen. Prior to this, the company had already completed its largest-ever share buyback in mainland China, worth 40 billion yuan ( $6 billion ), in July. Overall, in the first three quarters of this year, CATL's revenue still recorded an impressive growth of 56% compared to the same period last year, reaching 442 billion yuan ( US$66.19 billion ), while net profit increased by 32%, reaching 64.5 billion yuan ( US$9.66 billion ).

artigo.texto: GM has partnered with Peak Energy to develop next-generation sodium-ion battery cells, but they’re not going into EVs – they’re for grid-scale energy storage projects. GM Ventures is making a strategic investment in Peak Energy. June 10, 2026: Under the partnership, GM will develop the sodium-ion cells in its Michigan battery labs and retain exclusive manufacturing rights. Peak Energy will integrate the cells into its battery storage systems as it ramps up US manufacturing. The companies are targeting a market that’s growing rapidly as utilities add battery storage to support renewable energy, rising electricity demand, and the buildout of data centers and AI infrastructure. Today’s stationary storage market is dominated by lithium-iron phosphate (LFP) batteries. But Peak Energy believes sodium-ion batteries can deliver a lower-cost alternative for grid applications, where energy density is less important than cost, reliability, and safety. A key part of Peak’s pitch is its passively cooled battery storage platform. Conventional LFP battery systems require active cooling equipment to maintain safe operating temperatures, adding cost and complexity. Peak says its system eliminates those cooling systems entirely. According to the company, its sodium-ion platform can reduce energy storage costs by 20% compared with conventional systems while delivering more than 99% uptime. Peak also argues that its design wastes less energy. It estimates that replacing conventional LFP storage systems with its passively cooled technology could reduce annual battery-storage energy waste in the US by up to 2 terawatt-hours. That’s enough electricity to power a mid-sized city for a year. GM’s vice president of battery and sustainability, Kurt Kelty, said sodium-ion is a strong fit for stationary storage. “At GM, we know that the application should determine the battery, and for grid-scale stationary storage, sodium-ion is the right solution,” Kelty said. “Peak is already demonstrating the value of sodium-ion through their innovative energy storage platform, and together we’re working to push those benefits even further with our next-generation cell – helping deliver more reliable, lower-cost energy storage at scale for the US grid.” Sodium-ion batteries still account for a small share of the global battery market, but interest is growing because they can be made from more abundant, lower-cost materials than lithium-based batteries. GM and Peak are betting those advantages could make sodium-ion an increasingly attractive option for large-scale energy storage. But don’t expect GM to develop sodium-ion battery cells for EVs, because the energy density is too low. October 23, 2026, update: Peak Energy has raised $108 million in an oversubscribed Series B funding round led by GM Ventures, with backing from LG Technology Ventures and other investors. Trains don't worry about aerodynamics - or really even weight. Daisy chain 2 or 3 cars worth of these behind an electric engine or two and do full swap outs for recharge/refuel stops. The sodium-ion battery startup plans to use the money to expand US manufacturing, fulfill more than $1 billion in existing customer orders, and bring its passively cooled energy storage systems to the power-hungry data center market. artigo.texto: Close to three-quarters of Americans oppose artificial intelligence data centers in their local communities. Another two-thirds have broader fears about AI. That’s according to recent national polls. Opposition to new data centers and worries about AI eliminating jobs, or worse, come ahead of the midterm elections next month as big technology companies look to build new facilities to power machine learning models. A poll released Oct. 20 by polling firm IPSOS in a survey of U.S. voters for the Washington Post and ABC News shows: • 72% oppose new data centers in their local communities • 57% believe AI will be bad for society • 65% worry AI will eliminate jobs • 33% fear there is a high risk of AI resulting in human extinction. Another 32% believe there is a moderate risk. • 62% say AI could result in people losing their decision making capabilities. “When 72% of voters don’t want a data center down the street, that’s not a tech story anymore. It’s a kitchen-table story,” said Joseph Roberto Lopez, a Texas-based communications strategist and managing partner with The Prescient Group. Lopez said the AI data center issue has moved from Silicon Valley and Wall Street to Main Street and local communities throughout the country. “The fight moved from ‘jobs and investment’ to ‘my power bill, my water, my neighborhood.’ Once an issue gets that local, it stops being abstract and starts moving votes,” Lopez said. The wave of new data centers has also brought home wider fears about AI’s global impacts, including infrastructure, jobs and security. “In my view, a data center becomes the physical place where people can express concerns about a technology that otherwise feels abstract,” said Nick Khami, founder of call4me.com, an AI phone agent. Khami said there are security concerns about AI that need more examination and transparency. “Developers need to explain specific benefits and safeguard in terms people can evaluate,” Khami said. Sydney Gomez said AI is causing anxiety for some Americans. Gomez, a clinical training specialist with Thriveworks, said a recent survey by the national mental health provider shows more than one in five Americans (21%) say AI is causing anxiety for them. “Data centers make AI feel tangible. Instead of thinking about AI as something happening somewhere online, residents may see a proposed facility near their homes and begin asking what this technology will mean for their community, resources and future,” she said. “Those concerns can overlap with broader anxieties about job security, privacy, environmental impacts, lack of trust in government to regulate, losing control of what is happening in their communities, and how quickly technology is changing our lives,” Gomez continued. While there is bipartisan and across-the-board consternation about AI and data centers, Democrats and young people are the most concerned and most opposed. A late September survey by the Pew Research Center shows 81% of self-described liberals are opposed to new data centers in their communities. That compares to 58% of conservatives. Almost two-thirds (64%) of young adults, ages 18 to 29, in the Pew survey believe new data centers will be bad for the environment. Data center opponents frequently cite energy and water consumption as well as noise and land-use concerns in their pushes against the technology facilities. William Pirrone, a founding member and managing principal of Georgia-based Rubicon Professional Services and Rubicon Technical Services, said energy tops the list of local concerns. Pirrone and his firm are veterans in the data center and technology infrastructure space. “Primary objections about new data center builds typically center around whether the local electric grid and natural resources can withstand the additional demand,” Pirrone said. “Since electricity requires an enormous amount of additional energy, it’s often the center point of discussion.” Pirrone said power supplies outside of utilities’ power grids can help assuage community concerns about infrastructure strains and higher electricity bills. “Engineers are deploying various design strategies that include solar, battery energy storage, fuel cells and onsite power generation plants,” he said. Another September survey by the Associated Press, NORC Center for Public Affairs Research and University of Chicago shows 70% of Democrats want limits in data centers compared to 57% of Republicans. More than 360 U.S. jurisdictions have enacted pauses, restrictions or bans on new data center developments, according to Interconnected Capital LLC. That includes ones in Florida, Maryland, Wisconsin, Minnesota, North Carolina and Ohio. The AI data center wave is being pushed by some of the richest companies and richest billionaires in the world. That includes Amazon, Alphabet/Google, Meta/Facebook, NVIDIA and Microsoft. The majority of existing data centers globally are located in the U.S. The technology sector contends that new bigger data centers are needed to keep up with exponentially bigger computing needs to feed and fuel machine learning models. A hefty portion of U.S. economic activity is also currently tied into AI and the data centers to power machine learning, according to an analysis by the Columbia Business School. Trump warns if the U.S. does not embrace the AI wave, including data centers, it could see China challenge American technology hegemony. Trump wants AI data center users to offer financial dividends to communities where they are landing. “I have watched the process closely, and data centers that were highly unpopular in a certain area, have become extremely popular when a financial deal is struck. MAKE DEALS, and get them built!!! GREAT FOR THE U.S.A.,” Trump said in a Truth Social post Oct. 21. Some data center developers and users have been offering community benefits money to local communities that help with education funding childcare access and infrastructure improvements. artigo.texto: At Trump rallies, data centers take back seat to butts President’s comments on physiques keep making headlines The backsides of Ohio GOP Sen. Jon Husted, rapper Nicki Minaj, even former Rep. Mike Rogers. As the midterm campaign enters its home stretch, President Donald Trump has talked up what he claims are the benefits of increasingly unpopular data centers, at the same time that he has made headlines taking about the physiques of Husted and others. After being an outspoken proponent of the technology facilities for months, Trump has shifted to putting the onus on local jurisdictions to extract economic value. At a Saturday night rally in Perry, Ga., he said: “Tell them to pay you $10,000, $15,000, $20,000 for everybody that lives in the community — they’ll do it. You just got to ask.” At the same time, he continues to discuss the literal bodies politic: During a Friday rally in Florida, he credited 72-year-old Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., for having, “the body of a 30 year old.” At the Georgia weekend rally, the president focused on Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff, calling him “a guy that looked very much to me like Pee-Wee Herman.” There was plenty of time Tuesday night in Greenville, N.C., to make his pitch for data centers, which have become a big issue this election cycle. Trump set a new record for his second term, speaking for 1 hour and 51 minutes, besting his Feb. 24 State of the Union Address by 3 minutes and 14 seconds, according to Roll Call’s Factba.se. But Trump, a self-described data center true believer, didn’t bring up the sprawling, power-needy facilities. Instead, Trump waited a few hours after returning to the White House to make another plug for the power-hungry facilities that have angered voters. He walked back into the executive mansion around 11 p.m. Tuesday night. About two-and-a-half hours later, at 1:37 a.m. Wednesday, he told his supporters to “make deals” around them. “As the President of the United States, I have been watching Data Centers very closely, and have come to a very strong conclusion. New and large, in some cases gigantic, Data Centers are mandated by me to make their own electricity, and give or sell any excess back to the local community, or grid, and therefore there is electric price increase,” he wrote on his social media platform, Truth Social. “If companies want to make their Data Centers popular, pay the community, and/or individuals within the community, a ‘dividend,’” he wrote before giving technology companies some guidance. “MAKE DEALS, and get them built!!! GREAT FOR THE U.S.A.” Trump did make a passing mention of the facilities Wednesday night at a rally inside a livestock expo center in Clemson, S.C. — and the crowd reacted with silence. He said if the companies that own data centers begin paying local school systems, governments or residents, “all of a sudden you’re going to see data centers are going to be so popular.” But such comments get overshadowed by his other favored topics, according to transcripts compiled by Factba.se. Husted, for instance, was very much on his mind in eastern North Carolina Tuesday as he stumped for his hand-picked GOP Senate candidate, Michael Whatley. “I’m studying his body. I’ve never studied the body of a man before — it’s not my thing. Nothing wrong with it of course, nothing. I always precede by saying nothing wrong, but it’s never been my thing, to be honest with you, but I looked at his ass. And then I looked at his legs and … I said, ‘His ass is, it’s like it’s like a pile of muscle,’” the president said to laughter. “Then I looked at his legs, and I said, ‘Man, his feet are big.’ Then I looked at his shoulders. And I tapped him on the shoulder, and it actually hurt my hand — it was like a piece of steel. And I said, ‘This guy’s a monster.’ And Jon Gruden told me that he was a violent tackler,” he said, referring to the former NFL head coach who played with Husted in college. Trump spent nearly 10 minutes at a Sunday rally in Port Huron, Mich., saying the news media did not understand that he was joking about evaluating Husted. “I’ve been living with this whole thing about the ass,” he said. “And, believe me, it’s of no interest to me — except to say that Jon Husten is one hell of an athlete.” He told former Rep. Rogers, the GOP Senate nominee in Michigan, that he would say nice things about his rear end, too, if it would guarantee a GOP seat pick-up. As voters fret about the cost of everyday life, he also on Sunday brought up the derrière of entertainer Minaj, who was at the Michigan rally: “By the way, I looked at one hell of a beautiful ass before: Nicki Minaj. That’s hard to miss. Stand up. That’s hard to miss.” But he did not plug data centers. Vice President JD Vance, on the other hand, focused on Husted’s Senate voting record during a Wednesday rally in Cincinnati. “Don’t worry, I’m not gonna talk about Jon Husted’s ass. I’m not gonna do it,” the former Ohio senator quipped of his appointed successor. Trump has seemed fixated on Husted’s build since Gruden told him about the senator’s days as a defensive back before an Oct. 3 rally in Vandalia, Ohio. He did make a pitch for data centers at the Vandalia rally and one on Oct. 12 in Youngstown. But that was to boost Husted, who pushed for a vote on the “Ratepayer Protection Act” before the Senate broke for its campaign recess. That measure, which was not advanced by the Senate, would require state regulators to consider adopting standards to ensure large data centers pay for needed grid upgrades. The White House responded to an email asking for comment about Trump’s rally mentions of the centers by providing a link to the Wednesday social media post, and provided a list of such projects and their economic benefits. artigo.texto: On October 24, 2026, CnEVPost reported that CATL had said on Weibo that the 60-kWh Nio Firefly pack uses its Qilin battery line. Firefly had announced the pack the day before, rating it for up to 560 km on China’s CLTC test cycle. What the Qilin report adds The Qilin identification links the Firefly’s larger battery option to a CATL product line. Firefly’s October 23 announcement covers the 60-kWh capacity and its claimed performance and battery design; the Qilin identification came in CnEVPost’s account of CATL’s statement on October 24. How the 42-kWh and 60-kWh packs compare CnEVPost reports that the 42-kWh standard pack is supplied by Sunwoda and uses LFP cells. It identifies the 60-kWh pack as a CATL Qilin battery with NCM cells. Firefly describes the larger pack’s chemistry as ternary lithium. The two configurations’ stated ranges use the China Light-Duty Vehicle Test Cycle, or CLTC. The long-range version’s stated CLTC figure is 140 km higher, about 33% above the 420-km rating. Both capacity and chemistry change between the versions, so the range figures do not isolate the effect of chemistry. CLTC is a standardized test-cycle rating, not a measure of distance in everyday driving. Firefly’s claims about performance and battery design Firefly says the 60-kWh pack keeps the 42-kWh model’s acceleration and energy-consumption performance while adding thermal-protection measures. The company also describes its battery design as having an all-aluminum grid structure, cross-shaped crash beams and water-and-electrical isolation. It says it conducted 14 safety assessments that exceeded national-standard requirements. For battery longevity, Firefly lists five technologies for the 60-kWh pack: low-lithium-loss anodes, passivated cathodes, biomimetic self-repairing electrolyte, electrode-sheet microstructure design and adaptive expansion-force management. These are the company’s descriptions of its design and assessments.

artigo.texto: Belkin is now offering two new semi solid state batteries for your iPhone. There’s one 10,000mAh offering with a USB-C port for charging. The second is a 5,000mAh MagSafe offering, which offers 15W Qi2 charging. Both come in much lighter than you’d expect, and both offer premium aluminum builds that are cold to the touch. 10K When you pick up this solid state battery bank, you’ll notice it feels so much lighter than you’d traditionally expect compared to other batteries of its capacity. For example, this battery comes in at 220g, compared to older 10K batteries that weigh between 240 and 300g. As I mentioned earlier, it also has a nice aluminum build. This thing feels premium, and because of the shape of it, it’s very pocketable. There isn’t much else to write about a battery bank, but it offers up to 60W of charging, and comes with a smart display that’ll show your battery percentage. It’s available for $89.95 on Amazon. 5K MagSafe If you want a thin, MagSafe battery – this is the one. I’m tempted to say that this one takes the cake for my favorite MagSafe battery for iPhone, just because it’s very light and incredibly thin. Granted, this battery bank doesn’t have any bells and whistles like a kickstand or smart display – but it gets the job done really well. Top comment by S. Jobs It would’ve been great if you explained what’s a semi-solid state battery, its pros and cons compared to what’s the usual in power banks out there. It’s also worth noting that if you’re buying an iPhone Duo, this will protrude from the bottom of the phone slightly. That’s going to be an issue with pretty much any MagSafe accessory made for iPhone Duo. It wouldn’t surprise me that if by CES next year, we see some iPhone Duo-designed MagSafe batteries. You can pick up one of these on Amazon for $69.99. artigo.texto: Earlier this month, Gov. Gavin Newsom and former Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger staged a low-key celebration marking the 20th anniversary of Assembly Bill 32, the landmark legislation committing California to immense reductions in greenhouse gas emissions. It was the most notable achievement of Schwarzenegger’s governorship, not only setting a series of deadlines for emissions reductions, but creating as one of its major tools a system for industry buy-in known as “cap-and-trade.” Environmental groups were opposed, favoring direct regulations, but Schwarzenegger insisted. Since then, the state has auctioned off a gradually diminishing number of emissions permits, thus, in theory, incentivizing industries to reduce greenhouse gases. The Los Angeles Times has calculated that early goals were met. But in recent years reductions have slowed, and the 2030 goal of being 40% lower than 1990 emissions levels is highly unlikely. Popular and political support for the state’s commitment to reach virtual zero emissions by 2045 also has been waning. Public Policy Institute of California pollsters found that while Californians still support emissions reductions in concept, views on specific programs have slipped. That’s particularly true of Newsom’s desire to ban the sale of new gasoline-powered vehicles by 2035. Support for that has dropped from 49% in 2021 to just 32%. “Affordability has become a dominant theme in public discourse today — and it’s affecting the public’s views on the environment,” the PPIC says. “Most Californians choose cost of living as the top issue facing the people of California today; few name environmental concerns.” The declining popularity of climate change programs is visible in the political arena. Newsom spent months portraying gasoline refiners as price gougers and polluters, but when two refineries announced plans to shut down in 2025, raising the possibility of fuel shortages, he quickly changed his tune. “We are all the beneficiaries of oil and gas. No one’s naive about that,” Newsom said at a press conference. “So it’s always been about finding a just transition, a pragmatism in terms of that process.” Defying environmental groups, he and the Legislature passed bills designed to increase oil production, and this year the state even redesigned the cap-and-trade program to provide no-cost emissions permits to refineries. The flip side of declining popular and political support for emissions reduction policies is a new warning from Newsom’s administration that California faces a slow-motion apocalypse. “Climate change is increasing the frequency, intensity, duration, and impacts of climate related events in California, including short- or long-term hazard events like wildfire, extreme heat, drought, flooding, and sea level rise,” the administration’s 109-page Fifth Climate Change Assessment declares. It is the latest in a series of such reports issued since AB 32 passed. Newsom endorsed its findings while, as might be expected from a likely presidential candidate, taking a shot at President Donald Trump. “As the Trump administration turns its back on science, California is doubling down on climate action, on protecting our communities, and on building a safer future,” Newsom said in a statement. Meanwhile, the climate assessment report’s warning of potentially catastrophic effects is re-energizing those who prescribe aggressive actions. UC Berkeley’s Center for Law, Energy and the Environment issued what it describes as a “roadmap” of steps that must be taken. “California is at a critical moment in its efforts to protect residents from the extreme weather caused by climate change,” Louise Bedsworth, the center’s exective director, said. “The next governor will need to demonstrate strong leadership to help the state navigate the intersecting challenges of worsening climate impacts, affordability, and federal hostility to the state’s goals.” Xavier Becerra, the former attorney general almost certain to succeed Newsom, has been noncommittal about the issue, especially about the 2035 halt on sales of gas-powered vehicles. It’s smart politics given the reversal of popular support.
