artigo.texto: 23/10/2026 - 15:19 O Google derrubou cerca de 250 mil árvores em uma área de 330 hectares em Muhos, no norte da Finlândia, para preparar a construção de um data center, de acordo com reportagem do The Guardian. O desmatamento ocorreu antes da conclusão das avaliações de impacto ambiental exigidas para o projeto. A Autoridade Finlandesa de Licenciamento e Supervisão (LVV) determinou a suspensão das atividades preparatórias que alteram significativamente o ambiente em Muhos e em outro empreendimento, em Otanmäki, na região de Kajaani. A interrupção deve permanecer até a conclusão dos procedimentos ambientais. Por que as obras dos data centers do Google foram suspensas? Em comunicado de 6 de outubro de 2026, a LVV informou que os terrenos já haviam passado por intervenções extensas enquanto as avaliações ambientais permaneciam em andamento. A autoridade identificou retirada de árvores e da camada superficial do solo, além da construção de acessos e alterações na drenagem. Para o órgão, intervenções antecipadas podem limitar a análise de alternativas e a prevenção de danos ambientais. A suspensão abrange atividades como desmatamento, escavações e movimentação de terra. Trabalhos de planejamento e estudos com efeitos ambientais reduzidos podem continuar. Google pede desculpas pelo desmatamento O diretor do Google na Finlândia, Antti Järvinen, pediu desculpas pela retirada da floresta. Ele afirmou que a empresa agiu “com base no melhor entendimento que tínhamos da legislação na época”. A companhia declarou que trabalha para proteger a qualidade da água em Muhos e planeja plantar árvores em 130 hectares do terreno. Em sua resposta, afirmou ainda que atua no país há 15 anos e busca cumprir ou superar as exigências ambientais e de segurança. Projeto integra investimento de € 13 bilhões em inteligência artificial Os empreendimentos de Muhos e Otanmäki fazem parte de um projeto de infraestrutura de inteligência artificial de € 13 bilhões do Google. A Finlândia atrai empresas de tecnologia pela disponibilidade de terrenos e pelo clima frio, que favorece a redução dos custos de refrigeração. De acordo com a reportagem, o país tem 145 novos data centers em diferentes fases de planejamento. O governo finlandês apoia o investimento. O primeiro-ministro Petteri Orpo classificou a atração de capital como prioridade e afirmou que os projetos podem gerar benefícios duradouros. Donald Trump criticou o plano e pediu que o Google reconsiderasse o investimento, defendendo a construção dos centros nos Estados Unidos. Petição reúne mais de 93 mil assinaturas A retirada da floresta ampliou o debate sobre os impactos ambientais dos data centers. Mais de 93 mil pessoas assinaram uma petição que pede regras mais rígidas para o setor e uma cobrança destinada a compensar comunidades afetadas. Em Otanmäki, a estimativa citada pela reportagem é de outras 150 mil árvores derrubadas. A ecologista Mari Annala, da Associação Finlandesa para a Conservação da Natureza (SLL), afirmou que a irregularidade dos cortes impede a comercialização da madeira para unidades de processamento. A presidente do conselho da SLL, Hanna Halmeenpää, classificou a conduta do Google como “pura arrogância”. Já Jussi Kangasharju, chefe do departamento de ciência da computação da Universidade de Helsinque, questionou os benefícios econômicos dos empreendimentos para o país. Moradores relatam alterações na água e deslocamento de animais Moradores de Otanmäki relataram mudança na coloração de riachos, ruído das obras e presença de lobos na vila após a retirada da floresta. O biólogo Vesa Hyyryläinen apontou o deslocamento de pica-paus-de-três-dedos que ocupavam a região. O Ministério do Meio Ambiente informou que acompanha a expansão dos data centers e a aplicação das regras existentes. A pasta afirmou estar preparada para propor mudanças na legislação, caso sejam necessárias. Com informações do The Guardian e da autoridade ambiental finlandesa. artigo.texto: Setor elétrico cobra regulamentação do Redata ainda em 2026 Em carta a Lula, 21 associações pedem regras imediatas para habilitação de projetos e equipamentos; benefícios fiscais mais expressivos expiram em dezembro. O Fórum das Associações do Setor Elétrico (FASE), que reúne 21 entidades, encaminhou uma carta ao presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva solicitando prioridade na regulamentação do Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (Redata). O setor alerta que a demora na publicação das regras pode comprometer o aproveitamento dos incentivos fiscais previstos para 2026 e adiar investimentos em infraestrutura digital e energia elétrica. Enviado em 16 de outubro, o documento destaca que a Lei nº 15.504, sancionada em 15 de setembro de 2026, instituiu o Redata, mas sua implementação depende da definição dos procedimentos de habilitação das empresas e dos equipamentos contemplados. A principal preocupação está relacionada ao prazo dos benefícios de PIS/Pasep, Cofins e IPI, que produzem efeitos somente até 31 de dezembro de 2026, em razão da transição da reforma tributária. Segundo estimativa da Receita Federal citada pelas associações, o impacto fiscal do regime é de R$ 5,2 bilhões em 2026, com redução para aproximadamente R$ 1 bilhão por ano em 2027 e 2028. Para o FASE, a ausência de regulamentação impede que os investidores conheçam as condições necessárias para aderir ao programa e pode reduzir a capacidade do Brasil de atrair projetos de data centers. “Cada mês sem regulamentação representa, portanto, não mera postergação, mas perda efetiva de capacidade de atração de investimentos”, afirma a carta, assinada pelo presidente do fórum, Mário Menel. Associações pedem regulamentação em duas etapas O setor elétrico propõe que o governo priorize a publicação de dois conjuntos de regras considerados indispensáveis para iniciar os investimentos. O primeiro envolve os procedimentos de habilitação e coabilitação no Redata, com definição de requisitos e prazos, inclusive para comprovação do fornecimento de energia por fontes renováveis ou de baixa emissão. O segundo trata da relação de equipamentos beneficiados, com seus respectivos códigos da Nomenclatura Comum do Mercosul (NCM), incluindo produtos sem similar nacional que poderão ter o Imposto de Importação suspenso. As entidades defendem que os demais aspectos da regulamentação sejam discutidos posteriormente, sem impedir a habilitação dos primeiros projetos ainda em 2026. Na avaliação do fórum, a definição dessas regras também permitirá acelerar a contratação de energia e dar maior previsibilidade aos pedidos de conexão apresentados ao Operador Nacional do Sistema Elétrico (ONS). O presidente executivo da Brasscom, Affonso Nina, afirmou, em manifestação divulgada pela Associação Brasileira de Energia de Resíduos (ABREN), que a demora pode deslocar investimentos para outros mercados. “O Redata foi criado para que o Brasil deixe de processar seus dados no exterior e passe a atrair esses investimentos. Mas a lei só produz efeito com o decreto. Cada mês sem regulamentação é um mês de projetos parados e de investimentos que podem ir para outros países”, declarou. A Brasscom projeta US$ 92 bilhões em investimentos em data centers e equipamentos computacionais no Brasil até 2031, dos quais US$ 69 bilhões seriam destinados a equipamentos e US$ 23 bilhões à infraestrutura. Consumo de energia dos data centers pode chegar a 5,7 GW médios A expansão dos data centers também preocupa o setor elétrico pelo impacto esperado sobre a demanda de energia. Com base na segunda revisão quadrimestral da previsão de carga para 2026 a 2030, elaborada por ONS, Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE) e Câmara de Comercialização de Energia Elétrica (CCEE), o FASE estima que o consumo médio dos data centers passe de aproximadamente 0,3 GW em 2026 para 5,7 GW em 2030. Esse crescimento representaria quase um terço da expansão prevista para a carga do Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN) no período. Segundo as associações, a instalação de novos empreendimentos poderá impulsionar contratos de fornecimento de energia de longo prazo, projetos de geração e armazenamento e investimentos nas redes de transmissão e distribuição. O fórum também relaciona a expansão dos data centers à possibilidade de aproveitar parte da geração renovável atualmente limitada por restrições operacionais do sistema elétrico. A carta cita dados do ONS segundo os quais cerca de 20% da geração potencial eólica e solar vem sendo cortada desde 2025, com concentração dos cortes no Nordeste. Na avaliação das entidades, a entrada de grandes consumidores de energia pode contribuir para absorver parte desse excedente, desde que sejam consideradas as condições de acesso e a capacidade das redes. Energia de resíduos entra na discussão Entre as entidades signatárias, a ABREN defende a recuperação energética de resíduos como uma das alternativas para abastecer os futuros data centers. A associação destaca que o regime exige comprovação de suprimento integral por contratos ou geração própria a partir de fontes renováveis ou de baixa emissão. A carta do FASE menciona, entre as fontes elegíveis previstas na legislação citada pelo setor, a geração nuclear, biomassa, gás natural, biogás, biometano e recuperação energética de resíduos. Segundo a ABREN, as usinas que transformam resíduos em energia apresentam fator de capacidade entre 92% e 95%, característica que permitiria fornecer eletricidade de maneira contínua a instalações que operam 24 horas por dia. “A carta do FASE reforça o que a lei já prevê: a recuperação energética é uma fonte de baixo carbono apta a abastecer os data centers. Uma usina que trata o lixo das cidades gera energia o tempo todo, sem depender do clima, e é exatamente esse suprimento firme que cargas desse porte exigem. artigo.texto: EUROMETAL has joined 19 European industry associations and industriALL European Trade Union in calling for a broad extension of the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism to downstream products. The joint statement, published on Oct. 19 on the EUROMETAL website, comes ahead of trilogue negotiations between the European Parliament, Council and Commission scheduled for Oct. 20. The signatories are urging EU policymakers to reach an ambitious agreement that protects European industrial value chains, investment and employment. “Products covered by CBAM will benefit from a more level playing field, supporting their continued production in Europe,” the groups said. “Products left outside its scope will face growing risks of being replaced by imports or having their production relocated to third countries, where producers are not subject to equivalent carbon costs. This risk will become increasingly pronounced as free allowances under the EU Emissions Trading System are progressively phased out.” Under the current framework, CBAM initially focuses on carbon-intensive products including steel and aluminum, while free allocations under the EU Emissions Trading System are being phased out. Industry groups warn that manufacturers using these materials could face rising carbon-related costs without equivalent coverage for competing finished and semi-finished imports from outside the EU. The signatories said this could leave European producers at a competitive disadvantage and increase the risk of production being displaced by imports or relocated to countries with less stringent carbon-cost requirements. Such an outcome could also undermine investment in cleaner production within Europe, they said. The sectors identified as being exposed include construction, mobility, machinery, energy, packaging, household appliances and clean technologies, as well as other metal-intensive industries. For EUROMETAL, which represents European steel, tube and metal distribution companies, the competitiveness of downstream manufacturing is closely tied to the strength of the broader European steel value chain. The association has also been very vocal in the past about the importance of expanding CBAM to the downstream products. The association said the joint initiative supports a coordinated approach to ensuring that European-made products are not disadvantaged by carbon costs imposed under EU legislation. The signatories are calling for comprehensive downstream coverage in the final CBAM agreement, arguing that protecting European industrial production, investment and quality jobs is essential to the region’s economic security, prosperity and climate transition.W Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, assessed on Oct. 16 domestic hot-rolled coil in Northern Europe at €740/mt ex-works Ruhr and in Southern Europe at €740/mt ex-works Italy, both stable day over day. Platts assessed imported HRC in Northern Europe at €600/mt CIF Antwerp and in Southern Europe at €595/mt CIF Southern Europe, also both unchanged day over day. Author: Annalisa Villa

Sodium-ion batteries are not a universal replacement for lithium-ion batteries. Their suitability depends on energy density, discharge current, charging requirements, cycle life, temperature range, and total cost of ownership. For professional buyers, the priority is to identify the battery chemistry that best fits the target application and commercial requirements. 2. artigo.texto: Two clean energy companies, Vara Energia Ltd and HydroThermIA Inc. of Canada, have presented a technical and commercial framework to the Federal Government aimed at unlocking Nigeria’s estimated $3bn annual carbon finance potential. The proposal was presented during a technical session in Abuja with officials of the Mitigation Division of the Department of Climate Change at the Federal Ministry of Environment. In a statement issued by Vara Energia’s chief executive officer, Segun Aikulola, the companies said the framework was designed to support industrial decarbonisation, clean hydrogen production and the development of Nigeria’s carbon market. The initiative, according to the statement, aligns with the Federal Government’s climate commitments and the National Carbon Market Framework. The companies said the proposal builds on discussions at the National Green Growth Dialogue, organised by the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG) in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning under the theme, “From Commitments to Green Growth”. They also cited the government’s climate governance structures and emissions-reduction commitments as opportunities for developing carbon finance and clean energy projects. Under the proposed framework, the companies plan to deploy containerised technologies at industrial sites to address emissions from hard-to-abate sectors, including oil and gas operations. The proposed systems would capture gas currently being flared and convert it into hydrogen and electricity, potentially reducing emissions while providing an alternative source of energy for industrial operations. The framework also includes modular wastewater treatment systems integrated with hydrogen production, which the companies said could help industrial facilities secure water supplies and access lower-emission energy on-site. Speaking on the proposal, Vara Energia’s executive director of commercial and business development, Ochonogor Uche Zoe, said the initiative could reduce industrial carbon emissions while creating alternative revenue opportunities for Nigeria. He also stressed the importance of local technical integration and domestic manufacturing, saying Nigerian engineers should play a leading role in developing the clean energy sector. The assistant director and head of the Mitigation Division at the Department of Climate Change, Dr Asmau Jibril, said the partnership aligned with the government’s climate objectives and the National Green Growth Dialogue. According to the companies, the proposed technologies could reduce operating costs for heavy industries and upstream oil and gas operators by lowering dependence on diesel and unreliable grid electricity. Vara Energia’s deputy chief executive officer, Victor Ntofon, said the initiative could attract foreign exchange through verified carbon credit revenues, create jobs and improve access to international climate finance, including green climate funds. The companies also projected that the development of domestic clean hydrogen production could position Nigeria to supply hydrogen and ammonia to regional and international markets. They called on the Presidency, the National Council on Climate Change and the Federal Ministry of Environment to support the proposed framework, while urging manufacturers and energy companies to explore participation in the initiative. The companies said they remained committed to supporting Nigeria’s industrial decarbonisation objectives through technology deployment, local capacity development and investment in cleaner energy systems. artigo.texto: Funding data centers is drying up, electricity demand skyrockets Capital markets are closing out AI data centers while 15 GW of power is on the waiting list. What is realistic? Published on October 26, 2026 Team IO+ selects and features the most important news stories on innovation and technology, carefully curated by our editors. The Dutch data center sector is facing a double crisis: funding is drying up, while the waiting list for power connections is skyrocketing to 15 GW—enough to supply power to every household in the Netherlands. Grid operators warn that a third of these requests come from data centers, but in most cases these are not concrete plans, but rather reservations made to keep options open. The combination of closed capital markets, uncertain demand, and an overloaded power grid threatens to turn the AI boom into a bust. AI-driven growth hits a wall In recent years, demand for data centers has skyrocketed: neoclouds, which specialize in AI computing power, had already contracted 420 MW of colocation capacity in Europe in the first half of 2026—nearly five times as much as in the same period of 2025. Two-thirds of this growth is taking place in the Scandinavian region, where cheap, renewable energy is available and average temperatures are low. Yet this expansion is not without risks. Real estate advisor CBRE warns that the rapid growth is putting pressure on power grids and the availability of green energy. Despite strong demand for AI computing power, the market remains skeptical about the financial viability of these projects. Elon Musk recently emphasized that most of the more than 200 neo-cloud providers will not survive on their own. Capital markets are closing the door on high-risk projects By 2026, the financing market for data centers will be virtually closed to companies without solid, independent revenue streams outside of AI infrastructure. Musk and venture capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya point out the risks of debt financing and the need for better capital structures. Jensen Huang of Nvidia confirms this: the lack of working capital is the biggest bottleneck for neoclouds, while the scale of capital required exceeds current financing options. The AI infrastructure market is facing delays in project pipelines, which could lead to underutilization of expensive hardware by 2027. Analysts such as Dauvin Peterson of 22V Research do see momentum in demand for AI infrastructure through 2027, but emphasize the risks of insufficient capital. 15 GW on the waiting list: how realistic are these plans? In the Netherlands, 15 GW of power requests are on the waiting list, a third of which come from data centers. This capacity is enough to supply power to nearly all 8.5 million Dutch households. However, most of the demand is not for concrete plans but rather a strategic reservation. Stijn Grove of the Dutch Data Center Association explained to the NOS that companies are applying early and in large numbers to secure a spot in line, with wait times of about ten years. Grid operators such as Alliander emphasize that the waiting list of 15,500 applicants in 2026 says little about actual implementation. The government is being called upon to make tough decisions about where and how many data centers will be allowed to be built, with clear conditions regarding energy, the environment, and water usage. Financial risks and unclear demand forecasts The financing crisis in the data center sector threatens to lead to a harsh restructuring. Musk warns that of the more than 200 neo-clouds, only a few will survive. CoreWeave has approximately $50 billion in debt, Nscale has $24 billion in committed purchases, and Amsterdam-based Nebius has $10 billion in convertible debt. Gartner expects that more than 80% of neo-clouds will no longer operate independently by 2030. The market for used GPUs could come under pressure if financially weak neoclouds are forced to sell assets, which could trigger a negative chain reaction. In 2027, the sector faces a crucial test: project delays and insufficient revenue could lead to “stranded compute,” where expensive hardware fails to deliver a sufficient return on investment. Grid operators must anticipate uncertainty Grid operators in the Netherlands, such as Alliander and TenneT, face an impossible task: investing in grid expansion while actual demand remains unclear. The costs of grid expansion are estimated at over €200 billion through 2040, which will significantly increase household energy bills in the coming years. The government is being called upon to establish clear and uniform conditions for data centers, but ultimate control must remain at the regional level. State Secretaries Willemijn Aerdts and Jo-Annes de Bat acknowledge the need for better management of the scarcity of space and electricity, but no concrete policy has been established yet. Alliander advocates for more efficient electricity consumption by data centers, for example through the use of batteries or by supplying residual heat to homes.

artigo.texto: Experimentos de longa duração no interior paulista indicam que a recuperação de pastagens degradadas pode elevar a produtividade e aumentar o armazenamento de carbono no solo. A intensificação moderada — com correção da acidez, fertilizantes e quantidade equilibrada de animais — apresentou bons resultados sem exigir tecnologias inacessíveis. A pesquisa também desenvolveu formas mais simples e baratas de medir o carbono retido, o que pode facilitar o acesso de produtores ao mercado de créditos de carbono. Os estudos integram o projeto temático “Entendendo sistemas intensificados e integrados de produção: do mundo quântico à agricultura de baixa emissão de carbono”, apoiado pela Fapesp e coordenado por Ladislau Martin Neto, pesquisador da Embrapa Instrumentação. Os pesquisadores compararam desde pastagens degradadas, sem adubação e com pastejo contínuo, até sistemas com diferentes níveis de intervenção, incluindo áreas irrigadas, com altas doses de nitrogênio e maior concentração de animais. Em uma área de intensificação moderada, o carbono armazenado no primeiro metro de solo subiu de 102 para 162 toneladas por hectare entre 2011 e 2020. O aumento médio foi de aproximadamente duas toneladas por hectare ao ano em relação à pastagem degradada. Segundo Martin Neto, análises indicaram que uma parcela importante do carbono adicional veio da própria forrageira cultivada no local. A pesquisadora Patrícia Perondi Anchão Oliveira, líder do experimento, ressaltou que o modelo combina capins adaptados ao clima brasileiro com gado de origem indiana, como o nelore. Após mais de duas décadas de manejo, a pastagem apresentou 148 toneladas de carbono por hectare na forma de matéria orgânica associada aos minerais do solo, ante 92 toneladas na área degradada. A pesquisa mostra que é possível recuperar solos já convertidos para a pecuária e ampliar sua capacidade de armazenar carbono sem avançar sobre a vegetação nativa. Os resultados foram publicados na revista Geoderma e apontam a possibilidade de remunerar produtores pelo carbono adicional, desde que seja possível comprovar quanto foi incorporado e permanece no solo. Para investigar essa permanência, a equipe analisou as interações entre matéria orgânica e minerais. Parte da matéria orgânica pode ser decomposta por microrganismos e liberar carbono como CO₂; outra parte se associa a argilas e óxidos de ferro e alumínio, o que dificulta sua decomposição. Os pesquisadores usaram a espectrometria de massa de íons secundários (NanoSIMS), na Universidade Técnica de Munique, na Alemanha, com apoio da Fapesp e durante estágio de Lucas Raimundo Bento. A técnica produz mapas químicos em escala nanométrica. As análises mostraram que as manchas de matéria orgânica cobriam, no máximo, cerca de 3% da superfície mineral observada na camada superficial. Para Martin Neto, isso indica que a entrada de compostos orgânicos e a atividade dos microrganismos são decisivas e que ainda há superfície mineral disponível para novas associações. O manejo também favorece a fertilidade: na camada de até 5 centímetros, a capacidade de troca catiônica da pastagem bem manejada foi aproximadamente 250% superior à da degradada. Outro estudo, publicado em Soil & Tillage Research, comparou combinações de adubação nitrogenada, irrigação e lotação animal.

artigo.texto: BYD has reached a major milestone in commercial vehicle production, rolling out its 150,000th new energy commercial vehicle at its manufacturing facility in Huai’an, Jiangsu province, China. The milestone vehicle is the Q3 battery-electric semi-truck, highlighting the automaker’s growing ambitions in heavy-duty electric transport. The achievement comes as BYD shifts more attention toward electric trucks, particularly vehicles designed for long-distance freight operations. While the Chinese automaker is widely known for its electric passenger cars and battery technology, its commercial vehicle business is becoming an increasingly important part of its expansion strategy. According to CNEVPost, the milestone vehicle left the production line on October 9, marking 18 years of development in BYD’s commercial new energy vehicle business. The BYD Q3 is designed for demanding heavy-duty transport applications, combining a large battery pack, powerful electric motors and fast-charging capability. The electric semi-truck features a commercial-vehicle version of BYD’s Blade Battery technology, using lithium iron phosphate (LFP) chemistry. Its battery capacity is reported at up to 600 kWh, while the dual-motor powertrain delivers a peak output of 600 kW, equivalent to approximately 805 horsepower. That level of power makes the Q3 a notable entry in the growing market for battery-electric heavy-duty trucks. The truck is also reported to support a gross combined vehicle weight of approximately 108,000 pounds, or around 49 metric tons. With a fully charged battery, its reported range reaches approximately 325 kilometers (202 miles), although actual range will depend on payload, road conditions, weather and driving patterns. For operators running demanding freight routes, charging speed can be just as important as battery capacity. The Q3 supports dual-gun DC fast charging, with a reported charging time of around 30 minutes to increase the battery’s state of charge from 20% to 80%. These specifications are intended to help electric trucks handle intensive commercial operations while reducing dependence on diesel fuel. BYD Commercial EV Sales Continue to Grow BYD’s production milestone arrives as its commercial new energy vehicle sales show strong growth in 2026. The company sold 6,848 commercial NEVs in September, an increase of 113.33% compared with the same month in 2025. Sales during the first nine months of 2026 reached 53,032 vehicles, up 28.46% year over year. The figures are particularly notable because BYD’s overall new energy vehicle sales moved in the opposite direction during the same period. The automaker sold approximately 3.13 million passenger and commercial new energy vehicles in the first nine months of 2026, down 3.94% from a year earlier. This contrast suggests that commercial vehicles are becoming an important growth area for BYD as it looks beyond the highly competitive passenger EV market. However, the 150,000-vehicle milestone represents cumulative commercial NEV production, not the number of trucks produced in 2026 alone. BYD’s commercial vehicle portfolio includes multiple vehicle types and powertrains, rather than exclusively heavy-duty battery-electric trucks. BYD’s commercial vehicle business began with electric city buses before gradually expanding into other applications. The company started truck research and development in 2012, building a portfolio that now covers urban delivery vehicles, light-duty trucks, cold-chain logistics vehicles and heavy-duty trucks. Its commercial lineup includes both battery-electric and hybrid models. In 2025, production of BYD’s T5 light-duty truck reached 10,000 units, while the T4 mini truck was introduced for international markets. The expansion reflects a broader effort to apply BYD’s battery, electric motor and electronic control technologies to commercial transportation. Rather than relying solely on passenger cars, the company is targeting sectors where electrification could help reduce fuel costs and emissions across large vehicle fleets. Heavy-duty trucks are a particularly important opportunity, although their adoption depends on factors such as purchase prices, charging infrastructure, battery capacity, vehicle utilization and the availability of suitable charging stops along freight routes. International Expansion Becomes a Bigger Priority BYD says its commercial vehicle business has expanded into more than 70 countries and regions. Trucks are increasingly central to its international growth plans as the company seeks opportunities beyond its established electric bus business. At IAA Transportation 2026 in Hanover, Germany, BYD presented an integrated zero-carbon logistics solution combining commercial vehicles with charging infrastructure, fleet management and maintenance services. The strategy goes beyond selling electric trucks. Commercial operators need dependable charging access, vehicle servicing and fleet-management systems to keep vehicles working efficiently and control operating costs. By combining vehicles with supporting services, BYD aims to offer fleet operators a more complete electrification package. This could become especially important for businesses managing multiple trucks across regional distribution networks and long-distance routes. International expansion will also require BYD to address local regulations, service coverage, charging standards and the specific operating requirements of different markets.

artigo.texto: A instalação de data centers no Rio Grande do Norte pode ampliar o aproveitamento do potencial energético do estado e atrair investimentos em tecnologia, indústria e geração de empregos. O tema esteve em debate na Data Center Conference, realizada nesta sexta-feira (23), na Casa da Indústria, em Natal. Na abertura do evento, o presidente da Federação das Indústrias do Rio Grande do Norte (FIERN), Roberto Serquiz, destacou a disponibilidade de fontes renováveis, como o vento e o sol, mas alertou que limitações na transmissão de energia e cortes na geração dificultam o aproveitamento desse potencial. “Essas condições por si só não garantem investimentos. Em função de restrições na transmissão e dos cortes de geração, passamos a conviver com uma realidade que representa desperdício de oportunidades”, afirmou. Serquiz defendeu que o estado avance na transformação da energia renovável em atividade econômica. “Somos um estado de energia verde e precisamos dar o próximo passo, que é transformar energia em indústria, tecnologia, investimentos, empregos e desenvolvimento”, declarou. FIERN destaca segurança jurídica e ambiente regulatório O presidente da Federação também ressaltou a importância de modernizar as regras ambientais e regulatórias para atrair empreendimentos. Segundo ele, os investidores precisam de segurança jurídica, previsibilidade e infraestrutura adequada. Serquiz afirmou que a FIERN mantém diálogo com o Governo do Estado para contribuir com a construção de um ambiente regulatório mais moderno e competitivo. Entre os temas discutidos estão resoluções voltadas ao hidrogênio, às baterias e aos data centers. Projetos reforçam potencial da economia digital no RN Durante o evento, Serquiz citou iniciativas que, segundo ele, demonstram oportunidades para ampliar a economia digital e atrair investimentos ao Rio Grande do Norte. Entre os exemplos mencionados estão projetos de investimento da Brasil Green Energy, em Areia Branca, e da Atlântico, em São Gonçalo do Amarante. Ele também destacou a parceria entre o Serviço Nacional de Aprendizagem Industrial do Rio Grande do Norte (SENAI-RN) e a Petrobras para instalar uma planta-piloto de hidrogênio e amônia verdes em Alto do Rodrigues. Setor de data centers aponta necessidade de previsibilidade O vice-presidente da Associação Brasileira de Data Centers (ABDC), Luis Tossi, também participou da conferência. Ele ressaltou a importância do apoio do setor produtivo para desenvolver a cadeia de data centers no estado. “Os investidores precisam de segurança jurídica para colocar os empreendimentos em operação o mais rápido possível. Vejo que o Rio Grande do Norte tem avançado para criar um ambiente favorável para esses investimentos”, afirmou. Evento debate infraestrutura digital e atração de investimentos A Data Center Conference reuniu profissionais, empresas, empresários e especialistas para discutir tendências e oportunidades relacionadas à infraestrutura digital no Brasil e no mundo. A programação abordou temas como energia, conectividade, refrigeração, inteligência artificial, computação em nuvem, eficiência operacional, sustentabilidade, regulamentação, financiamento e atração de investimentos. artigo.texto: Vantage data center plan draws questions ahead of Oregon vote Vote on Issue 25 decides whether to block construction of data center OREGON, Ohio (WTVG) - Vantage Data Centers held an open house Sunday at Clay High School, giving residents a chance to ask questions about its proposed $1 billion data center ahead of a vote on the project next week. Resident group opposes project United Neighbors of Oregon, a resident-led group, has spent the past few months working to prevent construction of the data center off Corduroy and Wynn roads. “We didn’t come this far to only come this far,” said Laura Davis, a volunteer with United Neighbors of Oregon. “They’re spending monies, thousands, hundreds of thousands of dollars on this campaign to try and buy their way into Oregon. But I keep saying Oregon is not for sale,” Davis said. Davis said she is concerned about the wetlands and the people who live near the proposed site. Vantage addresses energy, water questions Misty Allen, vice president of public policy for North America at Vantage Data Centers, said residents have raised questions about the project. “People want to understand the, where’s the energy coming from? How will that affect their energy rates? What about water use? And how is the data center going to use water?” Allen said. Allen said Vantage will purchase its own power and cover the necessary infrastructure costs. “When it comes to water use, we’re not going to use any more water than, say, a typical medium commercial office building. And we use closed loop water for chilling of the data center,” Allen said. Allen said the facility would use 22,000 gallons of water a day, the same amount used by 65 homes. She said Vantage checked with the city’s water plant and was told it has the ability to service that need. Open house draws mixed reaction Davis said she remains unconvinced. “They had some people in there trying to convince other people that this is the right thing for Oregon. But we were in there telling people, this is not the right thing for Oregon,” Davis said. Davis said Allen and Vantage staff gave her one answer she liked. “If we win this vote, they will pull out,” Davis said. “Obviously we would have to have conversations with city council and the folks who have been working on this development. But certainly, if the community doesn’t want us here, we’ll have to seriously consider not being here,” Allen said. What’s on the ballot Davis said the ballot language is confusing residents. Voting yes on Issue 25 supports amending the city charter to prohibit construction of the data center. Voting no on the issue opposes blocking the construction. artigo.texto: A data center under construction in South Brunswick is drawing environmental concerns from residents who said they only recently learned about the project, more than a year after local officials approved it. The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) is currently reviewing an application from Sentinel Data Centers to install several backup diesel generators at the former Princeton Nurseries property on Rt-1. The agency has opened a public comment period as part of its permitting process. Many residents said they didn't become aware of the project until the state began to seek public input on the generator permits. However, the proposed data center received approval from the South Brunswick Planning Board in May 2025. "It's only been in the last month, maybe a little bit longer than that that people have truly been aware of it and been able to raise their voices," said Kingston resident Karin Gillespie. "If there is an opportunity to impact the diesel generators and think about some kind of an alternative to that, that would be great." The property is situated on the border of several towns including South Brunswick, Kingston and Princeton. “This is about more than one data center. It is about the health of our families, the protection of our air and water and the long-term future of our communities,” said Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman. “Pollution does not stop at municipal borders. The impacts of this project will extend far beyond South Brunswick, threatening the health and quality of life of residents across the surrounding communities." Though the approval for the data center was granted by the South Brunswick Planning Board, Princeton Mayor Mark Freda and the city council released a statement at the beginning of October in opposition of the backup generators. "When running, these generators will undoubtedly send emissions across municipal boundaries, often negatively affecting air quality and public health in Princeton’s residential neighborhoods and at two of our elementary schools. We urge DEP to deny the air permit application for the center in its present form," the statement said. The two candidates running to replace Coleman in November are also speaking out on the data center and the potential impacts for nearby residents. Adam Hamawy, the Democratic candidate running to represent New Jersey's 12th district said in a statement, "Our communities deserve the right to decide their own future, not have it dictated by billionaires and corporate developers. The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection has a responsibility to protect public health, and that starts with denying this air permit.” His Republican challenger, Gregg Mele, also spoke to News 12 about the planned data center. “Residents deserve a complete, independently reviewed accounting of generator emissions, noise, water demand, and electricity infrastructure costs—including all planned phases," Mele said. "Developers should pay the infrastructure costs they create, and protections for neighboring communities must be enforceable." While the current state review is focused on the backup generators, some residents continue to call for the entire project to be reconsidered. "Maybe we can do what so many other communities have done. Maybe we can get them to not have this data center," said South Brunswick resident Janice Gossman. "A lot of people say it's too late. We have to try." For some neighbors, the debate is personal. Michael Van Pelt, who lives down the road from the site of the data center, said he worries about how the facility could impact his family, including his son, who has autism. "My son is very sensitive to sound," Van Pelt said. "His special education program is magnificent. His teachers are wonderful and if he loses that, I don't know what we're going to do."

artigo.texto: A Vertiv anunciou o lançamento do SmartAisle 3, uma solução modular para data centers que integra sistemas de alimentação ininterrupta (UPS), gerenciamento térmico, distribuição de energia, monitoramento e segurança física. Disponível no Brasil e em outros seis países da América do Sul, a plataforma pode ser configurada para suportar até 120 kW de carga total de TI. CONTEÚDO RELACIONADO – Vertiv compra empresa europeia para ampliar serviços de refrigeração líquida A solução incorpora recursos de inteligência artificial (IA) e autoaprendizagem para monitorar as condições operacionais e ajustar a temperatura conforme o ambiente. Segundo a fabricante, essas funcionalidades podem proporcionar economia de energia de até 20% em comparação com sistemas sem recursos de IA, desde que mantidas as condições operacionais estabelecidas para a infraestrutura. O SmartAisle 3 foi desenvolvido para atender à demanda por expansão e modernização de data centers, com uma arquitetura que reúne diferentes componentes de infraestrutura em um sistema modular. A proposta é simplificar a implantação e o gerenciamento operacional, reduzindo a complexidade de integração entre os equipamentos. “Aplicações intensivas em dados estão levando mais organizações a avaliar como podem expandir ou modernizar sua infraestrutura sem adicionar complexidade operacional desnecessária”, afirmou Felipe Vasco, diretor de Aplicações de Tecnologia da Vertiv LATAM. A arquitetura inclui um sistema flexível de distribuição elétrica por barramento, projetado para simplificar a instalação e reduzir a necessidade de cabeamento no local. A solução também conta com cabeamento integrado, sensores instalados nas partes frontal e traseira dos racks e monitoramento centralizado de variáveis como temperatura, umidade e status das portas. O sistema dispõe de um painel de controle com tela sensível ao toque de 15 polegadas, com opção de atualização para uma tela local de 95 polegadas instalada na porta. O recurso permite acompanhar as condições operacionais e auxilia na identificação e resolução de problemas. De acordo com a Vertiv, a integração dos sistemas de monitoramento e controle ambiental pode contribuir para reduzir em até 75% o ciclo de falhas operacionais. A empresa também informa que os principais componentes são integrados e testados em fábrica antes da instalação no cliente. O SmartAisle 3 integra o portfólio de soluções modulares da Vertiv e pode ser utilizado em ambientes de bancos e serviços financeiros, governo, educação e infraestrutura de edge computing, entre outros setores que demandam sistemas integrados de energia, refrigeração e monitoramento. artigo.texto: Patna: Bihar is preparing to introduce specialised green energy courses in its higher education institutions, aiming to equip students with skills in renewable energy, electric vehicles, battery technology and other emerging sustainable technologies. The state’s Higher Education Department has prepared a proposal to introduce these programmes in line with the National Education Policy (NEP). The initiative is intended to align higher education with the growing demand for skilled professionals in the green energy sector. According to the proposal, the courses have been designed with assistance from experts from the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) and National Institutes of Technology (NITs), with an emphasis on industry requirements, research and practical knowledge. Undergraduate and Postgraduate Programmes Proposed The proposed framework includes both undergraduate and postgraduate degree programmes. Students will have the opportunity to study energy management, carbon trading and sustainable business models, alongside technical subjects related to clean energy. The department has also referred to University Grants Commission (UGC) guidelines and directed that the necessary preparations be made to introduce the courses. A separate department dedicated to green energy studies is also being proposed at universities. EVs, Solar Power and Battery Technology Among Key Subjects The proposed curriculum will cover a range of emerging fields, including: - Renewable energy and solar power - Wind energy management - Green hydrogen technology - Electric vehicle (EV) technology - Battery technology and advanced battery management - EV charging infrastructure - Carbon accounting and auditing - Green corporate practices and sustainable business models These subjects are expected to help students develop expertise in technologies and practices associated with the transition towards cleaner energy. Research to Receive Special Attention The proposed initiative also aims to encourage teachers and students to undertake research in green energy and sustainability. By introducing specialised programmes, Bihar’s universities could expand opportunities for academic research while preparing students for changing industry requirements. Potential Career Opportunities in the Green Energy Sector The proposed courses could help students pursue careers in renewable energy management, solar and wind power projects, electric mobility, battery systems, EV charging infrastructure, carbon auditing and sustainability consulting. However, the programmes are currently at the proposal and preparation stage. Details regarding participating universities, admission procedures, course fees and the launch schedule have not yet been specified in the supplied information.

artigo.texto: Samsung — o maior diferencial hoje para data centers que pagam mais por HBM não é só tecnologia, mas a previsibilidade da entrega: clientes premium estariam aceitando pagar até 25% a mais pela garantia de fornecimento e pelos ganhos de rendimento que a empresa vem reportando. Preço e comparação: quanto custa um HBM no mercado A cotação atribuída à Samsung para HBM aparece em $4,50 por unidade, frente a $4,00 para Micron e uma faixa de $3,60–$3,80 para SK hynix. Esse spread equivale a um prêmio de até 25% sobre o preço dos concorrentes. A diferença de preço ganha sentido quando se considera que a HBM4 da Samsung é mencionada como posicionada na faixa média-alta dos US$4, tornando-a até três vezes mais cara que a referência anterior de HBM3E em cotações comparativas. A Samsung tem uma cotação de $4,50 para HBM, contra $4,00 da Micron e $3,60–$3,80 da SK hynix, refletindo um prêmio ligado à capacidade de fornecer volumes estáveis e avanços na produção de HBM4. Vantagens industriais por trás do prêmio A capacidade da Samsung de aliar sua divisão de foundry e múltiplos nós avançados, como um 4nm maduro, tem sido apontada como fator que reduz defeitos e eleva a utilidade industrial, favorecendo yields superiores durante a produção de HBM4. Relatos de rendimento em torno de 80% para HBM4 e a possibilidade de conciliar recursos entre memória e chips não relacionados à memória são citados como razões práticas para a empresa manter preços mais altos, atraindo clientes sensíveis a risco de falta de oferta. O que você acha? Você considera justificável que data centers paguem um prêmio por garantia de fornecimento e yields mais altos? Para acompanhar mais, acesse nossa editoria. Perguntas Frequentes Por que a Samsung está cobrando até 25% a mais por HBM para data centers? A Samsung está cobrando até 25% a mais por HBM porque sua capacidade de produção e estabilidade de suprimento oferecem menos risco aos data centers, com cotações citadas em $4,50 frente a $4,00 da Micron e $3,60–$3,80 da SK hynix. Essa diferença reflete preferência por continuidade de entregas e rendimentos superiores. O que torna a HBM4 da Samsung mais cara que a HBM3E? A HBM4 da Samsung aparece posicionada na faixa média-alta dos US$4, o que a deixa cerca de três vezes mais cara que a referência de HBM3E citada. Essa precificação incorpora melhorias de rendimento (relatos de até 80%) e custos de processo em nós avançados, além da integração com sua foundry. Como essa diferença de preço afeta os data centers na prática? A diferença de preço impacta o custo total de servidores e aceleradores: data centers que priorizam disponibilidade e performance podem optar por pagar $4,50 por HBM para reduzir risco de falta, enquanto outros podem escolher fornecedores mais baratos, como Micron a $4,00, dependendo de capex e estratégia de suprimento. © Diário da Mídia · Conteúdo protegido por direitos autorais — reprodução ou cópia proibida sem autorização. artigo.texto: Morro Bay City Council plans to ban battery storage plants October 25, 2026 By KAREN VELIE After a more than four-year battle, the Morro Bay City Council is planning to pass an ordinance on Tuesday in an attempt to ban battery storage plants that provide power to the state’s electric grid. Vistra Energy, a Texas-based energy company, has plans to construct and operate a 600 megawatt battery storage facility on approximately 24 acres of a roughly 70-acre site. However, residents, concerned the facility would endanger the public while negatively impacting tourism and the fishing industry, have battled against the proposed project for years. Legislation passed in 2022 allows applicants to skip local approvals. However, it requires approvals from both the California Energy Commission and the Coastal Commission. So, even if the California Energy Commission green-lights the battery storage plant, it would still need approval from the California Coastal Commission, which has criticized the project. In an Aug. 2, 2024 letter regarding Vistra Energy’s proposed project, the Coastal Commission outlined serious issues about the location of the project. In summary, they stated that the future hazards of flooding and sea level rise and the impact on the environmentally sensitive habitat area are acute. In the 2024 election, Morro Bay, residents largely supported a measure requiring voter approval for changes to some zoning on the waterfront. Vistra Energy decided to seek state approval while bypassing the city’s consideration shortly before the November election. On Jan. 28, 2025, the Morro Bay City Council voted for an urgency ordinance to temporarily halt the proposed battery storage project. The urgency ordinance, which was extended once, is set to expire on Jan. 28, 2027. Even if the city council enacts an ordinance banning battery storage plants in the city, Vistra Energy could ask the state to override the ordinance and permit the project. However, a large amount of the funding for the battery storage facility is slated to be provided through the Inflation Reduction Act, which included $369 billion in subsidies for renewable energy. “The Inflation Reduction Act is anticipated to provide the opportunity to realize material benefits to Vistra with respect to its renewables and energy storage projects, as well as provide strong price support via the nuclear production tax credit for its nuclear facilities, including those acquired through the Energy Harbor transaction,” Vistra Energy said in a first quarter 2024 press release. However, the Trump administration and the Republican-led Congress have frozen, and rolled back major provisions of the Inflation Reduction Act. Without subsidies and tax credits, it is unlikely Vistra Energy will move forward with its plan for battery storage in Morro Bay. artigo.texto: Davidson County commissioners to consider 4-month moratorium on data center development Davidson County commissioners are holding a public hearing about a proposed four-month pause on data center development to address zoning and infrastructure concerns. Davidson County commissioners to consider 4-month moratorium on data center development Davidson County commissioners are holding a public hearing about a proposed four-month pause on data center development to address zoning and infrastructure concerns. Davidson County commissioners are considering a four-month moratorium on data center development to give leaders time to evaluate regulations and address concerns about infrastructure and environmental impact. In August, commissioners rejected a proposal for a six-month moratorium. The new six-page proposal outlines the reasons for the 4-month pause, citing concerns local and national about data centers’ electricity use, water supply issues, heat production and noise pollution. Get the latest news stories of interest by clicking here Keep up with the latest news and weather by downloading the WXII app here. The document also states that the county’s zoning ordinance "has no current means to regulate the siting, construction, and operation of data centers in a direct and meaningful way." It further explains that state law prevents commissioners from making certain sweeping changes to the zoning ordinance. The proposal outlines a plan for the moratorium. During the first two months, county leaders would consult experts about data centers, review the county’s land and utilities, and visit nearby data centers. In the final two months, they would consider potential zoning changes and possibly propose rules to regulate data center development. Watch: NOWCAST streaming newscasts Members of the public can share their thoughts on the proposed moratorium during a public hearing at the Davidson County Board of Commissioners meeting, which begins at 6 p.m. Monday. The meeting will be held in the meeting room on the fourth floor of the Davidson County Governmental Center on Greensboro Street in Lexington. artigo.texto: The real test of India’s carbon market is getting the price right In today’s geopolitical and trade landscape, a credible domestic carbon price is not just climate policy, but an industrial strategy as well Visual Credits: Arkatapa Basu India is putting a national price on industrial carbon for the first time. Under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), baselines and final targets have been notified for seven energy-intensive sectors covering roughly 490 industrial emitters. The world’s sixth largest economy is joining a global shift: emissions trading systems now cover about 28% of the world's emissions and have raised more than $100 billion a year through auction revenues and other forms of carbon pricing. The debate so far was about whether India should have a carbon market. That is now settled. The harder one is whether the market India builds will actually work. A new report from the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA) and Environmental Defense Fund (EDF), examines precisely that, drawing on the experiences from carbon markets in the EU, South Korea, China and the state of California in the US. The report’s central conclusion is that getting the price signal right in the early years will be critical in building confidence and credibility in the market over time. One should start with why the price matters at all. The whole purpose of a carbon market is to incentivise emission reductions. International assessments estimate that a single tonne of carbon dioxide inflicts around $140-380 (₹13,000-₹36,000) of damage on society — through worse health, lower farm yields and harsher weather. An unregulated emitter pays none of it. A carbon market exists to close that gap. If the price it produces is weak, the gap stays open, and the market becomes less effective. India's carbon market design is deliberate. Rather than setting a single absolute ceiling on emissions, as Europe does, it has chosen an intensity-based system in which firms are judged on emissions per tonne of output, not against a national cap. That lets an economy growing at 6.6% to 6.8% a year keep expanding without the carbon limit constraining production levels. Also Read: Can biochar be India’s missing link to carbon capture? It is the right instrument for a country that still has to industrialise. Underpinning all of this, credits are issued only after a firm's performance is verified. While this design has much to commend it, it also raises a challenge that merits a wider conversation. A fine balance In an intensity-based market, economic growth can create both buyers and sellers of credits. Firms that outperform their emissions-intensity targets generate credits that they can sell, while firms that fall short must buy them. The balance between supply and demand therefore depends on how ambitious the targets are and which firms are expanding production. Carbon scarcity does not emerge automatically; it is created through policy design. Set the benchmarks too generously, and the market fills with cheap credits that reward business-as-usual and send little signal to invest in cleaner technologies. Set them too tightly, and firms face costs they may not yet be able to absorb. This is not a theoretical worry. Historical experience offers a useful lesson. Europe's carbon market, for example, struggled with low carbon prices in its initial phases, prompting a series of reforms to strengthen the market. It issued too many permits, prices fell close to zero, and for the better part of a decade, the market did little to cut emissions. Asia has similar stories: in their early phases, carbon prices sat below $10 in South Korea and between $6-$8 in China, drifting up to only around $14 by late 2024 — numbers set more by administrative design than by real scarcity. The lesson is blunt: a carbon market is only as strong as the scarcity built into it. There is a hard commercial reason to get this right, too. From 2026, the EU's carbon border tax will require importers of steel, aluminum and other goods to pay for the emissions embedded in them, in line with EU carbon prices. If India does not price its own industrial carbon credibly, that bill will simply be collected in Brussels. In today’s geopolitical and trade landscape, a credible domestic carbon price is not just climate policy, but an industrial strategy as well. Learning curve The good news is that India can choose not to repeat these mistakes. It also starts with a foundation: for more than a decade, the Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme has familiarised energy-intensive industries with compliance obligations, third-party verification, and tradable certificates. While a carbon market is a different instrument, these experiences provide a valuable starting point. Three priorities stand out. The first is a predictable tightening path. A blast furnace or a cement kiln locks in emissions for 15 to 30 years. No firm will price carbon into a thirty-year decision unless it believes the targets will tighten steadily and will not be quietly relaxed the moment industry pushes back. Europe, having learned the hard way, now follows a predictable annual reduction in the number of emission allowances available to the market. The rate of decline increased from 1.7% to 2.2% from 2021 onwards, steadily tightening supply and strengthening the carbon price signal. Publishing a clear, long-term trajectory of this kind is the single most powerful signal the government can send. Also Read: What can India’s bilateral carbon credit deals learn from the centralised global carbon market? The second is a stability mechanism built in from the outset. Rather than responding to challenges after they arise, India can strengthen market confidence by embedding appropriate safeguards from the outset. artigo.texto: S&P Global Ratings launches interactive North America data center dashboard New dashboard offers dynamic view of rated data center universe across Project Finance, Corporates, and Structured Finance Asset Backed Securities - Covers 32 digital infrastructure transactions totaling $105.3 billion in debt issuance - Includes market overview, issuer tear sheets and comparatives, and state-level capacity insights NEW YORK , Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- S&P Global Ratings, the world's leading provider of independent credit ratings, today launched a new interactive dashboard providing a dynamic view of its rated North American data center universe across Project Finance, and Corporates, and Structured Finance asset-backed securities (SF ABS). The dashboard brings together information across these three areas, providing an overview of the market, issuer tear sheets and comparatives, and insights into states where capacity is being leased. It accompanies S&P Global Ratings' fourth-quarter roundup, "North America Data Center Roundup: Fourth-Quarter 2026," published Oct. 16, 2026. "Our rated North American data center universe now spans 32 digital infrastructure transactions and $105.3 billion in debt issuance across project finance, structured finance ABS, and corporates," said Vishal Merani, Managing Director and Global Digital Infrastructure Team Leader, S&P Global Ratings. "Bringing this information together in an interactive format provides a more comprehensive view of our rated data center universe as demand continues to grow." said Dhaval Shah, Director, S&P Global Ratings. Key takeaways from the fourth-quarter roundup: - S&P Global Ratings currently rates 32 digital infrastructure transactions in North America across Project Finance (PF), Corporates, and Structured Finance asset-backed securities (SF ABS). The majority are SF ABS issuers (50%), followed by PF issuers (28%) and Corporates (22%), based on the number of issuers. - Total debt issuance across rated issuers reaches $105.3 billion , with PF accounting for 58.3%, SF ABS for 26.4%, and Corporates for 15.3%. - The rated transactions are backed by 143 properties with approximately 8.7 gigawatts of capacity available to tenants in North America . - S&P Global Ratings expects data center demand to remain strong in the foreseeable future, driven by exponential data growth, cloud migration, and the ongoing digitization of the global economy. - S&P Global Ratings believes power constraints, permitting challenges, public pushback and regulatory responses could delay or constrain new data center development. Access the interactive North America data center dashboard here. This report does not constitute a rating action. artigo.texto: Resumo - BofA projeta investimento global de US$1 trilhão em data centers em 2026 - Aporte deve mais que dobrar e chegar a US$2,1 trilhões até 2028 - Mercado avaliado em US$275 bi em 2022 pode somar US$2,93 tri até 2030 - Inteligência artificial é apontada como motor da expansão do setor - Construção custa cerca de US$49 milhões por megawatt, estima a corretora Segundo projeção da BofA Global Research divulgada nesta sexta-feira (23), os aportes mundiais em centrais de processamento de dados devem bater US$1 trilhão em 2026 e, até 2028, superar o dobro desse valor, atingindo US$2,1 trilhões. Na visão da corretora, a inteligência artificial é o principal motor por trás dessa aceleração. Segundo o BofA, os data centers movimentaram US$275 bilhões em 2022 e esse valor pode chegar a US$2,93 trilhões até 2030. Nesse período, puxado pela procura associada à IA, o setor avançaria a uma taxa composta anual (CAGR) de 37% entre 2025 e 2030. Entre os maiores beneficiados dessa corrida estão os fabricantes de chips e os desenvolvedores de servidores, especialmente no mercado norte-americano. Quanto custa erguer um data center O BofA calcula que a construção de uma central de processamento de dados custe cerca de US$49 milhões por megawatt. Desse total, as despesas com tecnologia da informação respondem por 78% do investimento. Já as chamadas 'neoclouds', data centers voltados especificamente para IA, saem mais caras: aproximadamente US$57 milhões por megawatt. Em contrapartida, exigem menos espaço físico do que os modelos tradicionais. Servidores e rede lideram os custos De acordo com o estudo, o maior peso recai sobre os servidores, que respondem por US$31,4 milhões a cada megawatt. Já em segundo lugar nessa despesa está a rede, cujo valor chega a US$4,8 milhões por megawatt. Os itens restantes representam valores muito inferiores. De acordo com os números do BofA, cada um dos seguintes custa de US$100 mil a US$1,1 milhão por megawatt: quadros de comando, distribuição e energia de reserva, geradores, resfriadores e sistemas de refrigeração.

artigo.texto: Home › Energy Storage ›GoodWe Launches ESA 125 kW/251 kWh BESS at REI Expo 2026 GoodWe Launches ESA 125 kW/251 kWh BESS at REI Expo 2026 GoodWe has launched its ESA 125 kW/251 kWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) for C&I applications at the Renewable Energy India (REI) Expo 2026, alongside showcasing its comprehensive energy storage portfolio spanning residential, commercial, and utility-scale segments. October 26, 2026. By Mrinmoy Dey At the Renewable Energy India (REI) Expo 2026, GoodWe announced the launch of its ESA 125 kW/251 kWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), expanding its portfolio of energy storage solutions for commercial and industrial (C&I) applications. The ESA Series is suited to a wide range of use cases, including factories, commercial complexes and other grid-connected or off-grid applications. It integrates the Power Conversion System (PCS), battery cells, Energy Management System (EMS) and Battery Management System (BMS) in a single cabinet, which simplifies installation, operation and maintenance while allowing flexible capacity expansion. The system scales from hundreds of kilowatt-hours to multi-megawatt-hours, supporting up to 15 units in parallel for a total capacity of up to 3.91 MWh in on-grid scenarios. At the expo, GoodWe also presented a full range of energy storage technologies, from residential systems to large-scale utility projects. In the utility-scale energy storage segment, the company showcased AC ESS 2MW/4MWh, which offers a one-stop integrated solution with in-house-developed battery, PCS, EMU and MVS components in a 20-foot containerised design that enables easier transportation and fast deployment. With 90.5 percent round-trip efficiency, a 7 percent increase in lifetime energy throughput and an AC/DC-separated architecture, it improves project returns while enhancing safety and simplifying maintenance, the company stated. It further added that the UT Series complements this offering for large renewable energy projects and grid-connected installations. GoodWe also showcased its residential hybrid energy storage portfolio, featuring the ES Uniq + Lynx A G3 and ET LV + Lynx A G4 solution. Designed to integrate solar power, battery storage, and intelligent energy management, these solutions highlighted the potential for greater energy independence, efficient solar utilisation, and reliable power supply for modern homes. In the C&I segment, the company showcased the GT Series string inverter, which is designed to enhance productivity and deliver high power density in C&I applications. With 8/10 MPPTs, a high input current of 21A per DC string and a maximum efficiency of 99 percent, it increases overall yield with high-power PV modules. It also supports string-level monitoring and an optional PID (Potential Induced Degradation) recovery function for better module performance. Type II surge protection on both the AC and DC sides protects the inverter against lightning, giving C&I PV projects added safety, reliability and a stronger return on investment. Aniket Sawant, Country Head, GoodWe India, said, “As GoodWe celebrates 10 years in India, we remain committed to driving the country’s clean energy transition through innovative and reliable solutions. The launch of our ESA 125 kW/261 kWh BESS at REI 2026 reflects our continued focus on delivering advanced energy storage solutions across residential, C&I and utility-scale segments.” If you want to cooperate with us and would like to reuse some of our content, please contact: contact@energetica-india.net.

artigo.texto: O Rio Grande do Norte busca ampliar sua participação no mercado de centros de processamento de dados, mas ainda depende da instalação de cabos submarinos de telecomunicações para atrair empreendimentos de grande porte. Apesar dos avanços na regulamentação do setor e da disponibilidade de energia, o Estado aguarda uma definição do governo federal sobre a infraestrutura de conectividade necessária aos projetos. O tema foi discutido nesta sexta-feira, 23, durante a Data Center Conference, realizada na Federação das Indústrias do Estado do Rio Grande do Norte (Fiern), em Natal. Leia mais: FIERN recebe em novembro maior evento sobre produção industrial do RN A instalação de cabos submarinos é considerada uma das condições para viabilizar estruturas capazes de atender empresas nacionais e internacionais. Esses equipamentos permitem a transmissão de grandes volumes de dados entre diferentes regiões e países, com capacidade e velocidade necessárias às operações digitais. A expectativa do setor é de que a infraestrutura amplie a competitividade potiguar na atração de investimentos associados à inteligência artificial, computação em nuvem e armazenamento de informações. Leia mais: Alecrim celebra 115 anos com ações para fortalecer o comércio O gerente comercial da Mendes Holler, Gladson Mortoza, afirmou que a chegada da tecnologia poderá ocorrer no curto e médio prazos. Segundo ele, a disponibilidade de energia representa uma vantagem para o Estado, mas precisa ser acompanhada de infraestrutura de telecomunicações. “O Estado já possui oferta de energia. Com a expectativa da chegada de conectividade via cabo submarino, o Rio Grande do Norte abre a porta para atender às demandas daqui, de todo País e até mesmo internacionais”, afirmou. Leia mais: Prefeitura amplia acesso à qualificação profissional O presidente da Fiern, Roberto Serquiz, defendeu a ampliação das negociações para acelerar a conexão do Estado às redes internacionais. Ele lembrou que o Ceará já dispõe dessa infraestrutura, o que poderia facilitar a integração regional. “É uma etapa que nós precisamos trabalhar. Os cabos já existem no Ceará, então, a ligação com o RN se torna apenas um ponto de diálogo. Com essa conectividade, fechamos mais um ciclo para que, definitivamente, os investimentos cheguem ao RN”, declarou. Leia mais: Procura pela primeira CNH cresce 86% no RN A secretária-adjunta de Desenvolvimento Econômico do Estado, Emília Casanova, informou que o governo potiguar já possui estudos sobre possíveis áreas de instalação, mas depende de uma decisão federal. “Nós temos um estudo de atracação em áreas de interesse, porém, não houve ainda uma decisão do Ministério de Telecomunicações, a qual inclui uma definição sobre os locais de instalação. A gente não sabe se será somente em Natal ou se haverá uma conexão também na região da Costa Branca”, explicou. A indefinição mantém em aberto a localização dos futuros pontos de conexão e o cronograma de implantação. Além da disponibilidade de energia e telecomunicações, projetos de data centers exigem investimentos em sistemas de refrigeração, segurança operacional e fornecimento contínuo de eletricidade, fatores considerados na avaliação econômica dos empreendimentos. RN já tem regras para licenciamento ambiental A regulamentação dos centros de dados no Rio Grande do Norte avançou em setembro, quando o Conselho Estadual do Meio Ambiente (Conema) aprovou normas específicas para o licenciamento desses empreendimentos. Publicada no Diário Oficial em 25 de setembro, a Resolução nº 2/2026 estabelece critérios conforme o porte das instalações, o consumo de energia e os sistemas de refrigeração utilizados. A legislação prevê procedimentos simplificados para instalações menores e estudos ambientais mais abrangentes para estruturas de maior porte. Projetos classificados como grandes ou excepcionais, quando utilizarem sistemas abertos de refrigeração, deverão apresentar Estudo e Relatório de Impacto Ambiental (EIA/Rima). As exigências procuram estabelecer condições para a expansão do setor, considerando o consumo de eletricidade e os possíveis impactos sobre os recursos hídricos. No âmbito federal, a sanção do Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Datacenter (Redata), em setembro, criou incentivos fiscais para investimentos em infraestrutura de processamento e armazenamento de dados. A medida contempla atividades relacionadas à computação em nuvem, inteligência artificial e processamento de alto desempenho. A demanda por esses empreendimentos também cresce no Nordeste. Levantamentos da Empresa de Pesquisa Energética (EPE) identificaram interesse em mais de 30 projetos na região, com potencial de consumo de 8,3 gigawatts. A dimensão dessa demanda reforça a necessidade de planejamento da infraestrutura elétrica e de telecomunicações. *Matéria atualizada às 11h55

artigo.texto: Brookhaven 'in no rush" to provide permits for 2 new battery storage plants Brookhaven Town Supervisor Dan Panico, while stopping short of declaring a moratorium on new battery storage projects in the town, indicated this week that the town was in no rush to provide needed permits for two large facilities proposed for the town. At a town board meeting Thursday night at which several dozen residents showed up in opposition to the proposed facilities while unionized contractors and green-energy advocates spoke in support, Panico assured residents that permit approvals were not on his short-term to-do list. "The town is not fast-tracking anything," he said, referencing to the state-approved batteries in Holtsville and Manorville. Noting that neither site has building permits, he said, "The town board, the town of Brookhaven is in no rush to issue building permits for that [Holtsville] site at all." He called on the state to do more to help extinguish lingering local concerns about battery fires, as well as detailing fire-suppression plans. Brookhaven, which is set to be the import site of 924 megawatts of offshore wind power next year, will be the beneficiary of upward of $139 million tax benefits from the Sunrise Wind farm, the excess power from which is expected to be stored in any available batteries. The town also is considered Ground Zero for battery-storage plans on Long Island, with most of the more than dozen facilities proposed in the region slated for Brookhaven. The Manorville site, a proposed 150-megawatt facility with 196 battery containers at 62 Weaks Ave. near farms and homes, has a prior site plan submitted to the town, but does not have building permits, Panico stressed. Panico noted that all battery sites proposed for Long Island are over a sole-source aquifer, sharply distinguishing them from others already built across the country. He also noted that "substantial questions" remain from local fire departments about whether or not to apply water to fires at the plants, following contamination at an East Hampton plant that experienced a thermal runaway fire in 2023. The state issued strict new fire safety standards for batteries in January. However, some residents remain unconvinced about their effectiveness. "Even though we’re hearing about these new standards, new practices, it’s all risk-mitigating, it’s not safe yet," said Gabriel Piazza of Holbrook, urging town officials to do "whatever we can do to stop the development of these near our schools and our communities." Seth Rivera, who lives near a proposed site in Manorville and formerly worked for the U.S. Department of Energy, told Brookhaven officials the majority of the community "does not want" the plants and asked why the town would even entertain the permits. Rivera said the Key Capture Energy project in Manorville was of "particular concern" given its location near schools and homes, and urged against any fast-track approval for it because "adequate environmental studies have not been completed, risk assessment studies have not been completed" and there are no planned evacuation routes. "Why are you so willing to go against the entirety of your constituency," Rivera asked board members, to applause. Panico assured him that was not the case. Most who spoke in favor of the batteries were contractors and unionized workers who have already built them and are eager to build more, along with green-energy groups who say they'll lessen reliance on fossil fuels and stabilize the grid. Some who spoke said they were affiliated with Haugland Group, the Melville-based company that built Long Island’s first two batteries, in East Hampton and Montauk. Repeated reference was made during the evening to the East Hampton plant, which is now shut down following reports of water contamination around the facility following the 2023 fire. The Montauk facility is also temporarily shut down following an agreement between battery owner NextEra and Suffolk County. Billy Haugland, chief executive of the Haugland Group, in messages to Newsday Friday, acknowledged the company was selected in a competitive process to construct the two existing batteries and, more recently, to rebuild them recently to "safer technology." "Now each individual battery unit has a suppression capability" built into it, he said. Lucia Yu, senior manager for development at Key Capture Energy, gave a presentation at the meeting about the safety of the new battery designs, and also met informally with residents after it. She told residents that there’s "no scenario" in which all 196 battery containers at the Manorville site would ever go on fire because of "safety measures that are in place in each individual container." With a new safer design for the plants and a new approach to fires that would involve allowing them to burn out on their own, Yu said that in the unlikely event of a fire at a new plant, it could fully burn out in 10 hours. The East Hampton plant burned for more than 30 hours. Asked why KCE wouldn’t just jump ahead to zinc bromide technology which is less likely to cause fires, Yu said, "The whole point of having a large-scale battery project is to stabilize the grid at a rate that’s economic to ratepayers. If we use zinc batteries it won’t be economic for us ..." Asked how much people’s bills would go down once the new battery was in place, she acknowledged: "It doesn’t directly correlate with bills decreasing. It helps bills increase at a lower rate than it would otherwise. Because energy costs more and more and if you have more battery storage projects on the grid, there’s less reliance on fossil-fuel peaker plants, which are extremely expensive ..." Erin Taylor, a Manorville resident, asked Yu why the Weaks Ave. plant wasn’t put in a more industrial area rather than in her neighborhood where schools and farms surround it.
