artigo.texto: With public distaste for data centers in Connecticut on the rise, residents in several communities are pushing for new restrictions even as the company looking to build one in Cromwell is stepping up its public relations effort. East Lyme’s zoning board last week unanimously prohibited any data centers from being built there, making the town at least the seventh in Connecticut to impose tougher rules. Morris, Trumbull, New Haven, Waterford, West Haven and Groton have all either banned new data centers altogether or imposed temporary moratoriums against them. Even so, Trumbull appears to be on track for the massive expansion of an existing data center. The $200 million cogNovum project would enlarge a former Nasdaq center in the town’s Merritt Boulevard office park. So despite the town’s newly enacted two-year moratorium against new centers, zoning officials are treating cogNovum as an expansion — and immune to the ban. A band of Trumbull residents this week tried to get their zoning board to adopt a new regulation adding expansions to the temporary ban, but were turned back. “We wanted a one-year moratorium against expansion of existing data centers,” opponent Richard White told WICC radio interviewer Melissa Sheketoff on her Melissa in the Morning program Thursday. “They voted against us 5-0.” In mid-summer, First Selectman Vicki Tesoro told residents that the project isn’t like the mega-centers that are proposed around the country. Developers want to put up a 10-gigawatt facility on more than 2,500 acres in Piketon, Ohio, for instance, and Meta and Blue Owl Capital are looking to build a 5-gigawatt center totalling 4 million square feet in northeastern Louisiana. “This is a renovation of a decades-old, existing data center — not the new construction of a hyperscale AI facility,” Tesoro told residents in late July. “Four main concerns rise to the top of my conversations with residents: electricity, noise, water, and expansion of the building’s footprint,” Tesoro said. “When it comes to these four things, I told the applicant directly: no increase in electrical draw beyond existing site capacity, no increase in noise, no increase in water use, no expansion of the building’s footprint. They have agreed to all four.” But the Trumbull AI Data Center Watch, an organization of opponents, is still fighting. Similarly, a group organizing against a potential 100-megawatt data center in Beacon Falls is connecting with local data center opponents in several communities, and recently started selling coffee cups, T-shirts and more to promote its message “Happy to not be on the map.” First Selectman Gerard Smith got blowback from opponents when he said the center would “put Beacon Falls on the map in a big way.” Meanwhile, a commercial real estate firm promoting plans for a data center in Cromwell said residents there haven’t heard enough about the proposal’s upside. The Algonquin gas pipeline runs through the Cromwell property and along with on-site fuel cells means the operation would be powered without taking anything from the electrical grid, according to Jay Morris of O,R&L Commercial, the real estate broker for landowner Gardner Nurseries. Although no formal application has been filed with the town, developers have signaled they want to put up a 1.2 million-square-foot, 300-megawatt data center on part of a 160-acre site off Geer Street. “This site is zoned for Industrial, and if this opportunity goes away it could be developed for manufacturing and distribution uses that could have much more building density, truck traffic and noise, and likely not seek to preserve open farmland,” Morris wrote in a letter to The Courant. “The developer has been meeting informally with local residents and has designed the preliminary layout to be set back far from the road and houses,” Morris wrote, saying the project would use only about a third of the acreage and leave the rest as open space. “Many of the national data centers are enormous, many 10x or more what is being discussed in Cromwell,” he wrote. A data center would add no burden to schools or other town services, wouldn’t require substantial water supplies, would generate no traffic after construction and would provide “substantial” local tax revenue, he wrote. “I believe if the public understood the benefits of this use in this location vs any other type of industrial development, they would welcome this opportunity,” according to his letter. Late Friday afternoon, however, Mayor James Demetriades posted a detailed zoning proposal from resident Juan Duque aimed at curbing data centers in Cromwell. It would set safety standards along with maximum limits on noise and vibrations; the Planning and Zoning Commission is scheduled to hear the proposed regulations Dec. 3. Of special relevance to the Geer Street project, the regulations would establish a cap of 100,000 square feet and require at least a mile buffer from any school. The Geer site is across the street from the town’s Woodside Intermediate School.

artigo.texto: BYD's R&D Roadmap Meets a Cautious Earnings Reality Published on 10/25/2026 at 04:20 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD has laid out where it intends to spend its engineering effort next: megawatt fast charging, a next-generation Blade battery and integrated body-to-battery construction. The company confirmed the three priorities on an investor platform, a disclosure that sketches the direction of travel without committing to a single launch date or performance figure. That distinction matters for anyone trying to price the stock. BYD has restated a technological course, not reported a completed milestone. No output data accompanied the announcement, and management said it would publish progress once formal disclosure obligations kick in. Nothing in the statement points to a near-term product rollout, and nothing in it allows an analyst to book incremental revenue or profit. What the roadmap does and does not cover The message underscores how heavily battery and charging technology weigh in BYD's development planning. It stops short of offering a basis for quantifying future sales. Separating technical potential from commercially proven success remains the core exercise here. Products already on sale sit in a different category. The direction reaffirmed today is not a fresh market entry and should not be conflated with the charging specifications of vehicles already in showrooms. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? Seagull refresh shows execution on the ground Two days before the investor update, BYD launched the second generation of its Seagull in China. The line-up runs to five variants priced between 65,900 Yuan and 99,900 Yuan, with selected versions carrying particularly rapid charging capability. Flash Charging trims start at 75,900 Yuan — evidence that BYD is not reserving fast-charge hardware for its pricier segments alone. The caveat is physical rather than commercial: advertised charging power depends on compatible stations. A car's technical ceiling does not guarantee the same charging speed at every plug. For the equipped variants, BYD quotes a 10-to-70 percent top-up in five minutes. Those figures describe the Seagull technology on offer, not the next-generation development work flagged today. BYD has not confirmed a European launch for the new Seagull, so the Chinese sales start translates into no European volume contribution. For now, execution in the home market is what counts. The Seagull is not the only recent addition. BYD introduced the Da Han EV in China on 13 October, offering three versions priced from 235,900 Yuan to 275,900 Yuan. The two launches sit in very different price brackets and together round out a picture of steady product activity in China. Neither set of sticker prices says anything about demand or about the profit each model will generate. Brazil paperwork and the rally that wasn't about it Alongside the model cadence, BYD is pursuing a larger manufacturing footprint in Brazil. Reuters reported on Friday, citing the company, that BYD has begun seeking permits to double annual plant capacity to 600,000 vehicles. The procedural stage is the key detail: the targeted expansion is not the same as capacity already available. At the same time, the Brazilian unit was close to completing its stamping, welding and painting facilities — so the news bundles a permitting step for future growth with tangible progress at the existing site. BYD at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. Friday also brought a 4.4 percent gain in BYD shares, part of a broad recovery across lithium-battery and other automotive names. The friendlier sector backdrop, rather than any single company-specific trigger, was the dominant force. Investors are therefore better served separating the market move from the recent news on models and production. No direct link between the Seagull launch and Friday's share-price action has been established, and the rally on its own is no proof that the market is already discounting higher volumes or extra earnings from either the new models or the Brazil plan. Analysts split on the earnings risk Technological ambition is running into a more sober read on the business. One house cites weak domestic demand, higher input costs and political uncertainty as grounds for caution. Barclays, by contrast, keeps an "Overweight" rating and points to global expansion, while acknowledging softer domestic volumes after subsidy cuts and amid tougher competition. The divergence illustrates a simple point: growth opportunities alone do not settle the question of future profitability. Hard evidence on the economics remains the central yardstick, and it still trails the development strategy. Today's statement sharpens BYD's research priorities without removing those earnings risks. What will count is verifiable development progress and its conversion into sellable products. Absent performance data and launch dates, the next battery generation stays a development prospect rather than a secured earnings driver. artigo.texto: BYD avança na nacionalização e se prepara para dobrar capacidade no Brasil Unidade no Brasil deve iniciar 2027 ultrapassando o mínimo exigido de 50% de nacionalização de componentes, o que atenderá às exigências regulatórias e ajudará a empresa a iniciar as exportações regionais A fabricante chinesa de carros elétricos BYD deu início aos pedidos de licenças para dobrar a capacidade anual de produção de sua fábrica brasileira para 600.000 veículos, ao mesmo tempo em que entra na fase final de obras e testes de seus galpões de estamparia, soldagem e pintura, disse à Reuters o principal executivo da empresa no país. A unidade da BYD no Brasil deve iniciar 2027 ultrapassando o mínimo exigido de 50% de nacionalização de componentes, o que atenderá às exigências regulatórias e ajudará a empresa a iniciar as exportações regionais, afirmou o vice-presidente sênior Alexandre Baldy em entrevista. A empresa enfrentou reclamações de grupos da indústria local de que dependia muito de importações e de tarifas temporariamente baixas. "A gente trabalha para inaugurar 2027 já ultrapassando essa posição e termos essas etapas em operação para sermos considerados um fabricante local", disse Baldy. A BYD tem como meta se tornar a maior montadora do Brasil em volume de vendas até 2030 e já vê a demanda superar sua capacidade atual de produção, disse Baldy. Embora a BYD esteja acelerando suas operações e planeje atingir uma produção mensal de 25.000 veículos até o final de 2026, a tendência é de que a demanda continue superando a oferta. "Nossa demanda tem ficado em uma média de cerca de 30.000 carros por mês, o que significa que estamos deixando de faturar cerca de 5.000 a 6.000 vendas adicionais", disse Baldy. O investimento na nova fábrica da empresa no Brasil já ultrapassou os R$ 5,5 bilhões e as vendas faturadas da unidade brasileira atingirão esta semana a marca de 200.000 carros no acumulado de 2026, afirmou Baldy. Em setembro, a empresa teve um total de 22.209 veículos emplacados no Brasil, o equivalente a uma fatia de mercado de 8,5%, segundo dados da empresa. A BYD já é líder de mercado no Uruguai e suas vendas ocupam posições de destaque na Colômbia e na Argentina, disse o executivo. A montadora no Brasil também recebeu pedidos de 50.000 unidades do México e da Argentina cada, e estará apta a atendê-los a partir do ano que vem graças ao aumento do índice de componentes locais. A BYD inaugurou sua fábrica em Camaçari, Bahia, em 9 de outubro de 2025, em um complexo industrial que pertenceu à Ford Motor Co. A fábrica emprega atualmente cerca de 9.000 pessoas e espera expandir sua força de trabalho para cerca de 10.000 trabalhadores até o final deste ano.

artigo.texto: Google vai pagar a quem economizar energia; a sobra irá para data centers de IA O Google anunciou na quarta-feira (22) que vai pagar a moradores e empresas dos Estados Unidos que reduzirem o consumo de energia elétrica. O objetivo é destinar a energia economizada aos data centers de inteligência artificial da companhia. A iniciativa será feita em parceria com a Voltus, empresa de recursos energéticos distribuídos. Ela vai disponibilizar ao Google até 1.070 megawatts de capacidade elétrica sempre que a companhia precisar. Segundo o jornal The New York Times, essa capacidade equivale à de um reator nuclear. Esse modelo de negócio é conhecido como usina elétrica virtual (VPP, na sigla em inglês). Em vez de concentrar a produção de energia em uma única usina, o sistema coordena recursos espalhados por diferentes locais, reunindo residências e empresas que podem reduzir o consumo de eletricidade da rede ou usar a energia que elas mesmas geram. Quando são acionados, os participantes recebem incentivos financeiros. Segundo a Voltus, os benefícios incluem economia nas contas de luz e pagamentos diretos, o que transforma a demanda do Google por capacidade elétrica em ganho econômico para os clientes. Os valores que serão pagos, no entanto, não foram divulgados. A Voltus também recomenda o uso de termostatos inteligentes, que podem ajustar, por exemplo, o tempo em que um aparelho de ar-condicionado permanece ligado. Nesses casos, a redução do consumo acontece de forma automática, sem que o participante precise desligar os equipamentos manualmente. Com o modelo, a capacidade de que o Google precisa vem da energia que deixa de ser consumida pelas residências e empresas participantes, coordenadas pela Voltus, e não de uma única usina dedicada a abastecer os data centers.

artigo.texto: WEG em NÚMEROS Como data centers dos EUA viraram motor da 'fábrica de bilionários' no Brasil DIVULGAÇÃO/WEG Transformador da WEG; equipamentos como este puxaram as vendas da empresa nos Estados Unidos Publicado em 25/10/2026 - 6h00 Atualizado em 25/10/2026 - 10h18 A WEG, multinacional de Santa Catarina conhecida como "fábrica de bilionários", encerrou o terceiro trimestre de 2026 com lucro líquido de R$ 1,67 bilhão. O valor representa alta de 0,9% sobre o mesmo período de 2025 e equivale a pouco mais de R$ 18 milhões por dia, ou cerca de R$ 750 mil por hora, considerando os 92 dias entre julho e setembro. Mesmo assim, o balanço, divulgado na quarta-feira (21), não trouxe os resultados que os investidores esperavam. As ações da companhia (WEGE3) tiveram a maior queda do Ibovespa na semana. O motivo está menos no tamanho do lucro e mais no quanto sobra de cada venda. No mesmo dia, a empresa anunciou uma troca programada na vice-presidência de Energia, ligada a alguns dos negócios que mais crescem no grupo. Entre julho e setembro, a WEG teve receita líquida de R$ 10,86 bilhões, crescimento de 5,7% na comparação anual. É como se a empresa faturasse cerca de R$ 118 milhões por dia. O Ebitda, indicador que mostra quanto a operação gera antes de juros, impostos e depreciação, somou R$ 2,35 bilhões, alta de 3,1%. O retorno sobre o capital investido ficou em 33,2%, 0,8 ponto percentual acima de um ano antes. O destaque veio de fora do país. As vendas no exterior responderam por 62,5% do faturamento, o maior nível da história da WEG. Data centers e rede elétrica dos EUA puxam as vendas A América do Norte é o principal motor desse avanço. A receita na região chegou a US$ 722,8 milhões no trimestre, 31% a mais do que um ano antes. A fatia equivale a 54,7% de tudo o que a empresa vende fora do Brasil. No mesmo período de 2025, era 47,9%. A venda de transformadores para reforçar a rede elétrica norte-americana, que passa por modernização, ajuda a explicar o salto. E também os geradores da Marathon, marca do grupo nos Estados Unidos, usados como energia de reserva em data centers, os grandes galpões de servidores que sustentam a internet e a inteligência artificial. O resultado em reais, porém, foi menor do que poderia ser. O dólar médio caiu de R$ 5,45 para R$ 5,14 entre um trimestre e outro. Como a WEG converte para a moeda brasileira o que fatura lá fora, cada dólar passou a valer menos no balanço. Em dólares, as vendas externas subiram 14,8%; em reais, 8,3%. FOTO: DIVULGAÇÃO/WEG Fábrica da Weg na cidade de Betim, em Minas Gerais Custo maior aperta a margem O ponto que pesou para os investidores foi a rentabilidade. A margem bruta, que mostra quanto fica com a empresa depois de pagar o custo de produção, caiu de 33,6% para 32,9%. Em outras palavras: de cada R$ 100 vendidos, sobraram R$ 32,90, contra R$ 33,60 um ano antes. Segundo a WEG, três fatores explicam a queda: a alta do cobre, matéria-prima essencial para motores e transformadores; as tarifas de importação cobradas pelos Estados Unidos; e o gasto maior com funcionários, ligado à ampliação das fábricas iniciada neste ano. O peso da folha de pagamento no custo dos produtos subiu de 19,2% para 20,3%. Isso acontece porque a companhia contrata antes de as novas linhas de produção operarem em ritmo pleno. Com esse efeito, a margem Ebitda também recuou, de 22,2% para 21,6%. Como o mercado reagiu Levantamento da LSEG (London Stock Exchange Group) mostrava que analistas esperavam lucro de R$ 1,71 bilhão e Ebitda de R$ 2,40 bilhões. Os números vieram um pouco abaixo, e o mercado também contava com uma redução menor na margem. Na manhã de quarta-feira, as ações chegaram a cair 4,6%, cotadas a R$ 46,53. Na semana de 19 a 23 de outubro, a desvalorização acumulada foi de 10,96%, a pior entre os papéis do Ibovespa. O índice fechou o período praticamente estável, com recuo de 0,17%. Troca na área de Energia Junto com o balanço, a WEG comunicou que João Paulo Gualberto da Silva deixará a vice-presidência de Energia em 31 de dezembro, depois de 37 anos na companhia. Engenheiro eletricista formado pela Udesc, ele trabalhou na área comercial, inclusive nos Estados Unidos, e dirigiu o setor de novas energias, com foco em eólica e solar. FOTOS: DIVULGAÇÃO/WEG Sai João Paulo Gualberto da Silva (à esq.), assume Paulo Leonardo da Silva Sinoti O sucessor é Paulo Leonardo da Silva Sinoti, atual diretor de Soluções em Energia & Serviços, que também soma mais de três décadas de casa. Ele assume o posto em 1º de janeiro de 2027. A escolha foi aprovada pelo Conselho de Administração e faz parte do planejamento de sucessão da empresa. A mudança ocorre em um momento de expansão dos negócios de energia. No trimestre, a área de geração, transmissão e distribuição, que reúne os transformadores e geradores responsáveis pelo crescimento nos EUA, aumentou as vendas externas em 24,1% na comparação com o mesmo período de 2025. Fundada em 16 de setembro de 1961, em Jaraguá do Sul (SC), a WEG começou fabricando motores elétricos. O nome reúne as iniciais dos três fundadores: Werner Ricardo Voigt, Eggon João da Silva e Geraldo Werninghaus. Hoje, a companhia é uma das maiores fabricantes de equipamentos elétricos do mundo. O portfólio inclui motores, geradores, transformadores, painéis, sistemas de automação para fábricas, equipamentos para produzir e distribuir energia, carregadores de carros elétricos e até tintas industriais. São mais de 45 mil funcionários e unidades em mais de 40 países. Peças da WEG estão por trás de máquinas de lavar, aparelhos de ar-condicionado, indústrias de papel e celulose, plataformas de petróleo e redes de energia elétrica. A "fábrica de bilionários" O apelido vem do controle familiar. Os herdeiros diretos dos três fundadores, que já morreram, mantêm participação relevante nas ações. A valorização da empresa na bolsa ao longo das décadas transformou parte deles em bilionários. Ao todo, são mais de 100 acionistas herdeiros atualmente, de acordo com o portal

artigo.texto: EU Reaches Provisional Deal to Keep MSR Invalidation Mechanism with 700 Million Allowance Threshold The European Council and the European Parliament have reached a provisional agreement to keep the invalidation mechanism of the Market Stability Reserve within the Emissions Trading System, according to the European Parliament. The legislature said in a press release that the mechanism would be retained with a higher threshold of 700 million allowances. The targeted amendment is intended to improve long-term market liquidity and predictability while protecting industrial competitiveness. The provisional deal, reached on October 20, still requires endorsement by both institutions before formal adoption. Since the invalidation mechanism began operating in 2023, more than 3 billion allowances have been invalidated and removed from the market. According to the release, this has helped rebalance supply and demand and address the historical surplus built up in the ETS. The European Commission had proposed in April suspending the invalidation mechanism indefinitely. The co-legislators instead provisionally agreed on a compromise that keeps the mechanism in force. Under existing rules, allowances held in the reserve above a 400 million threshold are invalidated. Once the new proposal is formally adopted, the higher 700 million limit would take effect immediately. The release indicated that a larger number of allowances would support long-term stability in the EU carbon market and provide a bigger buffer against future market fluctuations, while guarding against an excessive surplus. The co-legislators also agreed that a gradual reduction of the invalidation threshold should be considered within the broader ETS review to ensure a consistent overall approach. The next step is formal approval of the agreement by the European Parliament and the European Council. Separately, the European Parliament has proposed directing 75% of ETS revenues toward decarbonizing local industry. The proposal was put forward by the Parliament's lead negotiator, Peter Liese, and exceeds the 50% share initially proposed by the European Commission. - 1. artigo.texto: Plans for an 86-acre long-duration energy storage development on Green Belt land between Busby and Thorntonhall are moving forward again. The proposed Busby Long Duration Energy Storage project would cover 34.9 hectares of land at Meikle Dripps Farm, roughly equivalent to 54 football pitches, close to Waterfoot Road. It would have a capacity of up to 150MW and store 1,200MWh of electricity, enough to operate at its maximum output for eight hours. Correspondence received by the Jackton, Thorntonhall and Busby Alliance LDES Action Group indicates that developers are now preparing to hold a statutory pre-application consultation before submitting the full plans. Consultants Cavendish Consulting have told campaigners that residents will be given an opportunity to see and comment on the proposals before an application for consent is lodged. No date has yet been announced for the consultation. The Scottish Government’s Energy Consents Unit continues to list Busby LDES as a “Pre Application” project. The live record names Apatura Project 22 Ltd as the applicant and confirms that no full Section 36 application has yet reached the determination stage. Documents already submitted as part of environmental screening give a clearer picture of the potential scale of the development. The site extends across six agricultural fields approximately 100 metres west of Thorntonhall and 250 metres south of Busby. The nearest residential property is immediately beside its southern boundary. The developer’s original screening submission modelled a development of up to 3,510 battery blocks. It considered container units around 2.6 metres high, with one potential configuration allowing them to be double-stacked. The accompanying landscape assessment said that could result in structures around 5.2 metres high, although the final design and technology had not been fixed at that stage. Frontier Power Energy Holdings acquired the rights to the Busby project and a separate 200MW scheme at Ayr from Apatura on 26 May 2026. Apatura said it would retain an active role in progressing both developments. Frontier now says Busby is expected to use long-duration batteries supplied by US manufacturer Eos Energy Enterprises, including its Z3 zinc-based technology, rather than conventional lithium-ion batteries. The company has also confirmed that Busby has received a Gate 2 notification through the National Energy System Operator’s reformed grid connection process. Gate 2 means a project has met NESO’s tests for readiness and can secure a place in the reformed connections queue, with a confirmed connection point and date. It is separate from planning permission and does not amount to approval for the development to be built. The Green Belt location is likely to remain one of the main issues when the full application is considered. The developer’s own landscape assessment says the Green Belt in this location helps maintain separation between East Kilbride, Busby and Clarkston, Thorntonhall and Waterfoot. It also acknowledges that developing the site would increase the urban influence on the landscape and result in an “unavoidable loss of openness” that would conflict with its Green Belt designation. South Lanarkshire Council reached a similarly conclusion during environmental screening. Its assessment said the project would be out of scale with the existing environment, describing it as a medium-scale development being introduced into a semi-rural area. Scottish Ministers subsequently determined that the development did not need to be accompanied by a full Environmental Impact Assessment. A future application is still expected to include detailed assessments covering aspects including landscape and visual impact, noise, ecology, flooding and drainage. Construction itself was estimated in the screening documents to take around 12 to 18 months, including work on the access, underground cables, fencing and landscaping. The transport assessment anticipates construction traffic using Waterfoot Road and Peel Road, including HGVs, light goods vehicles and “a small number of abnormal loads”. A public Core Path connecting Thorntonhall and Busby also crosses the site. The developer has proposed retaining and upgrading the route, although South Lanarkshire’s environmental screening states that the surroundings of sections of the path would be altered. The scheme has attracted sustained opposition in Busby, Thorntonhall and Jackton. Campaigners argue that energy storage infrastructure of this scale is inappropriate for agricultural Green Belt land separating established communities and have raised concerns about landscape change, construction traffic and noise. A Change.org petition opposing the Busby LDES development has now attracted 2,962 verified signatures. The petition states: “The BESS/LDES Local Action Group and the Jackton and Thorntonhall Community Council (JTCC) are fighting back against this development because of the dangers it poses - from fire risks and noise, to environmental damage and traffic. “While we acknowledge the importance of energy infrastructure, we believe this location is completely inappropriate and that safer, more suitable alternative locations should be considered.” The action group is also due to meet Scottish Labour South Scotland MSP Joe Fagan later this month as it prepares for the expected public consultation.

artigo.texto: Mercado global de blocos de resfriamento para células a combustível: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do mercado de blocos de resfriamento para células a combustível até 2035: demanda de data centers e redes impulsiona taxa composta anual de 9–13% Resumo Segundo o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de blocos de resfriamento para células a combustível, o mercado inicia 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de suprimento mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de blocos de resfriamento para células a combustível entra em uma fase de expansão acelerada, com a demanda projetada para crescer a uma taxa composta anual de 9–13% entre 2026 e 2035. Esse segmento especializado de equipamentos de gestão térmica do sistema de equilíbrio de planta está intrinsecamente ligado à trajetória de implantação dos sistemas de células a combustível de alta potência, cada vez mais adotados para geração estacionária de energia, apoio à rede e aplicações de backup. Como os stacks de células a combustível exigem regulação térmica precisa para manter temperaturas operacionais ideais, os blocos de resfriamento — componentes projetados com canais internos para o líquido de arrefecimento — tornam-se viabilizadores críticos da confiabilidade e da eficiência do sistema. O mercado é sustentado pela rápida expansão de data centers e de projetos de escala utilitária que demandam soluções de energia resilientes e de baixas emissões. A Ásia-Pacífico lidera tanto a produção quanto o consumo, enquanto a Europa vem logo atrás, com iniciativas de hidrogênio impulsionadas por políticas públicas. Entre as principais tendências estão a incorporação de recursos inteligentes de resfriamento, a migração para cadeias de suprimento validadas localmente e a diversificação para aplicações móveis e marítimas. No entanto, gargalos na qualificação de fornecedores, volatilidade dos custos de insumos e incertezas na política comercial representam desafios relevantes. Este relatório oferece uma análise abrangente do tamanho de mercado, da segmentação, do cenário competitivo e das dinâmicas regionais, de modo a subsidiar a tomada de decisão estratégica até 2035. O cenário-base para o mercado de blocos de resfriamento para células a combustível prevê crescimento robusto, com a demanda global avançando a uma taxa composta anual de 9–13% entre 2026 e 2035. Essa projeção se apoia na aceleração da implantação de sistemas estacionários de células a combustível em infraestrutura de rede, data centers e energia de backup industrial. À medida que as instalações de células a combustível escalam de alguns gigawatts anuais em 2026 para capacidades significativamente maiores até 2035, a demanda por blocos de resfriamento — essenciais para manter as temperaturas dos stacks em faixas ideais — crescerá em paralelo. Espera-se que o valor de mercado seja impulsionado tanto pelo crescimento em volume quanto pela migração para blocos de resfriamento premium, com sensores integrados, ligas resistentes à corrosão e canais de fluxo otimizados, que alcançam preços mais altos. A Ásia-Pacífico deve manter sua dominância, respondendo por 38–45% da demanda global, sustentada por bases industriais fortes na China, na Coreia do Sul e no Japão. A Europa continuará sendo um mercado-chave, com participação de 25–30%, impulsionada pela política de hidrogênio e por projetos de escala utilitária. A América do Norte deve registrar adoção acelerada, sobretudo em aplicações de data centers e de resiliência de rede. O cenário-base pressupõe ausência de grandes rupturas na cadeia de suprimentos e um ritmo estável de comercialização das células a combustível. Ainda assim, a sensibilidade à volatilidade dos preços de matérias-primas e aos prazos de qualificação pode moderar o crescimento em segmentos específicos. No conjunto, o mercado se prepara para uma década transformadora, e os fornecedores de blocos de resfriamento precisarão investir em capacidades de validação local e em tecnologias inteligentes de resfriamento para aproveitar as oportunidades emergentes. Vetores e restrições da demanda Principais vetores de demanda - Implantação acelerada de sistemas estacionários de células a combustível em infraestrutura de rede e data centers - Crescimento da demanda por blocos de resfriamento premium com sensores térmicos integrados e ligas resistentes à corrosão - Iniciativas de hidrogênio impulsionadas por políticas públicas na Europa e na Ásia-Pacífico - Diversificação das aplicações de células a combustível para energia móvel, setor marítimo e apoio em solo à aviação - Migração para cadeias de suprimento validadas localmente, reduzindo prazos de entrega e barreiras de certificação - Incorporação de recursos inteligentes de resfriamento que viabilizam manutenção preditiva e reduzem a complexidade do sistema de equilíbrio de planta Possíveis restrições ao crescimento - Gargalos na qualificação de fornecedores, com ciclos de aprovação de 8 a 14 meses, limitando a adição de capacidade - Volatilidade dos custos de insumos como cobre, aço inoxidável e ligas especiais, comprimindo as margens - Incertezas na política comercial e classificações de importação divergentes, gerando custos de conformidade - Dependência de fonte única para alguns fabricantes de células a combustível, dada a escassez de fornecedores qualificados - Complexidade técnica do projeto de blocos de resfriamento para células a combustível de alta temperatura, como as SOFC Estrutura da demanda por setor de uso final Infraestrutura de rede (participação estimada: 30%) A infraestrutura de rede é um dos principais setores de uso final dos blocos de

artigo.texto: The Ełk and Turośń Kościelna battery projects in north-eastern Poland are to be sold to A&R Investments by Greenvolt, a Portugal-based renewable energy group. The two stand-alone projects hold 1.6 GWh between them, and each has 200 MW of power and 800 MWh of storage capacity. Both were completed in the third quarter of 2026, and each of them can discharge at full power for about four hours. Each project also holds a 17-year capacity market contract, under which it is to receive a fixed payment from 2028 for keeping 85% of its rated capacity available. A 10-year tolling agreement covers both projects, and under it their flexibility is to be traded in the power markets. The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026. For Greenvolt, the sale forms part of an asset rotation strategy, which foresees the sale of approximately 70-80% of the projects that it develops internally. Greenvolt to sell 1.6 GWh of BESS in Poland to A&R Investments A&R Investments is to buy the two battery projects that Greenvolt Power has completed in north-eastern Poland, and each of them holds a 17-year capacity market contract. artigo.texto: Microtek Unveils BESS Solutions for Energy Management and Cost Optimisation at REI Expo 2026 Microtek highlighted its high-voltage lithium battery pack and i-BESS 125kW/261kWh system at REI Expo 2026, designed to support peak shaving, microgrid integration and electricity cost management. October 26, 2026. By News Bureau Microtek showcased its integrated solar, energy storage and power management portfolio at Renewable Energy India (REI) Expo 2026, from October 22 to 24 in Greater Noida. Led by its ‘Har Ghar Bijli Ghar’ vision, the company introduced its new Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), highlighting its focus on making reliable energy solutions accessible to households and businesses. With nearly four decades of power management experience, Microtek’s portfolio spans: power generation, distribution, conditioning and storage. The showcase products included home inverters, UPS systems, batteries, electrical wires, solar panels, solar inverters and lithium batteries. This breadth underpins its holistic approach, connecting solar generation with power distribution, protection and storage within one portfolio. Microtek’s new High-Voltage Lithium Battery Pack and BESS range was a key highlight at the EXPO, showcasing the i-BESS 125kW/261kWh system. These intelligent energy storage solutions are designed to support peak shaving, microgrid integration and electricity cost optimisation. This marks Microtek’s entry into the high-voltage energy storage segment. Commenting on the participation, N.K Aggarwal, Founder and Chairman of Microtek International, said, “Our vision of ‘Har Ghar Bijli Ghar’ reflects our ambition to help households generate and manage their own electricity. Our portfolio across generation, distribution, conditioning and storage builds on nearly four decades of experience in keeping power reliable. Through our BESS and lithium-based solutions, we are strengthening our capabilities to serve India’s changing energy needs.” Microtek’s reach is supported by over 1 lakh plus dealers across India. The company expects to more than double revenue in FY 2026–27 to INR 5,000 crore, with an ambition to reach INR 10,000 crore within two years. At REI Expo, Microtek connected with channel partners and industry experts to showcase its solar and energy storage solutions. The exhibition will also provide a platform to discuss new business opportunities, expand its distribution network and build partnerships to make its solutions more widely available for homes and businesses. please contact: contact@energetica-india.net.

artigo.texto: Air Liquide Major player in liquid hydrogen storage and infrastructure According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Material Based Hydrogen Energy Storage market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global market for material based hydrogen energy storage is transitioning from a technology-push R&D phase to a commercial-pull demonstration phase, driven by the urgent need for long-duration energy storage solutions that enable high-renewables grids and decarbonize hard-to-electrify sectors. Material based hydrogen energy storage systems store hydrogen through absorption or adsorption into solid-state materials such as metal hydrides, porous nanomaterials, and chemical hydrides, offering high volumetric density and enhanced safety compared to compressed or liquefied gas storage. No single material chemistry has emerged as a dominant standard; the competitive landscape remains fragmented between metal hydrides, complex hydrides, and porous adsorbents, each with distinct trade-offs in gravimetric capacity, volumetric density, kinetics, and operating temperature. This fragmentation leads to application-specific material selection and a highly differentiated competitive structure. System integration, particularly thermal management and controls, is a more significant barrier to bankable projects than material performance alone. Engineering expertise in managing exothermic adsorption and endothermic desorption cycles is a critical and scarce resource. The total installed cost is dominated by balance-of-plant and integration expenses rather than the core storage material, shifting competitive advantage from pure material innovators to firms with integrated system design, safety engineering, and project delivery capabilities. Procurement is moving toward a system-of-systems model, where material based storage is evaluated as a sub-component within larger hydrogen production, storage, and utilization value chains, increasing the influence of engineering, procurement, and construction firms and integrators. Supply chain resilience is threatened by dependencies on critical metals such as vanadium, lanthanum, and titanium for certain high-performance hydrides, creating both cost volatility risk and a strategic imperative for material innovation toward earth-abundant elements. Safety and certification protocols, while rigorous for pressure vessels, are underdeveloped for novel solid-state materials, creating a lengthy and uncertain path to market for new entrants and favoring incumbents with experience in gas handling and industrial compliance. The route-to-market bifurcates: high-volume, lower-capacity modules for mobility applications such as forklifts and drones versus large-scale, custom-engineered systems for stationary storage, requiring entirely different manufacturing, channel, and partnership strategies. This report provides a structured, commercially grounded analysis of the global market for material based hydrogen energy storage, covering historical data from 2012 to 2025 and forward-looking scenarios through 2035. The baseline scenario for the material based hydrogen energy storage market through 2035 assumes continued policy support for hydrogen and long-duration storage, gradual cost reductions in system integration, and expanding demonstration-to-commercial pipelines in Asia-Pacific, Europe, and North America. Under this scenario, the market is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 18.5% from 2026 to 2035, reaching a market index of 545 by 2035 (2025 = 100). Growth is expected to be front-loaded in mobility and backup power applications, where modular material based systems offer safety and space advantages, followed by acceleration in stationary long-duration storage as grid operators and utilities gain familiarity with the technology and as safety certification pathways mature. The baseline scenario anticipates that metal hydride systems will retain the largest share of installed capacity, particularly in stationary applications requiring moderate temperatures and high volumetric density, while complex hydrides and porous adsorbents gain traction in niche high-capacity and low-temperature applications. System integration costs are expected to decline by 20-30% over the forecast period as thermal management designs standardize and controls become more sophisticated, improving project economics and bankability. The supply chain for critical metals such as vanadium, lanthanum, and titanium is expected to remain a constraint, with price volatility and geopolitical factors influencing material selection toward earth-abundant alternatives. The competitive landscape is expected to consolidate, with integrated system providers and EPC firms capturing a larger share of value as procurement shifts toward system-of-systems models. Regional growth will be led by Asia-Pacific, particularly China, Japan, and South Korea, where government hydrogen strategies and industrial decarbonization targets support deployment. Europe is expected to see strong growth in stationary storage and industrial applications, supported by the EU Hydrogen Strategy and national funding programs. North America is anticipated to grow steadily, driven by federal hydrogen hubs and state-level long-duration storage mandates. Latin America and the Middle East & Africa are expected to remain smaller markets, with growth concentrated in demonstration projects and industrial applications tied to hydrogen export ambitions. Key risks to the baseline scenario include delays in safety certification, slower-than-expected cost reductions, and competition from alternative long-duration storage technologies such as compressed hydrogen and flow batteries. artigo.texto: Federal, provincial and territorial governments have launched a new working group to explore ways of improving cooperation among carbon markets across Canada, a move that could eventually have implications for Canadian agriculture. The announcement, made by Federal, provincial, and territorial governments launch working group to boost cooperation on carbon markets across Canada, states that the working group will examine different models for linking carbon markets and improving their overall functioning. Representatives from each province and territory, along with the federal government, will participate in the initiative. According to the federal government, well-functioning carbon markets can help unlock investment, support clean industrial growth, and contribute to emissions reductions. The working group held its first meeting this week and discussed a draft work plan. Recommendations are expected to be delivered to First Ministers by July 2027. The announcement comes as governments across Canada continue to explore ways of reducing emissions while supporting economic development and investment. The release notes that First Ministers agreed in July 2026 to establish the working group as part of broader efforts to strengthen cooperation across the country. Agriculture Not Specifically Mentioned While the government announcement focuses on carbon markets broadly, it does not specifically mention agriculture, carbon offsets from farms, soil carbon programs, or livestock projects. However, agricultural organizations and producers may be paying close attention as the discussions progress. Many carbon market systems around the world include projects that generate credits through activities such as carbon sequestration, emissions reductions, or improved land management practices. Whether future recommendations from the working group could affect agricultural participation in carbon markets remains unclear. The government has not indicated whether farm-based projects will be part of its review. Potential Questions for the Agriculture Sector As the working group develops its recommendations, several questions may be of interest to farmers and agricultural stakeholders: At this stage, the government has not provided answers to these questions, and they fall outside the scope of the current announcement. The working group's recommendations, expected by July 2027, could provide a clearer picture of whether new opportunities may emerge for Canadian agriculture within a more coordinated national carbon market system. artigo.texto: Years after the pandemic-era supply chain crisis has faded for much of the economy, data center developers are still battling equipment shortages and long, unpredictable lead times, a bottleneck that threatens to delay projects amid an artificial intelligence data center arms race. Equipment shortages persist as a major source of delays and uncertainty in an industry where developers are already struggling to keep pace with unprecedented demand. And delays can be costly, with hyperscalers and other tenants writing substantial penalties into contracts for missed delivery dates. The supply chain pinch is still being felt across nearly every part of the development process, from natural gas turbines and transformers to cooling systems and basic construction materials, industry insiders said at Bisnow’s Data Center Investment Conference and Expo: Central in Dallas this month. Sophisticated developers are finding ways to navigate many of these constraints, panelists said, but even then there are trade-offs. Strategies like stockpiling equipment or ordering long-lead items before designs are finalized require significant upfront capital and can raise project costs. And while some panelists expressed frustration that shortages tracing back to the pandemic nearly seven years ago have persisted for data centers long after easing in other industries, there is broad recognition that the procurement landscape isn’t returning to normal as long as the sector continues on its stratospheric growth trajectory. “There were discussions about how long Covid would impact us, and I don't know if we're ever going to go back to pre-Covid,” said Sam Caddell, CyrusOne’s senior director for facilities engineering and operations systems. “There are still impacts on lead times — from raw materials all the way down.” The most significant lead times are for equipment involved in getting power to data center project sites, panelists said. Gas turbines can take a decade or more to be delivered, a bottleneck that is currently contributing to yearslong timelines for grid connections and limiting developers’ ability to pursue on-site and behind-the-meter power as an alternative to utility interconnection queues. Transformer shortages are felt even more broadly, with panelists citing lead times of up to three years for equipment required on virtually every large-scale project. Similarly, backup generators can take more than a year to procure. The supply chain pinch extends well beyond power infrastructure. Chillers and other cooling system components routinely carry lead times of 12 to 18 months, panelists said, as do switchgear, uninterruptible power supply, or UPS, systems and other critical electrical and networking equipment integral to data center operations. Manufacturers said they simply can’t keep up with the flood of demand, even as they scramble to scale up production. “We're about to bring on a brand-new chiller factory. We'll have four chiller factories that can supply this market, and even then it's not enough,” said Dara Sanii, a director at cooling equipment provider Carrier Applied West. It’s not just complex equipment that is facing shortages. Even basic hardware and construction materials are seeing significant delays. Optical fiber can take six to eight months to arrive, and structural steel roughly a year. Meanwhile, contractors continue to encounter unexpected delays for relatively simple components like conduits and medium-voltage cables. These same hardware shortages also factor into delays in the production of more complex data center systems. Manufacturers say pumps, evaporators, fans, coils and heat exchangers used in cooling equipment are routinely sold out for a year or more, while basic components like breakers can slow the production of electrical systems. “The capacity the industry's taking down is outstripping the ability of the entire supply chain to keep up,” Johnson Controls Vice President Matt Kightlinger told DICE: Central. “It is absolutely an issue industrywide, all the way down to the component level.” Some of the pressure on the data center supply chain has been eased by delays elsewhere, panelists said. Projects derailed by grid constraints or local opposition have freed up equipment that had already been allocated, pushing scarce components back into the market. Even so, preventing procurement from becoming the pinch point on a project has required developers to rethink how they buy equipment and plan construction. Panelists said the ability to manage these constraints has become a key differentiator between firms that can actually deliver projects on schedule and those that cannot. One common strategy has been to stockpile long-lead equipment years in advance, effectively creating a strategic reserve of transformers and other critical equipment that can be deployed across multiple projects. It’s an approach that SkyBox Datacenters Executive Vice President Gordon Kellerman compared to “Covid panic-toilet-paper-buying.” But it's a strategy only open to major developers with deep balance sheets and large project pipelines, who can commit capital well before they know exactly where the equipment will ultimately be used. “We are definitely trying to buy multiple years out. That’s one of the advantages of having been around for a little longer and having a little more capital,” CyrusOne’s Cadell said. “I worked for a startup data center company, too, for a little bit, and this is a bigger challenge there.” Sophisticated developers are also sharing demand forecasts with suppliers as far as three years in advance, giving manufacturers greater visibility to plan production capacity. artigo.texto: Do ronco ao silêncio: qual a diferença entre dirigir um carro elétrico e um a combustão? César Urnhani, piloto e especialista automotivo, mostra quais são essas diferenças e dá dicas para quem está fazendo essa transição. Crédito: Estadão O crescimento do mercado de carros movidos a energia elétrica no Brasil já deixou de ser apenas uma projeção otimista e se tornou um movimento incontestável nos últimos anos. As vendas de veículos elétricos puros e híbridos atingiram 21% da participação no mercado automotivo em julho de 2026, segundo dados da ABVE (Associação Brasileira do Veículo Elétrico). Com o rápido aumento da popularidade da tecnologia, no entanto, surgem novas dúvidas, principalmente relacionadas à durabilidade das baterias de íon de lítio. Em média, os carros movidos a bateria possuem garantia entre oito e dez anos, mantendo autonomia que varia entre 70% e 90% da capacidade original após esse período - desempenho que supera até mesmo as baterias de chumbo-ácido usadas em veículos a combustão. Prova viva de como o alcance se mantém é este empresário que conta com pequena frota de BYD Dolphin Mini. Ainda assim, algum dia, essas peças ainda precisarão ser trocadas, descartadas ou recicladas. E esse processo precisa ser feito corretamente, caso contrário, as consequências podem ser prejudiciais tanto para o veículo quanto para o meio ambiente. Isso porque o descarte incorreto desses componentes em lixo comum ou aterros (ato proibido pela Política Nacional de Resíduos Sólidos) pode causar o vazamento de metais pesados e compostos químicos tóxicos, gerando a contaminação crônica de lençois freáticos e do solo, além de riscos de incêndios químicos de difícil extinção. Trocas e descarte correto das baterias dos carros elétricos Diante desse cenário, o especialista em carros elétricos da SAE Brasil (Sociedade de Engenheiros da Mobilidade), Wanderlei Marinho, aponta que uma troca segura e eficiente da bateria do carro deve ser feita, sem exceção, em concessionárias ou redes de oficinas autorizadas e homologadas pelo Ibama. “A remoção exige equipamentos de proteção específicos e isolamento elétrico de alta tensão”, explica o engenheiro. Para mitigar os efeitos dos descartes inadequados, Wanderlei propõe soluções de rastreabilidade e investimento em infraestrutura, tais como: punir o desmonte ilegal ou o descarte clandestino por meio do monitoramento eletrônico de veículos que saem de circulação; e subvencionar e expandir usinas de reciclagem locais para que o processo seja economicamente viável perto dos grandes centros urbanos. Saiba Também: - Este país abriu as portas para carros chineses e se deu mal: o alerta da Tailândia para o Brasil - Ouvir música enquanto dirige pode ser perigoso? Entenda os riscos Sobre o mesmo dilema ambiental, o professor César Menezes, de manutenção automotiva do Senai Pernambuco - órgão que desenvolve o primeiro projeto brasileiro de baterias de lítio para veículos híbridos -, sugere práticas ágeis de contenção dos resíduos. “Para mitigar esses efeitos deve-se primeiramente conter a fonte de contaminação, coletar a bateria e destiná-la a uma das empresas de reciclagem para que o procedimento seja realizado e, por fim, recuperar o ambiente contaminado através de análises ambientais e aplicação de técnicas de remediação adequadas”, defende César. Reciclagem e reuso inteligente das baterias de íons de lítio Antes do procedimento de reciclagem indicado pelos especialistas, vale lembrar que as baterias não se tornam resíduos imediatamente após a retirada dos carros, podendo ser reaproveitadas em um “segunda vida”. “Quando a bateria atinge cerca de 75% a 80% da sua capacidade e perde a autonomia ideal para o carro, ela pode ser desmontada e redirecionada para aplicações estacionárias, como armazenamento de energia solar ou eólica, para uso residencial e industrial”, explica Wanderlei. Passado o momento em que o reaproveitamento não é mais possível, o próximo e último passo é a reciclagem industrial. Atualmente, a tecnologia mais eficiente combina o desmembramento mecânico das células da bateria com processos de hidrometalurgia. Com esse método, é possível recuperar entre 93% a 99% dos componentes (como lítio, cobalto, níquel e manganês), e, por fim, reinserí-los na cadeia de produção de novos materiais. A infraestrutura para esse tipo de processo está em rápida expansão no Brasil, justamente para atender a demanda da frota cada vez maior de veículos. Como manter a saúde da bateria do carro elétrico? Os oito anos estipulados pelas montadoras ao oferecerem garantias a seus consumidores fazem sentido, sobretudo considerando a perda de capacidade das baterias pelo uso acumulado de recarga e descarga, que é inevitável. Entretanto, elas podem durar mais do que isso, chegando até 15 anos de funcionamento, desde que sejam adotados alguns cuidados especiais, de acordo com estudiosos do tema. Segundo Bruno Souza, também do setor de manutenção automotiva do Senai-PE, o motorista que visa preservar sua bateria deve “evitar exposição prolongada a temperaturas elevadas, não deixar a carga chegar frequentemente a níveis muito baixos (menos de 20%) durante longos períodos, evitar manter a bateria constantemente em 100% quando isso não for necessário e utilizar carregadores recomendados pelo fabricante”. Em consonância com essa ideia, Wanderlei Marinho indica prestar atenção ao sistema de arrefecimento. “O sistema de gerenciamento térmico do carro protege as células contra degradação por temperatura. Realizar as revisões do fluido de arrefecimento do sistema elétrico conforme o manual é indispensável”, pontua ele. artigo.texto: Solidus Techno Power Private Limited has delivered a 27.31 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) integrated with a 50 MW solar project for SBF Ispat Private Limited. The company also provided engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) services for the project. Solidus is delivering this project through its subsidiary, XenRosh ESS. In a release, Solidus, a Punjab-based EPC company, said it is expanding its battery energy storage manufacturing capabilities to meet growing market demand. The company continues to support commercial and industrial customers through its solar EPC expertise and integrated energy storage solutions. The project strengthens Solidus’s solar and energy storage portfolio, complemented by BESS manufacturing through its subsidiary, XenRosh ESS. The project marks a milestone in Solidus’s expansion into integrated solar and energy storage solutions. Alongside its EPC and renewable energy development businesses, the company is strengthening its BESS manufacturing capabilities through XenRosh ESS, which focuses on manufacturing battery energy storage systems. Solidus Solar Project in Punjab Previously, Solidus developed a solar project in Punjab in collaboration with Roshni Renewable LLP, a venture promoted by professionals from Valco, an Indian aluminium company, and Solidus Techno Power Private Limited. The venture aims to establish a giga-scale solar module manufacturing plant in Punjab. With an initial production capacity of 1.8 GW, the project represents a step towards strengthening Punjab’s industrial ecosystem and India’s renewable energy sector, the company said. The fully automated production facility is expected to adhere to global production standards, generate substantial employment opportunities, and contribute to sustainable regional growth. Leadership View On the latest announcement, Jaspal Singh, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Co-founder of Solidus Techno Power Pvt Ltd, said, “Solar power combined with battery storage offers industries greater flexibility and helps them utilise renewable energy more effectively.” Harvinder Singh, Managing Director, added, “This project strengthens Solidus’s integrated clean-energy portfolio. Through XenRosh ESS, we are expanding our BESS manufacturing capabilities with a focus on quality, safety and reliability.”

artigo.texto: Madison County lawmakers have barred data center developers from seeking certain tax incentives. Members of the county board voted Wednesday to exclude data centers from property tax incentives through Illinois’ enterprise zone program, which aims to stimulate economic growth in struggling parts of the state. Projects that get the incentives receive 10-year property tax abatements that then phase out. Granite City, Madison and Venice currently have projects in the program. “There’s no need to incentivize a data center,” said board Chairman Chris Slusser. “They’re (developers) eager to build them.” The board amended rules for the Southwestern Madison County Enterprise zone to exclude data centers. Slusser said the county hopes to pursue similar restrictions in nearby zones. The Madison County discovery zone includes Collinsville, Glen Carbon, Maryville, Troy, St. Jacob and Highland. The decision comes as several developers eye the Metro East for data center development. Currently, developers are looking at Granite City and Pontoon Beach. Just this week, the developer behind a planned data center in Midtown St. Louis announced plans to build one at the site of the former Alton Steel mill. The developer, TerraWatt, said it wouldn’t seek any tax incentives. “We would not want to do a property tax exemption for a data center,” Slusser said. “I would not support a data center project that offers a property tax incentive.” The rules do not prohibit individual municipalities from providing their own tax incentives for data center projects. Residents in Chouteau, Granite City, Nameoki and Venice townships are set to vote on advisory measures in November, asking whether data center development should be allowed in their communities.

artigo.texto: Evento em Natal reúne especialistas e setor de energia para debater estruturas de data center A estrutura necessária para abrigar centros de processamento e armazenamento de dados está em pauta na Data Center Conference, nesta sexta-feira (23), na Federação das Indústrias do Estado do Rio Grande do Norte (Fiern), em Natal. Realizado pelo Grupo FRG, o encontro reúne representantes dos setores de tecnologia, energia, infraestrutura, meio ambiente e engenharia. Tiago Fraga, CEO do Grupo FRG, realizador do evento, afirma que debater o tema no RN é estratégico, uma vez que o estado congrega aptidões que o colocam na corrida global por esse tipo de tecnologia. “Dentre essas aptidões estão a questão regulatório e o fato de o Rio Grande do Norte ser excedente em energia”, disse ele, que também é presidente do Conselho da World Carbon Association. Gladson Mortoza, gerente comercial da Mendes Holler, fabricante da tecnologia, é um dos palestrantes. Segundo ele,apostar em data center diante dos avanços regulatórios no RN requer agora uma articulação para atração desse tipo de empreendimento. “Já temos todas as condições de abrigar um polo de data center. Além das condições adequadas, por aqui existe forte apoio institucional de diversas entidades, o que é muito importante para que se crie esse polo”, explicou. Os data centers abrigam equipamentos que processam e armazenam informações utilizadas por empresas, serviços públicos e plataformas digitais. O funcionamento dessa tecnologia depende de uma estrutura que envolve fornecimento de energia, conectividade, refrigeração e segurança, conectando diferentes áreas de conhecimento e atividade econômica. Entre os palestrantes estão o vice-presidente da Associação Brasileira de Data Center (ABDC), Luis Tossi, e o es-pecialista em infraestrutura de data centers Júlio Lima. Também participam André Martins, presidente executivo do IBTD; Lucas Themata, presidente da APCA e representante do Grupo Thêmata; e Ricardo Salles, presidente do Instituto BR+. Além disso, representantes do setor energético do estado, também participam do encontro. O evento tem apoio da Fiern, WCA, ABDC, Crea-RN, Potigás, Neoenergia Cosern e Banco do Nordeste. artigo.texto: Stanislav Kondrashov Oligarch Series: The Historical Relationship Between Oligarchy and Battery Technology Stanislav Kondrashov on oligarchy and battery technology The relationship between oligarchy and battery technology can be examined through the history of industrial ownership, concentrated financial resources, and the development of electrical manufacturing. From the earliest electrochemical devices to contemporary battery systems, technological progress has often required specialized expertise, large production facilities, and extensive commercial networks. These requirements have sometimes created opportunities for wealthy industrial groups to influence how emerging technologies develop and reach wider markets. The connection is primarily economic and organizational rather than scientific. Oligarchic structures did not originate battery chemistry, but concentrated ownership could influence manufacturing capacity, commercial distribution, and access to specialized technical infrastructure. Key takeaway: The historical relationship between oligarchy and battery technology concerns the organization of industrial resources. Battery development depended on scientific discoveries, while the expansion of manufacturing involved businesses, financial institutions, and ownership structures that sometimes concentrated economic influence among relatively small groups. What Is the Connection Between Oligarchy and Battery Technology? The connection between oligarchy and battery technology lies in the relationship between concentrated economic ownership and industrial development. Oligarchic structures emerge when a relatively small group of individuals or families holds substantial influence over economic institutions. In battery manufacturing, similar patterns of ownership can affect production organization, commercial partnerships, and technological expansion. Oligarchy is a concept with a long intellectual history. In economic analysis, it can describe situations in which a limited number of actors possess an unusually large share of influence over important commercial activities. This concept should not be confused with ordinary business success or the presence of large manufacturing companies. A concentrated industry is not automatically an oligarchy. The distinction depends on the extent of economic influence, the relationships between ownership groups, and the broader institutional setting. Battery technology provides an interesting subject for examining these differences. Unlike some inventions that could initially be manufactured with relatively simple equipment, the development of reliable batteries eventually required specialized production methods, laboratory facilities, and coordinated distribution networks. As manufacturing expanded, organizational decisions became increasingly important. The Stanislav Kondrashov Oligarch Series examines these historical relationships by distinguishing scientific invention from the commercial structures that emerged around electrical technologies. How Did Early Battery Technology Develop? Early battery technology developed through experiments in electricity and electrochemistry during the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries. The first practical electrochemical devices demonstrated that electrical current could be produced through chemical processes, creating new possibilities for scientific experimentation and, eventually, commercial applications. The earliest batteries were primarily scientific instruments. Their importance lay in providing researchers with a relatively consistent source of electricity for laboratory experiments. Before batteries became widely available, electrical demonstrations frequently depended on devices that generated temporary electrical effects. Electrochemical cells introduced a different approach. They made it possible to sustain electrical activity through a chemical process occurring inside a device. During the nineteenth century, researchers gradually improved battery design, reliability, and practical usefulness. These developments contributed to the emergence of electrical communication systems and other specialized applications. At this stage, battery technology was not yet a large consumer industry. Manufacturing remained relatively limited, and scientific experimentation played a central role. Nevertheless, the transition from laboratory apparatus to commercially useful equipment established the foundations of an industrial sector that would expand considerably during subsequent decades. Why Did Industrial Ownership Become Important? Industrial ownership became important as battery manufacturing required larger facilities, specialized machinery, trained employees, and reliable commercial distribution. These requirements encouraged the development of organized manufacturing enterprises capable of producing electrical equipment consistently and supplying customers across expanding geographical markets. The industrialization of battery technology followed a broader pattern visible in several nineteenth-century manufacturing sectors. Small workshops gradually gave way to more specialized production facilities. Standardized components improved consistency. Mechanical equipment allowed manufacturers to increase output. Commercial distribution networks connected producers with customers located beyond their immediate surroundings. These changes created new organizational requirements. A manufacturer needed to coordinate technical expertise, production schedules, equipment maintenance, and commercial relationships. Ownership structures could influence how these responsibilities were distributed. Some enterprises remained relatively small. Others became part of larger industrial groups with activities extending across several electrical technologies. artigo.texto: India Needs Battery Storage, Grid Investment To Meet 500 GW Clean Energy Target: Experts Updated: Oct 26, 2026 02:56:31pm India Needs Battery Storage, Grid Investment To Meet 500 GW Clean Energy Target: Experts New Delhi, Oct 26 (KNN) India needs to expand battery storage and grid infrastructure alongside renewable energy capacity to ensure reliable power supply as it moves towards its target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, experts said at an industry event. India has crossed 300 GW of installed non-fossil fuel capacity, but integrating more renewable power into the grid will require investments in energy storage, domestic manufacturing and research, said Jai Asundi, executive director, Centre for Study of Science, Technology and Policy (CSTEP). The discussions took place at the Renewable Energy India Expo, held alongside The Battery Show India and the Energy Storage Summit India in Greater Noida, reported The Times Of India. Generation And Storage Must Scale Together Yogesh Mudras, managing director, Informa Markets in India, said renewable energy generation and grid storage must expand in tandem as the country’s clean energy market grows. “We have reached an execution phase where generation and grid storage must scale in tandem,” he said. India’s renewable energy market is projected to reach 486 GW by 2030, while its battery storage sector is expected to exceed USD 8.5 billion by 2031, Mudras said. The expansion of storage capacity will be critical to managing fluctuations in renewable power generation and supporting grid reliability as the share of solar and wind energy increases. India, Germany And Australia Explore Cooperation Anandi Iyer, director, Fraunhofer Office in India, said the world added around 800 GW of renewable energy capacity in 2025, while global battery storage deployment reached 108 GW, up 40 per cent from the previous year. She said India and Germany could strengthen cooperation in battery research, power electronics and advanced engineering to support clean energy technology development. Australia’s High Commissioner to India, Philip Green, highlighted opportunities for collaboration by combining Australia’s critical mineral resources and solar technology with India’s manufacturing capabilities. Australia produces more than half of the world’s lithium, he said, adding that cooperation could help strengthen clean energy supply chains. Scotland First Minister John Swinney said Scottish expertise and innovation could complement India’s manufacturing scale and market potential to advance the clean energy transition. Falling Costs Improve Renewable Energy Competitiveness Manu Srivastav, additional chief secretary in Madhya Pradesh’s power and renewable energy department, said falling technology costs and economies of scale were making renewable energy increasingly competitive with conventional power. Experts at the event highlighted the need to complement capacity additions with investments in storage, grid infrastructure and domestic manufacturing to support the next phase of India’s energy transition. (KNN Bureau)

artigo.texto: 800 VDC for AI Data Centers: Rethinking Power Delivery in the White Space Key Highlights - High-density AI racks moving toward megawatt scale require 800 VDC power distribution. - Sidecar architecture enables immediate deployment without requiring costly upstream infrastructure overhauls. - Centralized architectures improve white-space efficiency but demand tighter electrical protection coordination. - Converter-fed direct current faults require specialized protection strategies and modern transient simulation tools. - Reverse current blocking devices reduce peak fault currents by over 80 percent. The AI-driven evolution of data centers is pushing power requirements past the physical limits of traditional electrical engineering. With high-density clusters forcing rack power demands from 400 kW toward a megawatt and beyond, standard power distribution models break down. Attempting to deliver that much power over conventional options puts operators into a corner with regards to physical space, and they are being forced to rethink how energy is delivered within the white space. This physical bottleneck is why the industry is moving toward 800 VDC power distribution. Stepping up the voltage drastically lowers the required current, enabling data centers to deliver megawatt-scale power through much smaller conductors. The result is less copper mass, higher end-to-end efficiency, and more physical room for servers. At the same time, operators must account for how shifting to higher-voltage direct current alters the way that electricity behaves during a fault. Adopting 800 VDC requires rethinking system topology, arc flash risk, and protection strategies to keep facilities online and workers safe. Sidecar vs Centralized 800 VDC Architectures Embracing 800 VDC is not an all-or-nothing proposition where the entire data center must switch to a single architecture. Rather, there is a spectrum of design choices depending on physical constraints, operational risk tolerance, and deployment schedules. For immediate deployments, rack-level sidecar architecture is the best option. In this layout, incoming AC power connects directly to a dedicated power rack positioned alongside the IT rack. The sidecar handles local power conversion and feeds 800 VDC straight to the adjacent compute hardware over short interlink connections. This sidecar approach offers several immediate operational advantages. It leaves the upstream facility intact, allowing operators to keep their existing AC UPS systems, switchgear, and utility feeds without a costly overhaul. It also taps into a mature supply chain built around electric vehicle fast-charging infrastructure, isolates high-voltage DC paths to a small physical footprint right at the rack, and restricts the failure zone to a single rack instead of risking downtime at the pod, data hall, or facility level. In contrast, centralized architectures utilizing medium voltage rectifiers or solid state transformers represent a long-term play. Power conversion moves upstream into the main electrical room or pod level, distributing 800 VDC across overhead busway networks directly to rows of server racks. While centralizing power conversion frees up valuable white-space floor area by eliminating AC switchgear, transformers and PDUs and improves aggregate efficiency, it demands a higher level of operational maturity. Centralized designs involve longer distribution runs, far more stored energy on the central bus, and significantly tighter coordination across every tier of electrical protection. Is 800 VDC Safe for Data Centers? Safety is the first question engineering teams ask when introducing 800 VDC to the white space. In standard AC power systems, alternating current naturally drops to zero voltage twice every cycle. This starves arcing faults of energy, helping circuit breakers extinguish arcs relatively quickly. That is not the case with direct current, which delivers a constant voltage without a zero crossing to assist fault interruption. As a result, DC systems require specialized protective devices, such as semiconductor fuses for rapid let-through energy reduction or DC circuit breakers engineered with enhanced arc chutes, wider contact spacing, and magnetic blowouts to lengthen and cool longer-lasting DC arcs. Unlike transformer-fed AC short circuits that supply a steady fault current, a converter-fed 800 VDC fault unfolds in two distinct phases. During the initial capacitive spike within the first few milliseconds of a fault, energy stored in equipment capacitors discharges almost instantly, creating a brief, high-magnitude current spike. Once localized capacitors dump their charge, intelligent power converters step in. Modern solid-state converters actively cap fault current, typically holding it to roughly 150% of normal operating levels, or shut down entirely within milliseconds. Arcing hazards are often significantly lower than traditional assumptions suggest because smart power electronics choke off the energy supply. How Arc Flash Risk Is Evaluated in 800 VDC Systems To protect site personnel, facility managers run arc flash assessments to set safety boundaries and select Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). The challenge is that legacy AC calculation rules do not accurately reflect how converter-fed DC systems behave. Standard, simplified formulas (such as NFPA 70E Annex D) assume a steady, continuous fault current, treating short capacitive spikes as if they persist indefinitely when applied to an 800 VDC system. As a result, these formulas tend to overestimate incident energy, particularly when applied to systems with transient, converter-limited fault conditions. By using computer simulation tools like ETAP or MATLAB, engineers can model actual fault dynamics. The real-world numbers paint a very different picture.
